As we have seen in almost every single chapter of Acts, this is the faith which we contend, the Gospel of Christ, resurrected. Amen.

And believing, Cornelius and his household full of family and friends come to salvation. And those once-Jews who had believed on Christ that accompanied Peter on this journey were astonished to see that this room full of Gentiles all received the gift of the Holy Ghost that had come down on the disciples on Pentecost, and had even filled Saul after his accepting the gospel from Ananias, now was given unto them.

And in joy of this event, Peter says "*Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?*"

And so they were baptized in the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: Salvation is not sanctification
teachings.summary: Jesus' call in John 14 to keep His commandments was to the already saved, and confusing it with the gospel mixes up salvation with sanctification.
teachings.text:
In before some works-spurg says "see, you have to obey commandments to be saved!"

They cite this moving speech to His saved apostles and disciples, conflating Jesus final encouragement to them with the Gospel of salvation by faith that's been preached by Christ to the masses for 13 chapters, unable to understand the difference between salvation and sanctification, the faith that saves and the love that shines from the saved. False doctrine in search of whatever hook they can find to hang it on.

The worst part is those who do this don't even keep the commandments, never go soul winning, never share the Gospel with strangers. They are constantly involved with their own piety and self-absorbed, vain and dead 'works' that benefit only themselves in their theology of self-righteousness. Fruit inspectors, hypocrites and fools.

teachings.title: Grace is not transactional
teachings.summary: Doing works and sacraments to earn or keep salvation is a selfish transaction, not love, since grace is an unearned gift and our only righteousness is Christ's.
teachings.text:
Doing works and sacraments, trying not to sin, etc for righteousness or to keep the salvation given by Christ is not love. It's not charity if it's for your benefit. It is a transaction.

Love is not transactional. Grace is not contingent on conditions, because it is unearned. Undeserved. Unconditional love.

The Bible says that God pays us for our labors, if they are works that don't burn up like wood hay and stubble. If they have eternal value. But His grace is given freely as a gift.

It is selfish, because it's done for an ulterior motive rather than simply love, of the Father or of the Son, or of others. Fear of damnation should lead you to understanding that our only righteousness is in Christ, imputed by His blood. Not keep you in line and doing works to earn your way into heaven.

teachings.title: No communion in John's gospel
teachings.summary: John, written so the unsaved may be saved, records no breaking of bread or wine at the last supper, so no such ceremony is needed for salvation.
teachings.text:
Another note on this chapter, John's account of the last supper. As we have said throughout the Gospel according to John, this is written specifically to the unsaved so that they may understand and come to salvation by faith. So it is important to recognize that there is no account of the breaking of bread and blessing of wine, which were symbols used to explain Jesus' coming trials and death in the other Gospel accounts.

If a ceremony of eating bread and drinking wine were necessary for salvation, it would be mentioned here. Of course if it were mentioned, it would contradict the entire message of God's grace giving us eternal life through belief on His Son found in every chapter.

teachings.title: The words I speak are spirit and life
teachings.summary: Eating His flesh and drinking His blood is an allegory for believing on Christ, as Jesus Himself explains that the flesh profits nothing.
teachings.text:
Jesus restates the entire gospel that he had given just moments before, essentially substituting believe with eating his flesh and drinking his blood. And although the analogy is clear to those who want to understand, and to those who believe, it confounds the unsaved and the natural man.

We must eat the spiritual bread and the spiritual wine, the belief in Christ and God's promise to us to be saved. And he will live in us and we and Him if we do. Forever. Eternally. The Spirit inside us. We as the body of Christ.

These dark sayings troubled even His disciples, and as often as the case, Jesus takes the time to explain what He's saying to them so that they have better understanding.

Jesus says that it's the spirit that is quickened, and that the flash profits nothing, that this is spiritually meat and drink, not literal. That "*the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life."*

He's literally telling them that it's an allegory for a spiritual salvation, and yet some couldn't believe despite being called His disciples. Despite having some semblance of faith, but not unto belief and thus missing the point and the mark, and not getting saved.

teachings.title: Ye must be born again
teachings.summary: In John 3 Jesus tells Nicodemus a man must be born again of the Spirit, and whosoever believes God gave His Son for the world has everlasting life, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
John 3 is possibly the most important chapter of the Bible as it's Jesus Christ giving the Gospel to an unsaved Pharisee named Nicodemus, who just can't see the truth or Kingdom of God. He comes by night, sneakily. He comes with flattery. Jesus knows his heart and understanding this uses the opportunity to not only preach the word, the Gospel, but to upbraid all the Pharisees, through Nicodemus.

Jesus begins with the need to be born again to *see* the kingdom of God. This is both literally true and, as Nicodemus shows with his answers, spiritually true here on earth. He can't *see* what Jesus is presenting.

Jesus presents the concept of being born again twice more, that we are born of water, in the flesh from our mother's womb, but must be born again of the Spirit to enter the kingdom of God.

Nicodemus' glib answer, taking it literally to crawl back into your mother, is so typical of the type of spergy sarcasm we see so often when explaining salvation to the proud who are vain in their own conceit.

Jesus goes on to compare telling who's been born again as determining where the wind you hear is coming from or going. Nicodemus hearing all this is unable to understand, but he *should*, being a Rabbi, a Pharisee, a religious leader of the Israelites. When Jesus says "*Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things"* He's saying it's the same doctrine of the prophets, that men in Nicodemus' position should know it. RIP dispensationalism.

In v11 and 12, the use of 'ye' is plural. The English of the KJV is incredibly precise. Thee is singular you, ye plural. Jesus is speaking of all the Pharisees. That they believe not the witness that God has given since the beginning. They can't understand earthly things, the basics of Biblical salvation, and so when Nicodemus is asking for more esoteric and 'hidden knowledge,' which is why he'd come, Jesus is giving him the basics, knowing he can't even grasp it and having confirmed this, moves on to meatier doctrine to show it; That the son of man is come down from Heaven and *is in Heaven*, at the same time. That the brazen serpent lifted up by Moses as a picture of Himself, the Christ. These are the heavenly things.

And this established, Jesus gives the most well known presentation of the Gospel with the best known verse of scripture, that ties up the entire good news of God's word in one sentence:

*For God so loved the world, that he gave His only begotten Son, that whosever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

If you believe this sentence, that God in His love for the entire world gave His Son as a sacrifice, and anyone who believes this one truth will not perish but have everlasting, eternal life, you are saved. That's it. That's the Gospel.

Salvation is in belief, trusting God loves us, that Jesus is His son, that His sacrifice was for the whole world, that any who believe this has life that will not end.

If you doubt any one of those concepts, you aren't saved. If you doubt Jesus died for the entire world (if they believe), or that whosoever doesn't mean whosoever, you're not saved.

If you're adding to this with works or requirements by man, you don't believe the record given and are just like Nicodemus and the Pharisees. And just like Nicodemus, unable to understand Heavenly things.

And just to make sure there's no misunderstanding, Jesus begins hammering the same point over and over:

His coming is to save the world. That those who believe that are saved, but those who don't are already condemned by their lack of faith.

Jesus' being there to fulfill the law, doesn't condemn man. Their being wicked and preferring the darkness and shunning the light that is Christ does. *For there are none righteous*, and so we are condemned without the light and in need of salvation.

*But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.*

teachings.title: Christ the end of the law for righteousness
teachings.summary: Zeal for God without knowledge of the gospel does not save, because Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone that believes and confesses Him.
teachings.text:
Verse 1, Paul prays that his fellow Israelites of the flesh be saved, by what? Faith.

Verse 2, because of their zeal for the Lord which he testifies is real. Many unsaved Israelites loved and wanted to serve God, zealously.

*But not according to knowledge*. Knowledge of what? The Gospel of Christ which is faith.

I feel this same way for all those who I know, in real life and online, that I work with and am friends with, who zealously serve God the way they know, but *not according to knowledge,* doing so with vain works of the law, and so, *are not saved.*

Why? Because Christ is the end of the law of righteousness, to EVERYONE who believes on Him. Once you obey the Gospel, that is believe on Jesus Christ and His perfect work on the cross, death, burial and resurrection, you do not have to rely on works of the law to try and obtain righteousness.

Paul says stop wondering who is going to heaven or hell based on their adherence to the law, because doing so denies that we are made righteous *in* Christ, by faith, and so denies His work that we are counting on.

And what is the word of faith that we preach? It's right there in your heart if you're saved, and the Spirit puts it on your tongue to be shared;

*That if thou confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus and shalt believe in thine heart that God raised him from the dead, THOU SHALL BE SAVED.*

Period. This is the Gospel. To obey the Gospel is to believe this one truth. There's nothing else regarding righteousness and eternal life to know.

There is no secret trick, no hidden gnostic secret. There is no catch. No strings. No being worthy, because no one is worthy of the righteousness of Christ. Just believe. And whosoever believes is saved. Not a chosen people. Not a limited few, picked to believe. Not those who do works, indulge in sacraments, keep Sabbaths, go to church...but those who believe the report given, by whom all prophets testified, given by Jesus Christ in the flesh, and shared by His disciples straight through unto this day.

teachings.title: Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: There is no difference between Jew and Greek and no chosen people; every saint from Adam on was saved by believing and calling on the Lord, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
For scripture says "*Whosoever* believeth on Him shall not be ashamed."

And because there is no difference between "Jew and Greek," there is no "chosen people." Dispensationalism rests entirely on the idea that there is, and so they deny the word of God.

*For whosoever call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

Adam believed. Able believed. Seth called upon His name. Enoch believed. Noah believed. Abraham believed and it was counted upon him for righteousness. Sara, Issac, Joseph, Moses, Joshua..all OT saints, they all are said to have believed and called upon the name of the Lord.

That's it. There is no "and..."

There is no church you must join, sacrament you must have, no works of the law, no special boy status, no hypocritical "fruit inspection."

 No other act, regardless of zeal and sincere hope in those acts, can save anyone.

teachings.title: Works without faith are hay and stubble
teachings.summary: Works of the law, ordinances and holy days cannot save; only faith in Christ saves, even him that worketh not, and many who trusted their works will hear I never knew you.
teachings.text:
How many of you are zealously trying to gain righteousness and get to heaven by the works of the law? By following carnal ordinances, sacrifices and holy days?

The Bible says those works are hay and stubble. They burn up, and only the work God has made us to do, in serving Him is giving the report of the good news by which we have hope unto eternal life to others that they may be saved.

Works without faith in Christ as the sole means of salvation are dead and cannot save anyone. Faith, even to him that worketh not, saves.

God doesn't hear the prayers of those who don't depend on faith alone for righteousness, or care about their works:

**Matthew 7**
*21 Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.*

*22 Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?*

*23 And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

Please do not be like the Jews Paul is writing about. Do not be among those counting on their works before Christ.

If you believe that God so loved you that he sent His only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, to live, die and be raised again so that all who believe on Him have eternal life, that can never be taken away or lost, never earned or deserved, given in grace, then confess with thy mouth, call upon the name of the Lord and be saved.

teachings.title: Dead to sin, yet saved as we are
teachings.summary: Grace is not liberty to sin and the Spirit sanctifies believers over time, but we are saved just as we are while yet sinners, so a wrong idea of repentance should not keep anyone from grace.
teachings.text:
As we see when we read Romans 5 and 6, in our recent study, there were people claiming that what was being taught was Liberty in sin, that because we are forgiven by the grace of God that we can continue in sin. But what does Paul say? God forbid.

We are dead to sin as saved believers. All things are lawful to me but not all things edify. The spirit does work in us the more we grow closer to God, to help remove the thorns in our hearts as we become more sanctified, praise God! But we are saved just as we are, though we still are sinners. *But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.*

Don't let the misunderstanding about repentance be the stumbling block that keeps you from His grace.

teachings.title: He is risen: confess and believe
teachings.summary: Because Christ rose from the dead, whoever believes in his heart and confesses Jesus with his mouth is saved, a free gift that can never be lost.
teachings.text:
After the third day, Jesus arose, the stone rolled away, the keys to Hell and Death, His.

**Revelation 1**:18 *I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.*
...
**1 Peter 1:3** *Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead*
*...*
**Romans 10**
*8 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;*

*9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.*

*10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.*

His life, death, burial, resurrection and ascension has purchased for all who believe on Jesus' name, the free gift of eternal life, given by God in grace, as we are yet sinners, to be washed clean in His blood. God's word made perfect.

If you haven't put your trust in this good news, and accepted that free gift, make today the day you do.

If you believe in your heart that God loved you so much, He sent His only begotten son to die for your sin and be raised again, then confess this with your mouth in prayer, calling upon Jesus' name, and be saved. Knowing that blessed assurance of eternal security, never to be lost or taken away.

teachings.title: Blessed is the man whose sin is covered
teachings.summary: As David and Paul teach, God imputes righteousness without works and does not hold the believer's sins against him, and this good news must be received today before God's Spirit ceases to strive.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 32** opens with a very familiar and important doctrine, the understanding of God's forgiveness for sin in the saved believer's life. This foundational fact is repeated by Paul in the letter to the Romans;

**Romans 4:6–8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

The truth is that, in Christ, whether it was in David's day, or Paul's or our own, God forgives our past transgressions, covers our current sin, and will not hold our future sins and iniquity against us.

This positional standing of righteousness before God, despite our sins, through His imputed righteousness is made possible, through the Holy Spirit, by the renewal, the regeneration, the quickening of our spirit. The new man within us. Blessed is the man *in whose spirit there is no guile.*

We are given the Spirit of truth, that we may acknowledge our sin, knowing that we are forgiven of all sin, first, not by works but by faith.

The same good news today as in David's day. And this Psalm serves as an evangelical appeal.

David writes of a man who kept his silence, who hadn't called upon the name of the Lord, who suffered in their sins, bones waxing old and dried up by their roaring in the daytime, the heaviness of their iniquity weighing on them at night.

But the honesty and humility of acknowledging sin, not hiding anything from God (as if we could), confessing our transgressions unto the Lord, and being forgiven, is a blessing. Rioting in the daytime and being kept up at night by our conscience, being convicted in the Spirit, gives way to the peace that passes understanding, through the forgiveness that is given to us by God's mercy and grace.

David reminds us that there is a time where God may be sought, before it is too late.

**Isaiah 55:6**
*Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near*

God's Spirit will not always strive with man. There comes a time when those that put off or reject the truth, not acknowledging that they are sinners, lying to God and themselves, are no longer able to come to Him. Where He no longer extends His hand, because they have hardened their hearts and will not seek Him, even as they face destruction.

**Hebrews 4:7**
*Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.*

We have the example of those in the days of Noah, who mocked him for his faith in preparing the ark, and whose disobedient spirits who Christ preached to in Hell, were destroyed by the flood, never coming nigh unto God. Just as those left to God's wrath to come will not repent, despite the horrors of His judgment.

There is a time, it is today. There is a day, and it is the present. If you haven't accepted the truth that we are sinners in need of salvation, and that it is offered as a free gift to all who believe, through the grace of Almighty God, now is the time.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

teachings.title: Transgression, sin and iniquity forgiven
teachings.summary: Transgression is wilful rebellion, sin is missing the mark and iniquity is our twisted nature, and on the cross Christ bore all three, imputing His righteousness to believers so they are found not guilty, past, present and future.
teachings.text:
While it isn't entirely wrong to take the words transgression, sin and iniquity, and use them interchangeably, they do carry subtle differences in their meaning.

Transgression is the wilful rebellion against the truth of God and His commands. The transgression of Adam, for example, having one law to obey, and choosing of their own volition (even as Eve was deceived, Adam most assuredly knew better), deciding to be disobedient.

Sin, which the Bible says is the transgression of the Law, also carries with it the idea of missing the mark, falling short.

**Romans 3:23**
*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God*

We aren't able, in the flesh, to hit the mark, the target being the perfect holiness of God. Only Jesus Christ did.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

Iniquity comes from the Hebrew word, *Avon*, meaning to twist, bend, or distort. The perverted and crooked nature of fallen man. The bent toward evil, the guilt that stays with us, and the perverted character that drives the outward actions. It is the *guile* or deceit mentioned in verse 2.

Our natural tendencies towards willful rebellion, to sin, and to lie to ourselves and others, including God, about the evil that we do. Excusing ourselves with lies.

Taken together, the blessed assurance that our transgressions, sins and iniquities are eternally forgiven demonstrates the mercy and grace of our Lord towards His children, through the suffering of Jesus.

**Isaiah 53:5–6**
*But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.*

He suffered these things for our iniquity and transgressions, that we may be purged. That His righteousness be imputed on our ledger, even as His blood blots away our sins.

Our transgressions are forgiven, our sin is covered, our iniquity will not be added to our account, because we are justified in Christ.

This accounting is a spiritual gift, applied to the ledger that in judgment, we are found not guilty by God.

(Some call this Penal Substitutionary Atonement, the idea that Jesus paid the price of the debt we owe, so that we do not have to receive the wages of sin. Many reject this idea. Whatever you want to call it, it is undeniable that Christ suffered that those who trust on Him, won't)

On the cross, Jesus carried away our rebellion, covered our failures with His blood, and cleared the ledger of our crooked nature by imputing His own perfect righteousness to us. Past, present and future. That we may be made the righteousness of God.

teachings.title: Righteousness from the God of our salvation
teachings.summary: Believers are made clean by God's imputed righteousness received by faith, not by their own works, and Roman Catholicism's denial of imputation at the Council of Trent is a lie.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 24** is a meditation on the truth of the Christ, the Lord, King of Hosts. Creator of all things, and the truth of the way of righteousness for those that trust in Him.

The gospel message of the Psalms, sung in the Temple, performed by the chief musicians and the congregation is the inspired doctrines of God, and the focus is entirely Jesus.

They may have looked through a glass darkly, but the concepts of Christ are hammered home, in verse after verse, chorus and stanzas of praise for the name of God, the Holy One, the Lord.

Here in the 24th Psalm, David asks *Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place?*

Those with clean hands and pure hearts, who hasn't put their trust in vanity or lying lips, but who trusted the God of their salvation.

*He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.*

We are made clean of our sins, our hearts purified by the imputed righteousness of God. We receive these blessings by grace through faith, and access to the Kingdom, not by our own righteousness but by submitting to the righteousness that is God's.

**Romans 4:5–8**
*But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

There are false religions that deny the imputation of righteousness by faith in Christ. They say that imputation is not taught in scripture. This is a lie.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

Our righteousness is as a filthy rag, our works could never justify us before a holy and perfect God. But these men believing vanity, and swearing deceitfully, teach that man needs to establish their own righteousness through works of the law, and many are misled by this lie.

**Romans 10:2–4**
*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

Roman Catholicsm rejects the idea that we are made righteous by receiving righteousness from the God of our salvation. The Council of Trent (Canon 11 on Justification) anathematized the idea that people are justified “by the sole imputation of the justice of Christ, or by the sole remission of sins” and that righteousness is "infused" by works, sacraments and "grace transforming a person," so that their own righteousness is established, rather than submitting to the righteousness of God.

But let God be true, and every man a liar. The generation of them that seek His face shall not be ashamed. All who come to the saving knowledge of Christ are made pure, in Him. Righteous, in Him.

**Titus 3:5–7**
*Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

The truth of imputed righteousness of God being given the believer is found throughout scripture. And thank God for His grace and mercy. That our sins are washed clean, justified by the blood, and remembered no more.

teachings.title: Thou art all fair, my love
teachings.summary: The bride seen without blemish pictures believers made righteous and unblameable in Christ, and the sealed garden pictures eternal security.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 opens with an ode to the beloved bride by her lover, the bridegroom. When he looks upon her he sees her fair beauty, her eyes as doves', her hair as the flocks of wild mountain goats. Picturing her black, flowing locks as the long, black, silky hair the goats have. When a herd of these dark goats grazes and moves down a steep mountain from a distance, the flowing movement creates a visual illusion of cascading hair.

He compares her teeth to the whitest of sheep, shorn and clean and notes there are none missing, a rarity to be sure in the ancient world.

Her lips, red as scarlet thread and her speech comely. Her temples and neck and breasts and scent, perfect and without blemish.

*Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.*

The poetic nature of the song, romanticizing the couples love, could be seen as hyperbole. The aura of beauty that comes with infatuation. The perfection we see when we are caught up in our love for the other.

But, as a spiritual allegory, we see the woman, who works the field and vineyard, black skinned, is without blemish when the King looks upon her. Just as we who are saved and sanctified by faith in Christ are pure when the Lord looks upon us. Clothed in righteousness. No sin imputed upon our new man.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

He has made us without blemish;

**Colossians 1:21–22**
*And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

Solomon's King sings passionately about his beloved; *How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse!* A sister of Israel, his spouse through their betrothal and marriage.

This is also how Jesus sees us, His beloved. We are His brothers and sisters, and spouse as a collective. Made one within the body of Christ.

**Matthew 12:50**
*For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother*.

His idealized view of us, despite our sin and despite our falling short of the glory of God, comes entirely by His love for us. That while we were sinners, Christ died for us. That He justifies the ungodly. That the Spirit quickens and seals us unto redemption.

So when Solomon compares his love to an inclosed garden, walled off, a spring shut up, barred from use by others. A fountain sealed, carrying the seal of the King, and so kept pure from pollution. In this allegory we see the promise of eternal security in Christ. We are eternally His.

The fruits of the garden are orchards, even pomegranates, and pleasant fruits, and flowers and spices used in ointments and perfume. Spikenard, the precious Himalayan plant, used to anoint Christ;

**Mark 14:3**
*And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.*

The odors of her garden are pleasing. Precious to the King.  Just as our fruit, our good works in Christ, are pleasing to Him.

*A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon*. He views us and the works we do for Him the same way, and we issue forth the living waters of the Spirit when we walk in His ways.

The chapter ends shifting to the beloved woman, the bride, calling upon her lord to enter her garden, *that the spices thereof may flow out.* Spiritually, calling upon the name of the Lord, that one may be saved, that God may eat His pleasant fruits.

teachings.title: Faith in the promise, not knowing the means
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous for believing God's promise without knowing the means, so OT and NT saints are saved by the same faith.
teachings.text:
Unlearned and unstable people confuse the means by which God delivered us, Jesus' life, death, burial and resurrection, with the means of receiving the promise of God, belief.

Abraham believed God's promise to him, by faith, without knowing the exact means by which He would make good on the promise, **only that He would**. And it was counted for righteousness.

We have the mystery of the means revealed to us, by the post-resurrection teachings of Christ to the Apostles, and that faith handed down, believer to believer in an unbroken line by which we can say that Abraham and the OT saints are our brothers in Christ, through they did not fully understand the mystery that was Christ.

This is what the Bible teaches.

teachings.title: Two tales of our lives
teachings.summary: Like Chronicles passing over David's sin, the believer's sinful flesh was crucified and his quickened new man cannot sin, so God will not impute sin and remembers it no more.
teachings.text:
Here is a condensed version of the events found in **2 Samuel 11 and 12**, and the telling of David's wars, the slaughter of the Ammonites and the slaying of giants.

We know, having read the earlier telling, that David had sinned with Bathsheba during this time, and murdered Uriah her husband by sending him out to war. That David tarrying in the city when it was the season of kings going to war, led to his temptation. But Chronicles doesn't much cover the failings of sin, but the glory of victory with God.

In a like manner, we see how as a Christian, we have two tales of our lives. The one, details our sin and the other remembers it no more. Because we crucified our sinful flesh to the cross when we believed, and our new man, the quickened spirit within us, is incapable of sin. When we are redeemed on the day of the Lord, God remembers our sin no more. Blessed is the man to whom God will not impute sin. Amen

teachings.title: God remembers our sin no more
teachings.summary: As Chronicles passes over David's sins, God does not impute the believer's sin and remembers it no more, so we should be as gracious to our brethren.
teachings.text:
And again, a retelling of events, this from [2 Samuel 5](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/14192). We can see that while Chronicles is often word for word, it also can be more concise, and far less judgemental against David, and Solomon. Stating things like David taking more wives as just a fact, and the generations added to.

But we see more directly the relationship David has with God. In the Christian life, we are not just our sin and failings. In some ways, we only are the things we do for God and reflections of His glory. Because the sin of our flesh and the trespasses we may do are not imputed against us. God remembers them no more. The flesh is nailed to the cross.

If God sees our sin as far from us as far as east is from west, we should strive to be as gracious and merciful to our brethren. Forgiving and avoiding the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

teachings.title: Not for thy righteousness
teachings.summary: As God gave Israel the land not for their righteousness, we receive the kingdom only by Christ's imputed righteousness, so we must not boast against others (Romans 11).
teachings.text:
Like the Israelites in the wilderness, on the eve of entering the promised land, we too commemorate the eve of our salvation and deliverance in the birth of Christ.

Jesus came to offer peace towards men from God the Father, goodwill and reconciliation, while we were yet sinners.

And just as we received the gift of eternal life by grace, the Lord reminds the children of Abraham, Issac and Jacob that it was not of their own righteousness that He delivered them, a stubborn and stiff-necked people, but by His mercy and strong hand. Undeserving and yet His love towards us brings our salvation.

And a reminder that His wrath upon the ungodly is just, not because of our own righteousness, but their own unrighteousness. We are not given the kingdom over those who refused to believe because we are better than they are, but because we submitted ourselves to receive the imputed righteousness of Christ. There but for God's grace go I.

**Deuteronomy 9** contains a similar message to the Hebrews as **Romans 11:18-27** does towards Christians;
*Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be graffed into their own olive tree?*
*For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Remember we were servants in Egypt, taken out from bondage by His mighty hand.

teachings.title: Abraham believed God and it was counted for righteousness
teachings.summary: Abraham was saved by believing God before circumcision or law, and his offering of Isaac justified him only before men, so all the glory is God's.
teachings.text:
*Abraham believed God and it was counted unto him for righteousness*.

Not by the law. Not by circumcision, for Abraham was saved decades before God gave circumcision as an ordinance. But by believing God.

Abraham didn't repent of his sins, follow the law, or grovel for mercy. God in His amazing grace, offered salvation unto him, and out of free will, Abraham accepted.

His faith was such that Abraham willingly offered his only begotten son upon the altar, knowing God would keep His word, and by this act, his faith was made perfect. That one may look upon that and see Abraham justified by men.

But not before God. It was faith alone that saved him. If it were his willingness to obey God, then Abraham would have the glory.

But all the glory is God's. He did it all. We just have to trust Him as Abraham did. That while we are yet sinners, Christ died for us.

teachings.title: The atonement in Romans 5
teachings.summary: Romans 5 refutes those who deny vicarious atonement, showing Christ's blood reconciles sinners and His righteousness is imputed as a free gift.
teachings.text:
It becomes impossible for those who maintain that "vicarious atonement isn't found in scripture," that Jesus wasn't the sacrifice for our sins, once we have reached Romans 5. The propitiation that is Christ is the atonement we have. The reconciliation is in His blood. Our hope is in His life from death.

When we were righteous? No, as sinners. Did we earn it through works, the keeping of the law? No, that would be debt, it is the imputed righteousness from Christ that justifies us in faith. It is the law of grace. We don't deserve it.

It is the free gift given by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ. The gift of His righteousness that we may be justified through Him to God. By His obedience to the end, and the death on the cross for all men, that in His resurrection we may enter into grace by faith.

*That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.*

teachings.title: The man to whom the Lord imputeth not sin
teachings.summary: Repentance from dead works to faith in God saves by faith alone, and God promises not to impute sin to the believer but to remember it no more.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:1**
*Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God*

Repentance from dead works and to faith towards God. Turning from means turning towards. From trusting in our works of righteousness to faith in God. This is the foundation that is built on the rock that is Christ.

And so, reckoned of faith, the man who does no works but believes, is saved by that faith alone. Paul quotes Davin from **Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, Whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, And in whose spirit there is no guile*.

The Lord will not impute sin, our ledger is clean, our transgressions forgiven.

For what is sin?

**1 John 3:4**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.*

But we who believe not only are forgiven of sins past, but God will not impute sin to us. Our transgression is forgiven. This is a promise of God.

**Hebrews 10:17**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

teachings.title: Abraham believed God
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by believing, since works would make salvation a debt owed rather than grace.
teachings.text:
What shall we say then? Paul, having concluded that all are under sin, all being unrighteous, and the grace of God given to all who believe on the Son, and that no man may be justified by the works of the law but only faith, now begins the application of this knowledge. The implications of this law of faith, given us by God. And he uses scripture and the promises to Abraham to explain the Old Testament in light of the New.

Abraham, the physical father of the Hebrews, including the remnant of Jews from the Children of Israel in Rome, what was Abraham's experience? A story every Jew would be familiar with.

Paul starts by saying, if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory. Abraham could brag in his works, his decades of service to God that includes willingness to sacrifice his only begotten son, but we know that there are none righteous. That boasting is excluded when we are judged by grace, as all the glory belongs to God, and the righteousness of Christ.

So Paul writes, if it were by works, Abraham could glory, boast, brag that it was due him being so righteous. But not before God, being in the flesh, a sinner. (Which we have already stipulated in chapter 3)

What then?

Well, scripture says in **Genesis 15:6**; *And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness*. Paul quotes this and argues that if it were of works, that means God would be indebted to us. To pay us for our works. That we were owed.

And so the reward would be not reckoned, or accounted for, by grace. Because grace is an unmerited and unearned gift or favor. Debt is deserved. Grace is undeserved.

*But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.*

*Abraham believed God and it was counted unto him for righteousness*.

teachings.title: Justified by faith, free to serve righteousness
teachings.summary: Romans teaches justification by faith as with Abraham, and believers freed from the law become willing servants of righteousness rather than continuing in sin.
teachings.text:
In the epistle to the Romans, is given us as scripture by God to spell out the theology of God; salvation by faith alone, to all who believe, not of works, not of the bondage of the law, but by Christ as the propitiation for our sin, and to the willing sanctification of us who are born a again, with the new man inside. Free of the law in the liberty of Christ, but not taking advantage of that liberty, leaving the bonds of the law to become willing servants of righteousness:

*For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.*
..
For Abraham *being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform. And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification*
..
*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*
..
*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.*
*For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.*
..
*But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many. And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification*.
..
*For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.*

*Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.*

*What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?*

*God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?*

*Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.*

*For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.*

*For he that is dead is freed from sin.*

*Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him. For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.*

*Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof. Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.*

teachings.title: He believed, and it was counted for righteousness
teachings.summary: Abram's faith in the promised seed was imputed to him for righteousness, and the sacrifices of Genesis 15 pictured Christ's blood offering.
teachings.text:
That's a lot of Bible this morning, and I didn't even get as deep as we could on this, but it's all fundamental to understanding the Gospel, and who is the seed of Abraham, how he blessed all nations. How through that seed, Abraham had multitudes too numerous to count as heirs to the promise made when he called upon the name of the Lord. The promise made when *he believed in the Lord; and He counted it to him for righteousness.* That his righteousness was imputed for that faith, by a gracious God. And it was faith in that seed to be given by the Lord, and the blessings for that heir and the promise made in Him.

As we will see in Esau and Jacob, the blessings and promises of the heir are important. The free will choices made by man, and faith in God determining who received them, not the law. For under the law the eldest received the inheritance. And the blessing.

*And he said,* Lord God, *whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?* And the word of God tells him to sacrifice *an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.*

Each a sign or a picture of Christ. As established in the Levitical laws, 400+ years from when this is happening, done to show they mercy of God in redemption by faith, in the blood offerings, the sin offerings, the burnt offerings. A testimony necessitates a blood offering. These were a symbol of Christ's.

And in a deep sleep, a darkness fell upon Abram, and the word of God said; *Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* prophesying the time to come and the sojourning to Egypt and enslavement. *And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.* Moses writing in the Spirit of the prophecy of Exodus given to Abraham.

*And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age. But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.*

The LORD telling Abram that he himself will die knowing peace, but that the land will not be given unto his descendants until the wickedness of the Amorites comes in. They are going to purge the land of Canaan of the wicked, as an instrument of the Lord. Against *The Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites, And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,*
*And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.*

And a furnace and a lamp appeared on the offerings, passing between those pieces laid on an altar, a testament signed by God.

teachings.title: I see men as trees, walking
teachings.summary: Those who call Jesus Lord but trust their own works are like the half-healed blind man and Peter, savouring the things of men and blind to the imputed righteousness of Christ.
teachings.text:
*I see men as trees, walking.*

*And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign?*

*Perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened? Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?*

*And whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.*
*And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him. But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.*

This is the theme of Mark chapter 8, isn't it? The blind, being shown the light, yet not fully seeing. Of seeking a sign and yet missing the signs all around them. Of seeing the truth, as trees, walking; blurry and not quite focused enough to understand the details and see it's true shape, like poor Peter. Or blind entirely like the Pharisees, asking for light when it's shining bright before then.

The healing of the blind man is the healing of the faithful, who at first see the light as if afar off, bringing some clarity out of the darkness. Seeing how things move, the shapes of things. But once saved, come fully into the light. Having our vision healed by the word of God, that we may see clearly.

The Apostles, despite having understanding, witnessing the feeding of 5000, the 4000, with a handful of loaves and a couple of fishes, filling all men up, and like the grace of God, with an abundance left over, stumble like the blind man with his partial sight restored. Missing the truth of it, though knowing Jesus was Christ.

This was why Jesus cautioned those He healed to say nothing of it to others. Both to protect them that were healed from the adversaries, the Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes, and to show signs and wonders that His sheep may see and believe, but not proclaiming them to those of that wicked generation, seeking after a sign, evidence of who Jesus is, while missing the signs all around them.

*That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.*

Jesus' exasperated sigh at the inability of His own closest disciples not understanding precisely who He is, and protesting what He must do on the cross that the glory of God be made manifest is something many Christians today feel when talking to those who call Jesus "Lord, Lord" and then proceed to talk of their works. Who call themselves by His name, Christians, and yet cannot see the truth when presented to them.

Who, sensing the light and seeing the movement, yet see men as trees, walking. Unable to discern the shapes of things. Missing the signs of the times. Not comprehending the wonders shown in Christ.

And as Jesus says, *Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.*

They savor the thing of man, not the things of God.

And so they remain blind to the full truth. Their faith is in vain.

*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

When believers are faced with those full of zeal for the Lord, but going about to establish their own righteousness rather than the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, we sigh in exasperation and ask, "are ye hearts still hardened?"

If Jesus felt that way, who being God is longsuffering and patient, it is understandable that we too can reach that point when dealing with the heresies and false understanding that so many have today.

teachings.title: Christ the physician of sinners
teachings.summary: Christ forgiving the palsied man's sins proves His deity, and His call to sinners shows all need the physician, made clean by His imputed righteousness, not by their own.
teachings.text:
The healing of the man lowered by 4 into a full house where Jesus was preaching is a beautiful picture how many with faith may bring us to salvation. Jesus forgiving his sins, and then healing his flesh in opposition to the scribes questioning in their hearts His authority gives a definitive statement of the divinity of Christ. "Who can forgive sins but God only?" Exactly.

Notice it's the faith expressed, not only of the man with palsy, but those who bring him to Jesus that moves Christ. It is the faith that leads to His forgiveness of sin. The healing of infirmity comes after. This is such a picture of salvation and the moving of the Spirit in a saved Christian's life. And notice, all to the glory of God. "*They were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.*"

Next we see Jesus call upon a publican, a tax collector, identified here and in Luke as Levi, but better known as the Apostle Matthew. Jesus calls him from his position collecting tax on the goods coming into port in Capernaum and bids the publican to follow Him and he does.

A Levite publican, a double blow to the worldly Pharisees. One of their own collecting tribute for Rome. No greater sinner in their mind, and to dine with one, that would be "unclean."

Jesus's answer to their outrage, that He was here as a physician, to heal the sick, calling the sinners to repentance towards God, as the righteous have no need of a "doctor," is a backhanded insult to the Pharisees. They are not righteous. There is none righteous by the works of the law, and certainly not these hypocrites. But their own conceit would keep them from seeing His point. In matters of righteousness we are all in need of a physician, Christ Jesus.

We shouldn't lose sight of that truth, and understand it's not the sins that make us clean or unclean.

It's not our own righteousness in following the law, but our hearts and spirit of faith in Christ Jesus to impute His righteousness on us that heals. That makes us clean. Washed in the blood.

There is a natural man argument that many unsaved scoffers and reprobates make is that Jesus "hung out with the sinners" and not the "holy rollers." They take this verse and blaspheme, claiming Jesus liked to "party with sinners" to excuse their own unregenerate lifestyle.

Of course they meltdown when you correct them that He certainly preached to the sinners to bring them out of sin, but actually hung out with, was friends with, His Apostles and closest disciples.

That physicians don't "hang out" with the sick, they treat them to be well. This understanding escapes them, and I have seen more than a few Christians unable to make this distinction and get confused or browbeaten into not calling out sin. Ignoring the sickness. Enabling the worst behaviors, simply to not be seen as a "Pharisee."

Both the hypocritical fruit inspectors and degenerates are sick and in need of a physician.

teachings.title: The wedding feast and the wedding garment
teachings.summary: The wedding feast parable shows God inviting all after the Jews rejected Him, and the guest without a wedding garment, in his own righteousness, is cast out because only Christ's imputed righteousness clothes us.
teachings.text:
We have begun the series of chapters in Matthew, (starting in 21 which we covered yesterday, and continuing in 22-25), of nonstop preaching by Jesus. In parables, in scriptures, in harsh rebuke, and revelation, leading up to His crucifixion. Where the scribes, lawyers, Pharisees and Sadducees come to tempt Jesus, to test His doctrine and find fault with Him, that they may accuse Him. But having not understanding of the word, they each fail to Christ's perfect understanding, as the word made flesh.

Today's reading opens with Jesus continuing in parables to convict the so-called holy men of Jerusalem for their dereliction and disobedience to God. He has described them as the son who agreed to work the fields for their father, but did not go. To being the husbandmen of the vineyard, who rather than giving of the fruits of the harvest to the lord,  beat and slay his servants, and betray and kill his son in an attempt to steal his inheritance and deny their lord his increase. Jesus has revealed to the crowd, hailing Him as a prophet of God, the hypocrisy of their religious leaders, and if it were not for fear of that crowd, the high preists would have seized Jesus there at the temple.

Jesus now boldly preaches on the Kingdom of Heaven, His Father's Kingdom, likening it unto a wedding feast for the Son.

And the King sends forth servants to bid all to come to the wedding, and none would.

He instructs his servants to tell all that that they bid to the feast that the work is done, the meal is ready, the meat slain and prepared, and so come, and yet those bidden scoff and make light of it, and returned to their merchandise, to their money, to their land and material goods and wealth. And some took the King's servants, treated them spitefully and murdered them.

And so the King in his wrath sends armies to destroy the people whom he had invited. Whom he had assured all was ready. Who refused to believe him and come. Who killed those who came to invite them. He destroyed them utterly.

And now, still requiring guests for the feast prepared, to share in the work the King had done, he tells his servants to go out, to the highways, throughout the land, and as many as they find, bid to the feast.

God had promised this wedding, this celebration of His righteousness and love, His creation, to mankind from Adam, and was rejected by most. He gave a select people the details, written in His law and spoken to of the prophets that they may be a light to the nations, bringing the world to the feast. And they rejected His word and slew His prophets.

And so, God destroying them, sends His servants to bid all to salvation. Both bad and good. Whomever will come.

And as the parable continues, the King sees a guest arrive, without a garment fit for the feast. In his own filthy rags, his own righteousness, representing those who believe they can enter the Kingdom by their own works. The King has him bound and removed, cast into the outer darkness. The lake of fire that is the fate of all who do not have the spotless white garment given to believers by the lamb of God. The imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ which covers all our sin.

For many are called, but few are chosen, for they rejected the invitation. Didn't believe the report. Didn't arrive dressed for the feast.

teachings.title: Christ the propitiation for the whole world
teachings.summary: A chain of scriptures shows Christ was the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, and by believing we are clothed in His righteousness.
teachings.text:
**Romans 3:25** - *Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;*

**1 John 2:2** - *And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.*

**1 John 4:10** - *Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.*

**John 3:16** - *For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

**Hebrews 9:14** - *How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?*

**2 Corinthians 5:21** - *For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

**Psalm 103:12** - *As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.*

*13 Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.*

*14 For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.*

**2 Corinthians 5:19** - *To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.*

**Titus 3:5** *Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;*

*6 Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;*

*7 That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

**Philippians 3:9** - *And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith:*

**Isaiah 53:11** - *He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.*

**Galatians 2:16** - *Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

Jesus took on our sin and paid the price for all of it. He was the propitiation. The ransom. The sacrifice.

By believing this, we take on His righteousness. His blood washes us clean. We are clothed in White of His perfection, our sins forgotten.

teachings.title: Righteousness exceeding the scribes and Pharisees
teachings.summary: Christ came to fulfil the law not destroy it, and only His righteousness, not the loophole righteousness of the Pharisees, can bring us into the kingdom.
teachings.text:
*17 Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.*

*18 For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.*

*19 Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.*

*20 For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.*

Jesus tells us that the law of God, being perfect and preserved, isn't being upended by what He preached or His eventual death and resurrection, but fulfilling all things in the end. That all shall be made subject to Him, the earth as His footstool and the promise of the Kingdom kept for the children of God. The Jews hearing this being familiar with scripture, knowing the law, the prophets and the promise, would understand, at least those with ears to hear. Those seeking righteousness.

Unlike the claimed righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, who taught loopholes and exceptions to God's law and accused Jesus of seeking to destroy it, we must have the righteousness of Christ to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, exceeding those hypocrites' false idea of righteousness.

teachings.title: Counting my own righteousness as dung
teachings.summary: Paul counted his lineage, circumcision and law-keeping as dung to have the righteousness of God by faith, warning of the concision, while still pressing on in sanctification out of love.
teachings.text:
Paul turns to the matter of adhering to the law and circumcision, a theme of epistles stemming from the decision made in Acts to warn against adding to the gospel of faith by Judaizers.

Paul argues to these Gentiles, that if birth, circumcision and zeal for the law saved anyone, it would be Paul, but he counts all his own "righteousness" as dung, so that he may gain Christ.

He warns to beware the dogs, reprobates sneaking in and judaizing churches, subverting houses, crept in unawares. Evil workers. They of the circumcision. Paul says
*they are the enemies of the cross of Christ.*

Because believers are not circumcised of the flesh, but of the heart. Saved by faith, *not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection.*

Paul does remind us that despite our having the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, we should strive for sanctification, to be more perfect, more complete in our walk. Striving for the mark.

*Nevertheless, whereto we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing.*

Obeying the law, not for our own righteousness but for the love of God. Not walking as the reprobates do, glorying in the sins of the flesh. Their end is destruction, but ours is in Heaven and eternal life.

By believing this, we take on His righteousness. His blood washes us clean. We are clothed in White of his perfection, our sins forgotten.

It is an exchange. That is the testament.

teachings.title: Repentance is metanoia, not turning from sin
teachings.theme: Repentance is a change of mind
teachings.summary: Repentance is a change of mind that brings discernment, and turning from sin follows only if the new man is fed, while the backslider is still saved.
teachings.text:
Repentance, or metanoia, having a change of heart, coming to a new understanding that is (by grace, led of the Spirit); discernment.

We gain discernment regarding the will of God and the state of ourselves and man in relation to Him, when we repent. When we believe the scriptures that say God would offer a sacrifice of His own making to free us from death and Hell. That that sacrifice is the Son of God, Jesus Christ.

That discernment, if the new man created at salvation is fed, leads to a change in attitude towards sin. It becomes less desirable. The lusts of the flesh can lose their appeal. Even disgusting us.

If that new man isn't fed, and they continue walking in the flesh, they are still saved by the knowledge of the truth, but that discernment is dulled and God may have to chasten the person to work godly sorrow in their heart. If they remain backslidden, God may call them home.

But they are still saved.

Saying "real repentance WILL mean you turn from sin, and WILL walk in the Spirit," is false. We must pick up our cross daily. It is a choice to engage in sanctification. But salvation is of Christ, not ourselves. It is by grace, not of ourselves.

teachings.title: Repentance is a change of heart, not works
teachings.theme: Repentance is a change of mind
teachings.summary: Repentance is believing what we did not before, and the lost stumble at accepting salvation as a free gift sealed by the Spirit, which false prophets exploit.
teachings.text:
These conditions aren't of you. They aren't works. They are the truth of God what we repent towards to avail ourselves of His gift to us. Repentance means a change of heart, to believe something that we hadn't before.

People know they are sinners. People understand that we are not right with God. His wrath is revealed from heaven, so that we have no excuse. The Holy Spirit works in all men (least they be reprobate concerning the faith), reproving us that we know we've done wrong and need reconciliation.

Most people, even secular types, have some understanding of who historical Jesus is, and that He is claimed to be the Son of God. They have a head knowledge that He lived, was crucified and that Christians say He rose again.

Where unsaved people fail at is in accepting that salvation is a free gift, that doesn't require anything of us beyond faith. That the grace of God is sufficient to save us, and that grace is given us through the blood of His Son. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. That once we are saved, we are sealed unto the day of redemption by the Spirit. People struggle with these things, and that is why most people are perishing.

And false prophets feed this insecurity and these misunderstandings, subverting the truth, and keep people from the faith.

teachings.title: Sinners called to repentance, the doctor first
teachings.theme: Repentance is a change of mind
teachings.summary: When Jesus called sinners to repentance He meant turning from works religion toward God for healing, not cleaning up first; we go to the doctor to be healed.
teachings.text:
What many miss regarding repentance in the Gospels is that Jesus had come to lead the people trapped in the works-based, hypocritical heresy that had become the religion of the Pharisees, and the hopeless secularism of the Sadducees. The state of religion in Judea and Jews in general, turning from the faith of their fathers and the prophets, and towards the self-righteous faith of outward appearance, the circumcision of the flesh over the circumcision of the heart.

When Jesus says to repent, He isn't talking about cleaning up your life, and trying to live more in line with the law. That's the false religion of the Pharisee that He repeatedly condemns.

He calls sinners to repentance, towards God. Towards the salvation of faith in grace He is there to fulfill. The remission of sins that is the result of repentance unto faith. Then the healing of the body. Then the turning from sin. We go to the doctor to be healed. We don't get healed to see the doctor.

*I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.*

The righteous in Christ should turn away from their sin. Put away and mortify the lusts of the flesh and the warring members of the old man. To feed the new man and walk in the spirit. But it is the sick of spirit, those dead inside that He came to heal that they could be made whole. That the Spirit could quicken ours in our faith.

*Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins.*

teachings.title: Judas repented, yet went to his own place
teachings.theme: Repentance is a change of mind
teachings.summary: Judas repented of betraying innocent blood yet was damned, showing that repenting of a wrong is not believing on Christ, which is why modern versions change repented to remorse.
teachings.text:
As the lamb without blemish is led away by the chief preists to Pilate, we are told Judas Iscariot, who had betrayed Christ for 30 pieces of silver, repented, changed his mind, thought better of what he'd done, and saying, *I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood.*

**Psalms 41:9** - *Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.*

**Zechariah 11:12** - *And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.*

Judas, rebuffed by the preists of the temple, and unable to come to salvation having been damned by his rejection of the truth, hanged himself, and the 30 pieces of silver used to buy a potters field for the graves of strangers.

**Luke 22:22** *For the Son of man indeed goeth, as it hath been determined: but woe unto that man through whom he is betrayed!*

Repenting of a wrong done doesn't equate with believing on Christ for salvation.

Jesus said to His Apostles, of Judas "*Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?”*

And as he hanged himself, the Bible tells us the details of his fate;

**Acts 1:18** *Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.*

*19 And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.*

*20 For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.*

*21 Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,*

*22 Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection.*

*23 And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.*

*24 And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,*

*25 That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.*

"His own place" being a euphemism for Hell, a place man earns for himself, (as opposed to Heaven by which no man can earn their way in to possess).

I will note that in modern translations, they remove the word "repented" here, and replace it with "felt remorse," because the idea that Judas repented would conflict with the false teaching of turning from sin to be saved, rather than faith in Christ, and it would lead people to question if Judas repented, if he is in Heaven. Again, reminding us that bad doctrine begets bad doctrine and confusion. And they have to further change God's word to take on new meaning to support it.

teachings.title: Conflating godly sorrow with saving repentance
teachings.theme: Repentance is a change of mind
teachings.summary: Making repentance of sin the way to be born again confuses sorrow with the change of mind toward faith in Christ, turns salvation into works, and shuts out many who come to Christ by other paths.
teachings.text:
It is the conflating of regret/godly sorrow/understanding of our sinful nature and the wages of death earned by it, with the actual change of mind, turning to faith in God, in Christ for our salvation, upon which bad doctrine and damnable heresies are founded.

"What must I do to be saved?"

*Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and thou shall be saved*.

*That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved*.

This is what we must repent towards, to believe to be saved.

Regardless of how we get to the point of repentance, of taking the truth we hear and believing it, in our heart, turning towards God.

Not of sin, though godly sorrow for sin may lead us there. Not of any works, or deeds of the law. Not of our sincere, careful, vehement desire to make right what we've done wrong in godly sorrow. These may work us to the change of heart and towards faith, but they aren't requirements for salvation, which is to believe on Jesus Christ, that He was raised from the dead.

Some call upon the name of the Lord while in tribulation, being beset by the wicked and surrounded by enemies. In desperation, stricken by poor health, or in mourning for a loved one. By example of the righteous being kind and compassionate to them in their hour of need. Of being fed and clothed by believers, when they had nothing and hungered. Of seeing God's light magnified in the kindness and charity, mercy and faith of we who believe.

The Bible tells us of many circumstance that brings a sinner to repentance towards God. It is not always of guilt and shame. Making it so excludes many from receiving the Gospel, and the prominence of this doctrine, making repentance of sin the way to be born again, places the onus of salvation, of being justified, upon the would-be believers to clean up their act. It implies that this is the means of salvation, their ability to do the works of the law. It becomes works salvation, either before the fact, or after, to show "genuine repentance," to maintain salvation, or as proof it was real.

To both backslidden believers and the unregenerate sinner who had already 'cleaned up their life,' and had genuine sorrow and repented of their sins, but not believed on Christ, it places a stumbling block.

It is a wicked heresy for this very reason. And that is why Satan pushes it so hard.

teachings.title: Resentment toward those saved without hitting bottom
teachings.theme: Repentance is a change of mind
teachings.summary: Teaching that one must repent of sins to be saved can make those who came to Christ through deep sorrow resent and doubt believers who came by easier paths.
teachings.text:
