But to be justified before man, that outward sign of his faith, made his faith more perfect. There was a visible tangible act of faith, works that a man may say that they've been shown his faith.

teachings.title: Delivered and translated into the kingdom
teachings.summary: Colossians 1 shows God has already delivered, redeemed and reconciled believers the moment they believed, so we should be thankful and extend that grace to others.
teachings.text:
**Colossians 1:9-15**
*For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God; Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness; Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins*

Be thankful that God has already done so much for us that have been justified in Christ, while we were yet sinners.

God has already made us *partakers of the inheritance of the saints*, *delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son*, and so, *we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins*.

As in verse 20-21; *having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled*

We are now reconciled, having made peace with the Father through the blood of the Son.

This is the good news, the glory of the Gospel of God. All of these promises have been fulfilled already, the moment you believed and received the baptism of the Spirit, quickening your spirit and sealing you into redemption.

*As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him.*

Amen. Let us give glory to the Lord Jesus for this, and to God the Father for having the grace and mercy towards us that all these things have been predestined for those who place their trust in Christ.

Knowing this peace and forgiveness and reconciliation, knowing this grace and mercy, let us extend it to our brothers, and to others that they know of our conversion, and hear the gospel on which we stand by faith.

Amen

teachings.title: Therefore being justified by faith
teachings.summary: Justified by faith we have peace with God now and stand in grace, and even glory in tribulations that work patience, experience and hope.
teachings.text:
Therefore.

When we see this word we have to ask ourselves "what's it there for?" What does it refer back to?

Well, 4 chapters of Paul logically and with irrefutable proof from scripture that all are under sin and need salvation, and that salvation is through faith in Jesus Christ, by the grace of God.

Therefore. Therefore what?

*Being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

As the heavenly hosts proclaimed in the hills of Bethlehem at the birth of the man Christ Jesus;

*Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.*

The peace and goodwill on earth was come from God to man. Not the peace of men not warring. Not goodwill between tribes. But the enmity of wrath in the transgressions of man made justified by the peace offering of His only begotten Son.

We are justified by faith alone. There is nothing more noted. We have already concluded that by the works of the law no man shall be justified. We already know that by faith, Abraham became father to all who believe. We already know that the judgment of God is upon Jew and Greek alike. And that Jesus as propitiation for our sin has given us salvation from the wrath we deserve.

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

What's more; By faith we have access into the grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

Believing, we are given grace, and by grace, God is given the glory for our salvation. Note, "wherein we stand." This isn't the future, this isn't a process. This is now, at the time of our repentance towards belief in Christ as our redeemer we then, at that moment, stand in grace. And rejoice.

And we not only rejoice in the glory of God's grace that provides us with salvation through faith, because it shows the mercy and judgment and righteousness of God (which remember is one way His glory is revealed to man from Heaven), we also glory in tribulations here on earth, knowing they are a refining fire; that worketh patience, which brings experience, and experience brings hope. Hope builds faith.

*Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*.

Hope is the sure knowledge that a thing will be that is not yet. The object of faith. Tribulation in our lives, not only persecution for our faith, but just general troubles like health, finance, whatever things common to all men, saved or unsaved, all of it gives opportunity to glorify the Lord, as it makes our faith sharper as we are brought out of it by His mercy and blessings, better for having experienced it.

And our hope is fufifiled in the love of God, by the comforter, the Holy Ghost, which is given us, who indwells with us, quickening our spirit and leading us to that peace which passes all understanding, even in turmoil and crisis.

Our faith in man, traditions, our own works, all will leave us ashamed at some point. But the hope we have in Christ Jesus will never bring us shame. God never lets us down.

teachings.title: While we were yet sinners
teachings.summary: God showed His love by Christ dying for His enemies, so much more shall the reconciled be saved by His life and spared wrath.
teachings.text:
And how do we know that God's word is good, that our hope is true? Because

*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us*.

That when we were still enemies, working inequities, dead in sin, God reconciled us through the death of His Son. God loved His enemies, and offered the free gift of salvation by the shedding of blood of His only begotten Son.

Think about this, for in it is the righteousness of God.

And if He offered us such a gift, if a righteous man gave His life for us while we were enemies, dying for us while we were dead in sin, then how much more shall He do for us whom have been reconciled to Him in faith by the death of His Son? Who stand in His grace? We shall be saved by His life in the resurrection.

And not only so, that we shall know we will be saved out of tribulation by His resurrection and the promise of God to us likewise for eternal life, but we also joy, rejoice, in God through our Lord Jesus Christ by whom we have now received the atonement.

Our hope is that, today we who believe are spared wrath for our sins, adopted to the promise, and that in tribulation on this earth we will be saved by God's love for His sons, because of the atonement of Christ Jesus that we holdfast to in faith. Amen

teachings.title: Jesus' torment in Hell for our sins
teachings.summary: Jesus spent the days after the cross in Hell bearing the sins of the world as the propitiation, which few Christians care to reflect on.
teachings.text:
We should consider that at this point that first holy week, that Jesus was spending His first full day in Hell, carrying the sins of the whole world. Each moment of torment must have felt like a lifetime; Jesus, as the burnt offering, the Holocaust, the propitiation of our sins that we may be justified in Him. He had 2 more full days to follow.

Many Christians gladly celebrate Easter, rejoicing that He is risen. Some will consider the pain and suffering of the cross. Few want to reflect on His torment in Hell for our sins. He who knew no sin, paying the price for us.

It's something we should reflect on.

teachings.title: One Offering Perfected For Ever
teachings.summary: Christ's one offering cleanses the conscience forever, and the conscience marks three states of man: guilty, cleansed, or seared in reprobation.
teachings.text:
Now having established that Jesus Christ, the Son of God seated at the right hand of the Father, is greater than the angels, greater than Moses, Abraham, David, in all ways, better than the Levites and the descendants of Aaron as the High Priest after the order of Melchisedek, Paul continues to show the superiority of Christ to the Mosaic law itself, which is a picture of His glory. That faith in Him that saves and the promises made of God for that faith, a better covenant. A new and better testament.

Better than the commandments which condemn us, transgressions of the law being sin, better than the dead works which cannot save us and Jesus as our redeemer is a better sacrifice than all the sacrifices offered under the law.

The entire epistle is an appeal to the superiority and primacy of Christ Jesus as our Lord, High Priest, advocate, and sole means of the cleansing of our sins, in either dispensation. Man has always been saved by grace through faith in Christ. The blood of bulls and goats never took away sins. It was not possible, the Bible says. No sacrifice other than Christ cleans the conscience. And so those who yearly sought forgiveness by sin offering rather than as a picture of their faith, fruitlessly returned year after year seeking to clean their conscience.

A conscience, or "with knowledge," offended by sin, knowingly transgressing the law, with understanding, can only be made clean with the blood of Christ. The vail only removed by His flesh, offered for us. A better sacrifice, done once and forever. Taking on the sins of the whole world.

Burnt offerings and sacrifice for sin gave God no pleasure, but Jesus doing the will of the Father, to become sin and die for us that all may be called and those that believe be saved, sanctified once and for all in the offering of Jesus Christ's body. In this the LORD delights.

For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

Practical application of this, the implications of this, that we are forgiven of all sin by this perfect sanctification, total remission, forever, is that we be freed from the burden of guilt and the fear of judgment that we may serve the living God.

Faith in Christ is to be born again, our spirit without sin. The Holy Ghost as witness that we can let go of the sins of the past and have full assurance of forgiveness for sins of the flesh going forward. The knowledge that God so loved us, He offered His only begotten Son. The rest that is found in Christ. The true Sabbath.

*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

*Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin....*

Most of our troubles as man come from the carrying of that burden. The heavy yoke of the conscience. The fear of judgment and death. The pangs of guilt are the Spirit, bringing us reproof of sin that we may understand the need for salvation, and pricked by the hearing of His word, come to understanding and in that knowledge, repent unto faith.

But for some, who taste that heavenly knowledge, partake in the rebuke of the Holy Ghost, reject it. Resenting being judged. Clinging to the trauma, reveling in their sin. And they willfully sin knowing the judgment of God, rejecting Christ and being made reprobate by God. Having their conscience seared as with hot iron.

These are the three spiritual states of man. Unsaved, saved and reprobate. And the underlying condition of fallen man comes in our conscience; be it guilty, cleansed by the blood, or seared by God for our hardened heart.

teachings.title: Christ Offered Once to Bear Our Sins
teachings.summary: Substitutionary atonement teaches that Christ's blood, pictured by the old sacrifices, sealed the better testament and removed the veil between God and man.
teachings.text:
Substitutionary atonement, also called vicarious atonement, the Biblical understanding Jesus Christ being the sacrifice that takes away the sins of the whole world, to the salvation of those who believe, is laid out here (and throughout scripture) as the blood needed to affirm the promise made by God the Father. Just as the blood of bulls and goats was used to seal the covenant with Moses, or marked by Abraham with his promise from God.

But these sacrifices were for a time and a place and acted as a picture for the perfect sacrifice of Jesus Christ, Whose blood marked the promise of a better testament, one in which the separation from God pictured by the temple, the veils, the Levitical priests, dietary laws, marking of days and carnal ordinances of the Old Testament is done away with.

Here at the end of the world, Jesus was offered once and put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself. And in doing so, became our High Priest, and we who believe adopted sons, a holy priesthood. The separation from God is gone. The veil torn asunder.

Many false religions posing as Christians deny the idea that Jesus was the sacrifice that gave us the offer of God's mercy. They deny the grace of a loving God who bought them with the price of His Son. That the shedding of blood and the remission of sins isn't the way, but instead these thorns and briars produce evil fruit that cannot repent from dead works to serve the living God.

But the Bible teaches us the truth of the matter. That Jesus as the sole mediator between God and man was by the means of His death, becoming sin for the redemption of transgressions. (For sin is the transgression of the law).

A testament having no power while the testator liveth. And so the death of the testator signified that those called had come into their promised inheritance. Amen.

So Christ was offered once to bear our sins. And those of us who believed look to His coming to our day of redemption. The Spirit as the surety of the promise, a testimony within us to the truth of God's word.

teachings.title: Princes under tutors until the adoption
teachings.summary: Proverbs for kings and princes are for saved believers, co-heirs who will rule with Christ, since the adoption, the placing as sons, comes at the resurrection, the redemption of the body.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 25** introduces a section (chapters 25–29) of Solomon’s proverbs that were compiled by King Hezekiah's officials, approximately 250–270 years after Solomon's reign.

Hezekiah, the son of the wicked king, Ahaz, began a revival and reformation, tearing down altars and idols. In the first month of his reign, Hezekiah opened and repaired the doors of the House of the Lord. He commanded the Levites to "sanctify" themselves and carry *forth the filthiness out of the holy place*. He restored the observance of Passover. He brought order to the Levites, and proclaimed tithes and offerings from the people.

And in his zeal, the young king commanded scribes to write these sayings of Solomon, that they be preserved and observed.

They begin with the honor of kings to search out the hidden things of God.

**1 Corinthians 2:10**
*But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.*

As I have previously stated, my opinion is that the wisdom for princes and kings is for the saved, as co-heirs with Christ. Even the least in the Kingdom of Heaven is a prince, who will judge with Him in the millennium. We will judge angels. The study of the word is like unto princes under tutors, until the day of adoption. The resurrection where we come into our power as glorified sons of God.

**Galatians 4**
*Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father*.

The context here is the law bringing man to understand the need for a savior, but the application mirrors the process of a prince coming into his own by instruction, until the determined time of the King.

As Paul writes in **Romans 8:23** ...*even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.* The day of redemption, the resurrection, is the day of our adoption; the time of the giving of the inheritance, to rule and reign with Jesus.

The Greek word Paul uses for 'adoption,' *huiothesia*, carries a heavier legal meaning than our modern idea of adoption. In that context, it wasn't about bringing an outsider into a family; it was the formal ceremony, the "placing as a son," where an heir reached the age of maturity, the father publicly recognized them as a legal adult, granting them the full authority, a signet ring, and power to manage the estate, or the lands appointed them.

We become sons of God when we are born again, but notice the adoption is at the resurrection. At the day of redemption.

So, when we see proverbs about kings or princes, about judgement and mercy, who to be influenced by, who to seek counsel from...it is all instructions from THE King, God our Father, to His children, who will inherit the Kingdom.

teachings.title: Who are the sons of God?
teachings.summary: Scripture defines the sons of God as believers who receive Christ and are adopted as joint heirs with Him, from Seth's day to now.
teachings.text:
And so, who are the sons of God? The Bible says *as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Believers. Those that call upon the name of the Lord.

*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope, Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.*

Those born again into the promise, adopted sons, heirs to the Kingdom of the Lord.

Adopted now, as in the days of Seth and Enos and Enoch and even Noah; *That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world.*

*Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God!*

Take comfort in this knowledge, joy in the incomprehensible love God has shown us, that we may be adopted joint heirs with His only begotten Son, Christ Jesus.

*Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.*

We know that all who believe are the sons of God. That we appear before God in Heaven to present ourselves before the Lord. When God laid Jesus as the cornerstone of our salvation, the angels sang and all the sons of God shouted for joy. And in Christ Jesus God has made His covenant with man, that He *will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.*

teachings.title: Then are the children free
teachings.summary: As kings take tribute from strangers not their children, believers are free sons who pay nothing to enter the kingdom, yet as sojourners still pay tribute to whom it is due.
teachings.text:
The second story told in the chapter is one of tax collectors seeking tribute from Peter for him and Jesus. Peter rightly tells them that he will make good on the payment of tribute to whom tribute is due. And he goes and asks Jesus on the matter. Jesus takes the time to teach an important lesson regarding salvation and the inheritance obtained by our faith.

He asks Peter *of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers?* Peter replies, "Strangers."

*Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free.*

We who are saved by grace through faith are adopted as sons of God, heirs to His promise and the Kingdom of Heaven. We are free of custom and duty, tribute and tax.

Our entrance to the kingdom is free, for we are at Liberty in Christ. We pay nothing, not our works or labors or deeds. It is a gift of God given to all who believe.

But while we sojourn here on earth, we pay tribute to whom tribute is due, and render custom to whom custom is due, because we are sojourning here, strangers in the land. Princes of a better country. Amen

teachings.title: All believers are saints
teachings.summary: Saint is the New Testament title for every believer, not a rank Rome bestows for works, and the peace announced at Christ's birth is peace between God and men through grace.
teachings.text:
Another point to make regarding the introduction, that Paul addresses to the saints and believers, terms which are interchangeable in the New Testament. All believers are saints. It's a title bestowed throughout to all who believe. It is not a select few whose Works were so good that they are honored here on Earth with the title. By making a church of man the arbiter, and basing it on works, the Catholic church has cheapened the term. I am a saint. If you believe you are a saint as well. Even if your backslidden, even if you need to turn from sins that are consuming your life. And as saints we should turn from sin, we should live a righteous life as possible. Live up to it.

Secondly Paul frequently writes that he prays for Grace from God to us the reader, and with that grace, peace.

The only piece we have with God is through his grace, and Christ Jesus. At the nativity the Angels announced peace on Earth. Goodwill towards men. This is a message from God to man, that he is granting them peace with Him, and goodwill through the birth of Jesus. The angel isn't saying that they'll be peace upon the Earth between men, but rather peace between God and men.

teachings.title: Sons of the freewoman, not the bondwoman
teachings.summary: Believers are adopted heirs freed from the tutors of the law, and as Isaac and Ishmael show, those born of the Spirit inherit while those under the bondage of works are cast out.
teachings.text:
Building upon the doctrine that we who believe God are adopted by God, sons according to the promise; being heirs. Continuing that thought, Paul makes the comparison of the law vs grace, that the son can be heir but under a schoolmaster, tutors and governors, yet in the fullness of time, be as the Lord, an inheritor of all. So to, he's saying, the Israelites were when under the law, children of the promise, not come into their inheritance. Now, with the fullness of Christ, all who believe are adopted and freed from the burden of the law, of the tutors and governess, to their inheritance.

Paul explaining this in these terms, as laid out in Hebrew scripture that they may understand, given there are Jews pushing the Galatians to go back under that bondage. Paul says he's afraid of the Galatians that they may be so easily led to a false gospel, that he questions if they even were saved. That we who believe have the Spirit of the Son within us. That we have that quickened spirit, born again crying "Abba!"(Father) to God. They should know better. They should recognize the error. Yet they don't, and so Paul has to assume his labor in preaching the Gospel of grace was in vain, that they aren't saved.

He reminds them that before his preaching the word to them, they served idols, living as heathens, and these judaizers come in and return them to superstition, marking sabbaths and holy days done away with in Christ. Returning them to the bondage of works based salvation.

He reminds them of when he was present with them, the zeal for the Gospel they held, that in spite of a physical infirmity, apparently with Paul's eyes, they readily accepted him to the point they'd have plucked out their own eyes to right his. But now he's their enemy for telling them the truth. He compares winning them to Christ with travails of a mother in birth, and says he's willing to do it to bring them to salvation.

Changing gears, and having established that our salvation is one of adoption, blessing and inheritance from the Father, he asks those who are going back to the OT if they even know it, and uses an example from the Law, the story of Isaac and Ihsmael. How, as told in Genesis 17, Abraham had a son, Ishmael, with a slave woman, Hagar, by natural means, and Isaac with his wife Sara, by spiritual means. When Issac was still an infant, Ishmael teased him, and Sara demanded Abraham to kick Hagar and the boy out, denying him any share of inheritance.

Thus we who are born again in the Spirit become heirs, while those trying to work their way into the kingdom, those under bondage, are denied.

*Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.*

And, again as Ishmael the son of the flesh persecuted Isaac, son of the Spirit, so to now the Jews after the flesh are misleading them, persecuting the heirs in Christ.

*Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.*

teachings.title: Continue in the grace of God
teachings.summary: Shows from Acts 13:43 that converts were persuaded to continue in the grace of God, and that there was never a different plan of salvation, only grace by faith.
teachings.text:
**Acts 13:43**
*Now when the congregation was broken up, many of the Jews and religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas: who, speaking to them, **persuaded** them to continue in the grace of God.*

These Jews and Gentile proselytes, or converts to the Hebrew religion of the Old Testament, were persuaded to *continue in the grace of God*. Not repent. Not leave the faith, but to continue in it, knowing Jesus was the Christ. The Messiah that the prophets all gave witness to. The Lord they'd called upon to to be saved. The Deliverer. Him that all them that looked for redemption, for the Savior.

They were persuaded by the scriptures and how they all pointed to Jesus, to continue in the grace of God.

There was never a different plan of salvation. It was always by faith in God's Christ. Paul preached the gospel, according to the scriptures. 

Not a new gospel. Not a different Dispensation. A new covenant that fulfils the old, replacing it with better promises and blessings. 

But it has always been grace entered into by faith.

teachings.title: One gospel in all ages
teachings.summary: Says there has always been one gospel, salvation by calling on the Lord and believing His word by grace through faith, and quotes Galatians 1:8-9.
teachings.text:
There was, is and will always be one gospel. The same in all ages. Salvation by calling upon the name of the Lord, believing His Word. By grace through faith.

**Galatians 1:8-9**
*But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

teachings.title: Calling upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Says calling on the Lord is admitting you are a sinner and confessing He is the Christ, not turning from sins, asking Jesus into your heart or giving your life to Him.
teachings.text:
Admitting that you're a sinner. Not "turning from your sins.

Calling upon the name of the Lord isn't "asking Jesus into your heart." It's confessing He is the Christ.

It's not giving your life to Jesus, it's knowing He gave His for you.

teachings.title: One way of salvation in every dispensation
teachings.summary: Says animal sacrifice was never a means of salvation and that dispensationalism errs in claiming a different means of salvation for ethnic Jews in the end times.
teachings.text:
I don't know who needs to hear this but animal sacrifice never was a dispensation or ministration of salvation or grace or a means of justification. The blood of bulls and goats could never take away sin. 

There's only ever been one ministration given to save souls, and that's calling upon the name of the Lord and trusting in Him alone. We have a dispensation to administer the gospel to all men.

The biggest issue with "dispensationalism" isn't the past, it's the unbiblical claim that there will be a different means of salvation or a different dispensation in the end times, reserved for ethnic Jews.

teachings.title: Predestination and free will
teachings.summary: Says people mix up free will and predestination from false definitions, and that the destination of adoption was predetermined for all who enter in through Christ.
teachings.text:
But that's not what predestination is. 

The destination of adoption was predetermined for all who enter in through Christ, not predetermining which people would step through the doorway.

People get really caught up in free will vs predestination, because they begin with fundamentally false premises, and wrong definitions of terms.

teachings.title: No Mid-Acts dispensation
teachings.summary: Uses Acts 15:8-11 to show Peter and Paul preached the same gospel, and that all men from Adam through today have been saved by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
**Acts 15:8-11**
*And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the *Lord* Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.*

"Mid-Acts" Dispensationalism holds that by chapter 15, a different gospel is made known unto Gentiles, that the Jews keeping the law of Moses still, despite believing, were under a dispensation of the law still. That the Gospel of Grace was given to Paul to preach to the Gentiles. That these verses "prove it."

A plain reading of the text shows that Peter held the same Gospel of Grace, and that it is not given by works of the law, but by the grace of the LORD (made distinct in the text, using the same capitalized distinction reserved for YHWH. A divine Lord, absolute authority, Greek is *Kyrios*).

*We believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they*. This sentence refutes any of the idea that Jews had a different gospel or standard, or that Peter's preaching to the circumcision was any different than Paul's ministry to the Gentiles. 

There is no "Mid-Acts Dispensation." All men, from Adam through today have been saved by the grace of God the Father, through faith in His deliverance, which is by His Son, Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Saved by His death, burial and resurrection
teachings.summary: Quotes John 3:16-18 and says one who does not trust the death, burial and resurrection of Christ is not saved, since the gift is the point of His sacrifice.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him **should not perish**, **but have everlasting life.** For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned**: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

If you don't believe that your sins are all forgiven, that you have eternal life, that Jesus died for your sins, past, present and future, so that you may have eternal life, you aren't saved. 

OSAS is just shorthand for the gift promised by the grace of God, paid for by the Son and sealed by the Spirit. Never perishing, everlasting life, not condemned. This is an essential part of what you're believing on Jesus *for.*

If you don't know for sure you have eternal life, you don't know the gospel and you aren't saved. 

**1 Corinthians 15:1-2**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and **wherein ye stand**; **By which also ye are saved,** if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, **unless ye have believed in vain.***

If you don't believe that you stand and are saved by the death, burial and resurrection of Christ Jesus, as foretold in scripture and witnessed by many, you aren't saved. 

The gift is the point of Jesus' sacrifice. It's what you receive when you trust in Him. 

If you don't know what He did it for, you don't know why you need it, or what the purpose of it even was.

teachings.title: Blasphemy against the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: Quotes Matthew 12:31-32 and Mark 3:28-29 and notes that no one may claim blaspheming the Holy Spirit is forgivable.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 12:31-32**
*Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men. And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.*

**Mark 3:28-29**
*Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation*.

Let God be true, and every man a liar. Beware false prophets who contradict the clear and undeniable word of God.

While I have seen people debate what it means to blaspheme the Holy Spirit, I have never seen anyone, even the most dishonest and despicable false teacher, ever directly contradict Jesus and claim that it's actually totally forgivable to blaspheme the Holy Spirit. 

Mark and avoid. That person is 100% not saved and can't discern the spiritual things of God.

teachings.title: Hope for the dead and the true gospel
teachings.summary: Says many have a false hope that anyone who acknowledged God was saved, and that the answer is soul winning and preaching the whole word to the living.
teachings.text:
Between the Pope, John MacArthur and Ozzy dying, it's really exposed how vacant and lost most people's understanding of salvation is.

People believe all manner of nonsense and vain beliefs, the primary one being that if someone vaguely acknowledged God in some way, or mentioned Jesus, that they were likely saved. 

Of course the same people promoting this desperate false hope will turn to the living and say "You can't just say a prayer and be saved!" Mock "easy believism," and "once saved, always saved." 

"You can't be saved and live however you want!" 

"We are saved by faith....BUT...."

They will promote false teachers and men who profess another gospel, or worse, unregenerate celebrities who outright tell you they believe some unbiblical nonsense about "a higher power," and get angry when we point to scripture and the specific plan of salvation given to show that we can pretty much guarantee these people died in their sins and went to Hell. 

"Only God can judge! You don't know what's in their hearts!" 

God told us His judgement, and out of the abundance of their hearts, they spoke. We don't condemn them, their own words do. 

**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

"Maybe God will be merciful to them!" He was when He sent His only begotten Son to die for us. 

"Maybe they repented on their death bed!" Maybe, but if they didn't hear Moses and the prophets and the gospels and the preachers their whole life, they probably won't. 

This is why we go soul-winning. This is why we preach the whole word, in season and out. 

Hopes and prayers that someone gets right at the last moment, or wishing someone be saved after they die, are all vanity. 

There is the gospel, preached by the saved to the lost, and the Spirit moving with their spirit, that they repent towards the gospel of grace and reconciliation in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: When Paul was saved
teachings.summary: Says Paul was not saved on the road to Damascus but in Damascus when he called on the Lord after Ananias taught him the gospel, and that no one is saved without hearing the word preached.
teachings.text:
Below is an audio sermon on Paul's conversion. I've heard many dispensationalists claim that the 144,000 of the book of Revelation are actually modern Jews, who unbeknownst to them carry the exact genetics of the 12 tribes mentioned, and they are given salvation in some sort of Calvinist way "Similar to Paul on the road to Damascus." 

Paul did not get saved when he was blinded and heard the voice of Christ. Paul was saved in Damascus 3 days later when he called upon the name of the Lord after being instructed in the gospel by Ananias. 

Every saved person has another saved person who acted as their minister of the Gospel of reconciliation to bring them to Christ. Nobody is given salvation without hearing the word preached and believing what they heard.

teachings.title: The laborers in the vineyard and lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Answers lordship and repent-of-your-sin teachers with Matthew 20, saying the saved are chastened by God but receive grace as the late laborers did.
teachings.text:
Lordshippers and repent-of-your-sinners are hypocritical vipers. 

They just want to judge other people. They want to rate their own righteousness by finding others who aren't living up to whatever arbitrary standards they have set. 

And it's always vague because they need to have wiggle room for their own sin. " You got to give your life to Christ!" What does that mean? Well it depends on when you ask them. 

"You have to repent of your sin and change your life!" What does that mean? Depends on when you ask them. 

It has to be vague and loaded with ambiguity and subjective judgment because they always have to have a way to justify their own sin. They always need to have someone else they can look down on. 

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees. HYPOCRITES!

People who think this way also neglect to understand that we who are saved are chastened by God, who scourges every son he receives. 

"You can't just live however you want!" is code for "It isn't fair that you get paid a penny for showing up at the end, when I worked all day!" 

**Matthew 20:1-15**
*For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

2 And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

3 And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,

4 And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.

5 Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.

6 And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?

7 They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.

8 So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

9 And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.

10 But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny.

11 And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house,

12 Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

13 But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?

14 Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.

15 Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?*

teachings.title: Only the blood atones
teachings.summary: Says turning over a new leaf, baptism, joining a church or good deeds cannot satisfy the price of sin, and that only Christ's blood offered on the mercy seat propitiates, with Hebrews 9 quoted.
teachings.text:
Turning your life around, repenting of sin, joining a church, getting water baptized, making Jesus the Lord of your life, seeing real change, sacraments and good deeds... None of these things satisfy the price of sin. 

Only the blood of a holy God offered in our place and sprinkled on the mercy seat can atone for our sin and justify us before God. That is the only propitiation. The blood is for the heavenly Father.

**Hebrews 9:11-26** 
*But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, **but by his own blood** he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.

It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others; For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.*

**Romans 3:25**
*Whom God hath set forth to be a **propitiation** **through faith in his blood**, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God*

teachings.title: The gospel is not a call to discipleship
teachings.summary: Says the gospel Jesus proclaimed is repentance unto belief and calling on the Lord for eternal life by His blood, not a requirement of submissive obedience.
teachings.text:
This is not the gospel that Jesus proclaimed. It is a decision, repentance unto belief. A prayer, calling upon the name of the Lord. It was not a "call to discipleship" or a requirement for "submissive obedience." 

It is eternal life and forgiveness of sins by the blood of Christ Jesus, because we aren't capable of submissive obedience or sufficient discipleship to ever pay any of the wages of sin. Our filthy rags aren't what the Lord wants. Faith is. 

John MacArthur's heresy is hypocrisy.

teachings.title: The election of grace
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 11:5-6 and Galatians 3 that election is of grace, and that salvation for the Jews as Abraham's seed makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
Every damnable heresy in "professing Christianity" is based on rejecting the election of grace. They make grace contingent on merit, making grace no more grace. 

**Romans 11:5-6**
*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

Grace is the undeserved and unmerited favor of God. 

Here in Romans, Paul is writing to explain why physical Israel, Jews after the flesh, are not elect. That their blood relation to Abraham cannot save them. That it is by the election of grace man is saved. Continuing in verse 7;

*What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.*

Which election? The election of Grace. And so, the heresy of dispensationalism fails when the scriptures are searched to see if it is so. And the damnable heresy of hyperdispensationalism is undone by the doctrine of grace. 

**Galatians 3:16**, **26-29**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

*For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.* *For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The Jews being saved for being the seed of Abraham makes grace no more grace.

**Romans 9:6-8**
*Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.*

teachings.title: Same gospel for Jews and Gentiles, and idols
teachings.summary: Shows from Acts 15:11 that the apostles believed they were saved by the same grace as the Gentiles, and from Acts 19 that early Christians opposed idols in worship.
teachings.text:
*Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

**But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.***

The heresy that Paul taught a different gospel to Gentiles than the Apostles taught the Jews relies on a false interpretation of **Acts 15**. But it is made clear here in **Acts 15:11** that the Apostles in Jerusalem believed they were saved by the same grace as the Gentiles. By the Lord Jesus Christ.

**Acts 19:24-28** 
*For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen; Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth. Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth. And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.*

Catholics, particularly Orthodox, all insist that graven images and "icons" were always part of worship for Christians, from the days of the Apostles. Obviously false, as Idolatry was consistently prohibited by God's commandments, and by the Apostles and Epistles, saying to flee idols and not to eat meats offered to them. 

But to really reinforce this idea, we have the story in **Acts 19** of the silversmith, Demetrius and the cause he's tired up against the disciples of Christ in Ephesus. Because the Christian teaching was against images in worship, Demetrius was able to argue their craft was in jeopardy. That they'd go bankrupt if people no longer required idols made of hands. 

If early Christianity only taught against images of false gods, and not the entire practice itself, their trade would not be unprofitable. Instead of Diana they could make a living with crucifixes and statues of the passed saints. 

It's just another example of how foolish these appeals to vain tradition are in light of the Bible.

teachings.title: The doctrine of baptisms
teachings.summary: Reads Hebrews 6, Mark 1, John 20 and Acts 2 to explain that there are three baptisms in the New Testament: John's and the believer's by water, and the Spirit's by God.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:1-3**
*Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, Of the **doctrine of baptisms**, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. And this will we do, if God permit.*

The doctrine of baptisms, plural, is one of the "milk of the word" doctrines according to Paul. Along with the understanding of salvation in Christ, repentance from dead works (both ceremonial and self-righteous) and of faith towards God (biblical repentance), laying on of hands as a means of ordination and ministry, the resurrection at the day of the Lord, the rapture and the eternal judgment of Christ, the judge of the quick (we who are saved, at His judgment seat) and the dead (the damned, cast into the lake of fire at the Great White Throne).

Each one is prone to misunderstanding and abuse and heresy, despite them being the foundational doctrines of the faith. If we are to grow as Christians we need this milk to be understood, that we may go on to the meat of the word. 

There are three main baptisms mentioned in the New Testament. Two water and one fire. All significant. 

First, to define the word, baptism means to be immersed, to become part of, to join with. It does not mean to wash or get wet. Jesus uses the term to mean to be part of His suffering. To join in it. To be immersed:

**Matthew 20:22 **
*But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able*.

This understanding of the word is why Baptists fully submerge believers, in the likeness of His death, burial and resurrection. Sprinkling and pouring are a taste of a thing, baptism is to become one with it.

Baptism then to be fully joined to something, we see then there are more than one method or reason, and of what one is joining and becoming part of. 

While Jesus uses the term to mean partaking in the unique suffering, death and Hell He would experience, in **Matthew 20:22**, there are 3 other Baptisms man could partake in mentioned in the Bible. 

This first is the Baptism of John. The baptism unto repentance. 

**Matthew 3:1-6**
*In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.*

John as prophet was leading all who would hear to make their hearts ready for the Christ Who would come, to understand that the prophesied Kingdom of Heaven was near. They believed the word of God and were baptized in the water of the Jordan. But they did not know Who would be the Christ, let alone what Jesus would do to deliver them. 

They had the scriptures John preached to them, and the same faith of other Old Testament saints of deliverance. But the specifics were not clear, and faith in Christ to come was given from the word alone. 

They were led to repentance from dead works and faith towards God, but received not the sign of Jonas, nor the holy Spirit. This is an important point to keep in mind. They confessed sins, admitting they needed salvation and placed their trust alone in Him without ever seeing Jesus. But their hearts were prepared to receive Him. The paths made straight. The King's Highway laid.

**Mark 1:1-11**
*And John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey; And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose. **I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost**. And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan. And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.*

John the Baptist preached that the Christ he was preparing the way for was not only greater than he, but that He would baptize believers with the holy Ghost the way John has with water. 

Matthew 3:11 
*I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: **he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:** Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.*

Jesus is the first water baptism that the holy Ghost was involved with. The only one up and until after the resurrection. But John speaking the word of God promised they would be baptized by the holy Ghost, by the Spirit, as with fire. Signifying there was another baptism than his.

*I indeed baptize you with water **unto** repentance...*

Unto is another word with specific meaning. As the scripture uses it, unto means move towards till joined or completed, the state of going to a specific end, or being made part of that end. 

John's baptism is repeatedly called the baptism UNTO repentance. For the forgiveness of sins. These people were before Christ, in the old covenant, without the Spirit, only faith in a promise yet to be fulfilled. They were baptized unto repentance, in the lifetime of Jesus that when He came, they knew Him. 

**John 1:40-41**
*One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother. He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.*

**Luke 7:17-23**
*And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about. And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight. Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached. And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.*

Unlike the prostyles of the Pharisees and Sadducees, who were not meet for repentance. Who were being made twofold more the child of Hell by their vain traditions, the disciples of John had repented to believe the Christ was imminent. Even if there was doubts and wonder, they sought after Christ in Whom all their faith layed. 

**John 11:25-27 **
*Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.*

They had been baptized with the baptism UNTO repentance. To the faith in something yet to come. In someone yet to prove they were the anointed of God. Jesus before the death, burial and resurrection. Without the Spirit yet sent to them. Without the baptism of fire.

**John 20:20-22**
*And when he had so said, he shewed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord. Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you. And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost*.

The disciples and Apostles gathered in the great room after Jesus' death. There He revealed Himself to them, and it was there that He breathed the Spirit, the Holy Ghost upon them. The baptism of the Spirit of God He had promised them. 

**John 3:5-6**
*Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.*

They were born again in the Spirit, quickened, regenerated and sealed unto redemption. This is a separate occurrence from the gifts of the holy Ghost that came as tongues of fire upon them at Pentecost. 

**Acts 1:4-8 **
*And, being assembled together with them, commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he, ye have heard of me. **For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost** not many days hence. When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. **But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you**: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.*

It was during this time the resurrected Jesus taught them of yet another water baptism, in the name of the Father, Son and holy Spirit.

**Matthew 28:18-20**
*And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, **baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost**: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. Amen.*

The baptism of John was, we have to assume, was in the name of the Lord. Jehovah God. People were saved by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord since the sons of Seth. The baptism of the holy Ghost, the Spirit of regeneration and forgiveness of sins, is in the name of Jesus. 

But the new criteria for the ordinance of water baptism for believers was in the name of the Godhead itself, Father, Son and Ghost.

**Acts 2:38 **
*Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost*.

Peter preaching at Pentecost lays out all the ways the Jews gathered there had failed to recognize Christ among them, killed their Saviour and not believing the promise of God which all the prophets gave witness. He calls on them to change their minds, believing and in Jesus' name, be baptized by the holy Spirit for the remission of sins.

He isn't leading them to water. He isn't ignoring Christ's great commission to water baptize in the name of the Father, Son and holy Ghost. He is talking about being born again in the Spirit, baptized by fire.

**Acts 8:34-39 **
*And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus. And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized? And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.*

Here, we see how salvation is by faith, hearing the word of God. Calling upon the name of Christ Jesus, and this is required before water baptism. Believers baptism in the name of the Trinity is the only water baptism of the New Testament. And it is different from the baptism of John unto repentance. 

**Acts 19:1-7**
*And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples, He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost. And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus. When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied. And all the men were about twelve.*

First, Paul differentiates John's baptism from what he is preaching to them. John baptized **unto** **repentance** *that they should believe on Him which should come after him. *

But hearing the gospel, the truth that Jesus is the Christ, and had come, Paul asks if they'd been baptized by the holy Spirit.

In my opinion, these men believed God and it was counted for righteousness. Had they died before this moment, I believe they were saved. Yet they were lacking the truth of Jesus and the baptism of the holy Spirit that was now available to them. 

Note that it is **after** they call upon the name of Christ and are baptized by the Spirit that Paul then lays hands upon them, ordaining them to ministry with the gifts of the holy Ghost. 

These gifts were given the first generation of believers, to be a sign and witness, absent the completion and availability of the scriptures. Before the Bible was complete and available. This is the difference between what happened on the great room when Jesus breathed in the gathered disciples, and the gifts of the Ghost that came on Pentecost. 

One is a baptism of regeneration and forgiveness which all believers receive, the other a special gifting of supernatural abilities not given to all who are saved.

And so, in my opinion, there are 3 primary baptisms in the New Testament. Two by water, acts of man to give testimony of their faith, and one by God, of fire, given by the Spirit upon repentance towards that faith. 

John's was for repentance to come. The Spirit, upon repentance. Believers baptism for those to whom repentance and Spiritual baptism had already occurred. 

The Apostle Peter, writing to the saints about the salvation from mockers and scoffers, as Noah was saved by the flood from those disobedient who jeered at his faith, compares the ordinance of believers baptism to the deluge:

**1 Peter 3:21 **
*The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ*

He says, it isn't the means of putting away the filth of the flesh, of how we are cleaned from sin, but **an answer** of a good conscience, received already by the resurrection of Jesus Christ. By faith in His being risen from the dead. By the baptism of the Spirit, inwardly, that seals us and quickens us and is the earnest payment, a promise for redemption in the last days giving us a clean conscience that we may be baptized in the name of the Father, Son and holy Spirit without fear. Knowing our sins are forgiven. Being adopted as sons of God.

That's a lot of Bible. I don't claim to know definitively that this is all there is to understand about the doctrines of baptisms, but it occurs to me that the Bible teaches this. I would ask that Christians of good faith spend the time to read it and search the scriptures to see if it is so. And enter the new year with the joy of the Spirit, having been baptized by fire into the Kingdom of Heaven.

teachings.title: Romans 3 against works salvation
teachings.summary: Walks through Romans 3 to show that no flesh is justified by the deeds of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ.
teachings.text:
A key passage teaching against the damnable heresy of works salvation comes in **Romans 3**, where Paul writes;

*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God...**Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.**

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: **For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:** Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus...Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. **Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.***

Of course, this passage clearly states that by works of the law, no flesh shall be justified. It is undeniable.

But a common argument against the scripture that they will use is that "works of the law" refers only to the ceremonial law of the Old Testament. The Levitical laws and ordinances, sacrifices and washings done away with in the New Testament. *
*
Fortunately, we have the full context, established in the previous chapter.

**Romans 2:14-15** 
*For when the **Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves**: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)*

Paul, speaking of the Gentiles, says they do by nature the things contained in the law. That they have the works of the law written in their hearts, even in their conscience. 

Is Paul saying the Gentiles are keeping feasts and sabbaths and not mixing fabrics "by nature?" That the sacrifices and offerings and other carnal ordinances of the Levitical ceremony is written in their hearts? 

Of course not. That's foolishness. 

The law is the knowledge of sin. A schoolmaster to lead us to repentance, that we accept Christ as our savior. 

Paul clearly means the commandments and civil ordinances that make up the law of God when he writes that no flesh shall be justified by the deeds of the law. By works. 

For sin is the transgression of the law.

God is not the author of confusion. Let God be true and every man a liar. 

We conclude that no flesh shall be justified by the deeds of the law, but by faith. Believing on Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Repent-of-your-sins is a false gospel
teachings.summary: Notes the inconsistency of KJV-only believers who claim grace alone through faith alone yet teach repent-of-your-sins and Lordship salvation.
teachings.text:
It is amazing to me that there are supposed KJVOists, who claim salvation is by grace alone through faith alone, and yet teach the false gospel of "repent-of-your-sins" which comes from satanic perversions.

Of course these same vipers will simultaneously denounce John MacArthur for Calvinism, while embracing his false "Lordship salvation" gospel.

teachings.title: Baptism does not save in 1 Peter 3
teachings.summary: Shows the order of operations in 1 Peter 3 and says those who see baptism as a means of grace are spiritually blinded to it.
teachings.text:
It always amazes me when a Protestant tries to use this passage to justify baptizing babies, or to say that it is a "means of Grace," That somehow the water water creates the ability for someone to believe. 

And when you show them this order of operations and break it down for them, they simply cannot understand it. They see baptism saves and call it a day. 

The only thing that can explain their inability to simply read the passage and follow along the order of operations is that they are spiritually blinded. They have a supernatural blindness to the truth

teachings.title: You can know you have eternal life
teachings.summary: Sets Romans 3 beside a gospel message for anyone hoping to be good enough for Heaven, offering eternal life as a free gift through faith in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Romans 3:10-20**
*as it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, There is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; There is none that doeth good, no, not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre; With their tongues they have used deceit; The poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: Their feet are swift to shed blood: Destruction and misery are in their ways: And the way of peace have they not known: There is no fear of God before their eyes. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

Donald Trump's going to Hell, but you don't have to! The Bible tells us that we can know, today, that we have eternal life. A free gift given by the grace of the Father through faith on His Son, Christ Jesus.

If you aren't sure that you're saved, if you are like Trump and are hoping on being good to get to Heaven, please take a few minutes to hear this message of the Gospel. The Bible way to Heaven

teachings.title: Look and live: the brazen serpent and John 3
teachings.summary: Shows from John 3 that, like Israel looking at the serpent, anyone who believes is saved without turning from sins or doing anything but looking and living, and will be raised on the last day.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**
***And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life**. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life**. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.***

When Moses lifted up the serpent, all who looked upon it were saved from the venom of the fiery serpents. All who looked and believed were healed. They did not have to turn from their sin. They did not have to make the serpent the Lord of their lives. They did not have to do anything but look and live. 

Jesus Christ tells us that this is a figure of the salvation that He came to bring the world, that through Him man is saved. That God the Father so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son. And all who BELIEVE, that is trust that Jesus died for them and nothing else, are justified. Given eternal life. 

As Jesus says again in **John 6:37-40**

*All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that **every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.***

Not might. Not if they deserve it. Not if they have repented enough to please some man or group of men, but that see Jesus and believe, and they have eternal life and shall in no ways be cast out. Because the Father's will is that all who look to Christ, raised upon the cross and believe that was for our sin, have eternal life. Will be raised on the last day. 

If you are trusting in anything else but Christ on the cross, and the hope of the promise of resurrection of which He was the first fruit, repent. Think again. And if you don't believe that gift is eternal, that Jesus WILL raise you up on that last day, that your works are needed to keep you in grace, repent. Think again. All who believe are not condemned. All who believe HAVE eternal life in Christ. All who believe WILL be raised on the last day. Amen

teachings.title: Salvation is by Christ's righteousness
teachings.summary: Warns against teaching that salvation depends on our own righteousness and reminds that all fall short of the glory of God.
teachings.text:
Too many false teachers are in the world teaching that our salvation is contingent on our ability to be righteous rather than by Christ's righteousness. Denying eternal life. Teaching salvation can be lost if we aren't "good enough." 

News flash, you aren't good enough. No one is. We all fall short of the glory of God.

teachings.title: Repent and be baptized in Acts 2:38
teachings.summary: Explains that repent in Acts 2 means to think better of unbelief in Jesus as the Christ, and that baptism follows remission of sins rather than bringing it.
teachings.text:
How baby baptizers read **1 Peter 3**

When Peter is preaching to the crowd at Pentecost, and many Jews who were there were convicted of the heart and asked "*Men and brethren, what shall we do?*" Peter responds, "*Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost*."

This has been abused by many false teachers, both who say that repent here means to turn from sin, and that say water baptism is how our sins are forgiven. 

The repenters argument is foolish and has no basis in the text. Peter clearly explained their failure to recognize Jesus was Christ, and so he is saying they need to repent, to think better of that and believe.

The baptizers argument has more weight. But it comes from not understanding the meaning of the word "for" in this usage, and placing the emphasis on the baptism itself, rather than the cause of remission. 

"For" in this usage is "because of," Jesus Christ the reason.

Because of that repentance, in Christ's name they received the remission of sins, and for that reason they should be baptized.

teachings.title: James 2:17 used against the gospel
teachings.summary: Observes that those who use James 2:17 against the gospel hold to a self-righteous zeal not according to knowledge and are very hard to reach.
teachings.text:
When someone pulls out **James 2:17** as a Uno reverse card against the Gospel, they have admitted they aren't saved, and it is nearly impossible to get them to budge from their self-righteous position.

*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.*

They seek to establish their own righteousness, and so they oppose themselves. There are none righteous. Our only righteousness is imputed of Christ. 

*Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

I have never managed to free a person who has stumbled and been snared by **James 2:17**. All the scripture in the world, and they cannot see.

teachings.title: Doctrine in Psalm 119
teachings.summary: Points out that two verses of Psalm 119 hold salvation by the word, confession with the mouth, being taught His precepts and eternal security.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 119:107-109**
*I am afflicted very much: **quicken me, O Lord, according unto thy word.** Accept, I beseech thee, **the freewill offerings of my mouth,** O Lord, and teach me thy judgments. **My soul is continually in my hand: yet do I not forget thy law.***

The Psalms are dripping with doctrine.
