Here, in just two verses of the longest (and best IMO) Psalm, you have salvation by the word of God, calling on Him to quicken our spirit as He has promised in His word, the confession with his mouth, the promise to teach us His precepts and judgments. Eternal security. And the understanding that despite our salvation, we still do not forget the law.

teachings.title: Palm Sunday and the cry of the stones
teachings.summary: Reflects on Luke 19 and the multitude praising the King, noting that some who cheered Him were calling for His crucifixion days later.
teachings.text:
**Luke 19:37-40**
*And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen; Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest. And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples. And he answered and said unto them, **I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.***

That verse stirs my soul. That this dead sinner became a lively stone, crying out to the Lord. Amen.

Imagine on Palm Sunday (I think Palm Saturday, but who's counting?) making the same mistake as the Pharisses, telling Jesus that the cries of the people, that *He is the King that cometh in the name of the Lord* was offensive.

Some that cheered Jesus that day were calling for Him to be crucified a few days later. 

Most of the people tweeting "Christ is King" aren't saved. 

*What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.*

 *I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.*

Christ is King.

teachings.title: John 5:24 is the gospel
teachings.summary: Holds that justification is only by the imputed righteousness of Christ through faith, not works, from John 5:24.
teachings.text:
**John 5:24** 
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

This is the Gospel. There are no other way to justification before God but by the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. Who died for the sins of the whole world, a propitiation for sins, especially for those that believe. Sealed unto redemption by the Spirit. Predestinated to be adopted into the promise in Christ, by faith. Whosoever believes this, not works, not of themselves, not by any other means but the gracious offer of God the Father, though the Son, to all who believe.

teachings.title: John 3:16 is the whole gospel
teachings.summary: Walks through Jesus teaching Nicodemus and urges testing any doctrine against John 3:16, since anything that violates it is a false gospel.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life**. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life**. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned**: **but** **he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.***

This set of verses contain everything anyone needs to know regarding salvation, Biblical repentance in the context of salvation. The clearest explanation of the gospel found in scripture. 

He that believes *not* is condemned. 

He that believes is not condemned.

Repent and believe; Turn from non-believer to believer. That is the Gospel.

*Sirs, what must I do to be saved? ... And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved*.

The same Gospel Jesus preached is given by Paul. 

Not believing that God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son is what makes a man perish. Believing that He did, and that His Son is Christ Jesus, gives a man eternal life. 

This is the choice. This is the repentance. This is the good news. That is the God, that is His Son. The gift is eternal. Everlasting.

It's an amazing thing, in **John 3** You have one of the head religious leaders of the Jews, Nicodemus, sitting down with the Son of God, and Jesus teaches him the Gospel. We are allowed to witness this. Think about it. Think about how amazing that is. What a blessing it is.

Nicodemus who is a teacher of the people, well versed in the law, one of the highest ranking Pharisees, rich, powerful, sitting down being instructed by the Lord. And missing it.

*If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?
*
We have the preserved word of God, spoken to man, and he received it not. 

And how many people today are like Nicodemus? And cannot read this in all and wonder and take it as God's word that this is how you are saved. That there's nothing more to it than this simple truth.

If someone cannot agree that the plain reading of **John 3:16** is the entire Gospel, they aren't saved. 

*For **God** so **loved** **the world**, that **he** gave **his only begotten Son**, that **whosoever** **believeth in him** should **not** perish, **but have** ***everlasting* life.***

That's it. That's the entire good news of the living God by His grace, His **love** for the entire world, not some. Not few. And for that love, The Father gave His Son as a gift. Not to some. But to  **whosoever**, without caveat or conditions except one, **that believes**. Believe means trust to be true. To have faith in. A secure knowledge. A lively hope. It doesn't mean anything more than that. He gave a gift of His Son to the whole world that if they believe in Him, they won't perish. They will never die. They **have** everlasting life. That means eternal. Never ending. 

This is not some esoteric rendition where the "God" means a mode of Jesus, not a Father sacrificing His son. Or of a Jesus that is not divine. Not where "the world" and "whosoever" don't mean "the world" and "whosoever." Where "believein Him" actually means doing works and trusting in yourself, or a denomination, or rituals and sacraments. Where "perish" isn't wrath and Hell. Where "have" means "will have" or "used to have" "or could get" or "could lose." Where "eternal" doesn't mean eternal.

All of those things, as well as the addition of things and concepts not present in this or the verses that immediately follow them, culminating 20 verses later, God summarizing it once again in **John 3:36**;

*He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

That's it. If you don't believe this is the sum total of the Gospel, the theology of salvation, you need to repent, and believe. Or the wrath of God abides on you.

Pro tip: When someone is bringing doctrine to you that sounds ok or a little sus, and you're just not sure if it's right or not, compare it to **John 3:16**. 

If it violates any of it, you know immediately it's a false gospel. 

There are some doctrines you have to get elsewhere, most actually. But salvation, the most important one, can be taught straight from **John 3:15-18** and **3:36**.

(Go ahead and try it in the comments. Think of a damnable heresy you've heard and see where it violates **John 3:16)**

teachings.title: Grace and love in human relationships
teachings.summary: Explains that modern culture's trouble with relationships comes from rejecting the free gift of God's grace, and shows from Romans 8 and 1 John 4 that Christ's love is what heals and teaches us to love.
teachings.text:
The foundational problem with modern culture when it comes to human relationships, is that we've abandoned Christ, and so the knowledge and understanding that we are saved by God's grace, through faith, that is trust, in His promise. 

People reject that free gift, offered up front by God, paid for by Jesus. Grace being the unmerited and undeserving favor of God. His love shown by being for our best interest, Jesus dying for us while we were yet sinners. A gift of love. Charity. 

They do this for a variety of reasons, but it mostly comes down to seeing love as transactional. 

They may think they aren't worthy of His grace; an oxymoron. They may think they can earn it on their own, and so they deserve His grace; pride. They may not be willing to trust that which they cannot see, just by the word of God. Trust issues and defensive behavior created through trauma. 

They may have been raised in a toxic household where parents doled out approval transactionally. They may have been raised in a church that teaches you have to work for salvation. They may have been poisoned by culture, as the video posted here suggests. 

But it is directly a result of people and our culture losing the meekness and humility that comes from accepting the gospel, and the grace and charity that follows when you realize what true love is. 

**1 John 4:10**
*Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins*.

**Romans 8:35-37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

It is God's love: The Father so loving the world that *He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.*... *That God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us...*That Jesus so loved us, He died for us...*Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends...For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die*... *For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.*...*So I will be with thee: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee...and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me...And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.*

**Zephaniah 3:17 **
*The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.*

It is by this love that we are healed. This is how the brokenhearted are comforted. This is how we learn to live God with all our hearts and to love our neighbor as ourselves. This is how a husband learns to love his wife as his own flesh. And how a wife learns to submit to her husband. And how a child learns to honor his parents. 

It is how we as saved believers develop charity. 

**1 Corinthians 13:4-7**
*Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.*

Having grace and mercy for others, comes from God's grace and mercy on us. His love for us is magnified through us towards others. 

**James 1:27 **
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

This is the purpose of our salvation. These are the works we are asked to do. To love one another. To esteem others more than ourselves. To put their profit above our own. 

**Philippians 2:3-4**
*Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.*

If you are saved by the love of God, then show His love to others. Have grace. Understanding that their condition isn't any different than yours. That it is only by the grace of God you're in a better spot than they appear to be. Showing them the love you'd want shown unto you.

**Proverbs 11:4**
*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.*

teachings.title: Titus 2 and 3: grace teaches good works
teachings.summary: Strings together verses from Titus 2 and 3 to show that grace teaches us to live godly and that believers need to be reminded to maintain good works.
teachings.text:
***For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men**, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; **Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works**. These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. But after that **the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour**; That **being justified by his grace**, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that **they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men**.*

Amen

Note that this series of verses from **Titus** 2 and 3 debunks Calvanism, works-based false salvation, and shows that good works are not automatic, but that we need to be exhorted and reminded that they are good and profitable to do.

teachings.title: The children are free: the tribute money
teachings.summary: Sees in Matthew 17:24-27 a picture of the free gift of salvation without works, since the King's children do not pay tribute.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 17:24-27**
*And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received tribute money came to Peter, and said, Doth not your master pay tribute? He saith, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? Peter saith unto him, Of strangers. Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free.*

What a wonderful example of the free gift of salvation, without works. The children are free. They don't pay tribute to the King. We are adopted into the Kingdom as heirs in Christ. We don't pay a thing.

teachings.title: The Ethiopian eunuch: a textbook salvation
teachings.summary: Reads the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8 as salvation by hearing the word and believing Jesus is the risen Christ, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
It still stuns me that there are people who read the story of the Ethiopian eunuch, a textbook salvation; from hearing the word of God from a saved believer, to accepting that Jesus was that promised Christ, who takes away the sins of the world. And then getting baptized, already saved, as a believer, and add things to it of their own. 

It's God's word, His testament, that saves. Accepting His word as true. That Jesus is the Risen Christ, and by His blood we are saved. Just as He promised. Plus or minus nothing.

teachings.title: "Naughty or nice?" and the gift of grace
teachings.summary: Contrasts the works-based Santa Claus idea of earned gifts with God's gift of salvation, freely given by grace.
teachings.text:
"Naughty or nice?" 

There is none nice. No not one. There is none that isn't naughty. 

"Santa Claus" teaches a false, works-based doctrine. That gifts have to be "earned" by good behavior. But if you have to earn something, it is not a gift. 

But the gifts of God are by His grace, undeserved, given freely of love by His mercy:

*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus*

Make sure your children know that whatever gifts you decide to bless them with, that it is done freely, out of love unfeigned. Unconditional. 

Not by some creepy old elf judging their worth.

teachings.title: The gospel is not 200 years old
teachings.summary: Traces the same salvation by faith in the sacrifice of the Lamb from Adam and Eve, Abel and Cain, and Enos in Genesis 4:26 to answer the claim that the gospel is new.
teachings.text:
There is a resurgence of unsaved people using the false argument that the Gospel by which we are saved is "only 200 years old." Many heresies come in cycles. You will see the same one suddenly pop-up from multiple people, and it is currently the trending heresy I am witnessing. 

The idea that the same salvation of Genesis is "new," is absurd. 

Adam and Eve, having sinned, sought to cover themselves with figleaves they sowed themselves. God corrected them and showed them, covering their sins with the lamb skins He provided, the blood shed representing Christ's, the redemption by faith. 

Righteous Abel believed God and He pleased the Lord. Cain sought to offer his own works and God rebuked him. And Cain in his pride became the first reorobate. 

**Genesis 4:26**
*And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

This is the same Gospel as we preach today. Faith in the sacrifice God offered for us. Calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation. Justified in the blood. Covered by the snow white wool of the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. 

Amen.

teachings.title: Trusting anything but the finished work of Christ
teachings.summary: States that anyone trusting works, rites or turning from sin to be saved is perishing, and gives the gospel of grace by which whosoever believes on the Son is saved, plus nothing, minus nothing.
teachings.text:
If you are trusting in anything other than the finished work of Christ to save you from Hell and death, if you believe that your works play a role in justification before God at the judgment, if you are trusting in traditions, rites, your sacrifices, prayers to saints, carnal ordinances and sacraments, doing good works or turning from your sins to save you, you are assuredly perishing. You must repent towards the Gospel of grace and reconciliation.

The Bible is clear. 

The only salvation is by grace of God, the unmerited favor He extends to all, that whosoever believes on His Son, who was made flesh, lived a sinless life, died for our transgressions, suffered in our place, and rose again to life after 3 days and nights, the propitiation for our sin, and ascended into glory, the first fruits of the promise of eternal life that all believers share. Period. 

Plus nothing. Minus nothing.

teachings.title: Easy believism and the simple gospel of grace
teachings.summary: Answers those who mock the simple gospel as easy believism, saying they add burdens to what Christ paid in full, and calls for repentance toward the gospel of grace and reconciliation.
teachings.text:
People who use the term "easy believism" to derisively mock the simple Gospel of grace and reconciliation, are trying to keep men under the yoke of bondage. They deny that Jesus paid it all. They add burdens grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders. 

If you aren't sure you have eternal life, if you don't know for certain you have peace with God, if you are counting on your own ability to turn from sin, obey commandments or keep traditions of men, ordinances and sacraments to be saved, repent towards the Gospel of God. The truth that in Christ Jesus, all is forgiven. It doesn't seem easy to just believe, but that is the only way to heaven. 

**Galatians 2:16-21**
*knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid. For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor. For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God. I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me. I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.*

teachings.title: The clearest presentation of the gospel in John 3
teachings.summary: Reads John 3 as the clearest gospel from Jesus: all are condemned by sin, and whosoever believes on the Son has everlasting life, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
**John 3***
14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

17 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
...
33 He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true.

34 For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him.

35 The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

36 He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.
...

34 For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him.

35 The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

36 He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him*.

This is the clearest presentation of the Gospel of God, given by Jesus and note all the elements contained in it. That we are condemned by sin. But God so loved the world, that's everyone in it, that whosoever shall believe, that is trust and have faith in Christ Jesus, not our works or our genealogy or our ability to turn from sin, but faith alone, has eternal life and shall not perish. 

This is what we believe to be saved. 

If you don't accept any element of this or add something to it, you deny the record and aren't saved. You are perishing.

teachings.title: Justified by the faith of Christ, not the works of the law
teachings.summary: Answers the claim that works of the law means only ceremonial law, using Galatians 2 and Romans 4, and sets Christ's once-for-all sacrifice in Hebrews 10 against Rome's daily sacrifice.
teachings.text:
**Galatians 2:16-21 **
K*nowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, **but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ**, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified*.

I just banned a pagan heretic from the chat, who insisted that works are needed for salvation. When presented with this emphatic passage from the epistle to the church at Galatia, he used the standard apologetics dodge that "works of the law" only pertains to Levitical ceremonial laws. 

This is false, as we see elsewhere (**Romans 4** for example), but even within this passage they always fail to address the other emphatically-made point, that man IS JUSTIFIED ***by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ***.

**Romans 4**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?

2 For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

3 For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.

4 Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

6 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,

7 Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

This defines it clearly, that works of the law is a debt, not grace, and that it pertains to sin. And what is sin?

**1 John 3:4-6**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law. And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin. Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him.*

As we see in **1 Timothy 1:9**

*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers*...

It's simple. But those carried away by their own vain conceits cannot see it.

**Hebrews 10:9-13**
*Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. **By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.** And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: **But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, **sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.*

The apostate cult of Rome, with its priests daily offering meat and drink sacrifice to idols, that profane Christ by turning His sacrifice once and for all, and the ordinance to remember it by, into a cannibal cult, deny that Jesus Christ, being the substitutionary sacrifice, the propitiation for sin that was offered once and for all, paid it all.

teachings.title: Belief on the Son: what the record in John says it takes to be saved
teachings.summary: Strings together the believe passages of John and 1 John 5 to show that eternal life is given to those who believe on the Son, and that anyone who adds requirements to that belief brings another gospel.
teachings.text:
**1 John 5:9-12**
*If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son. **He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself**: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. **And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.***

**John 1:6-8**
*There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. **The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.** He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.*

**John 1:11-13**
*He came unto his own, and his own received him not. **But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name**: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.*

**John 2:11**
*This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; **and his disciples believed on him***.

**John 2:19-23**
*Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body. When therefore he was risen from the dead, **his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.** Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, **many believed in his name,** when they saw the miracles which he did.*

**John 3:12**
If *I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, **how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?***

**John 3:14-18**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: **That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.** For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish,** but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
**He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already,** because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**John 3:36**
***He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life:** and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

**John 4:39**-**42**
*And many of the Samaritans of that city **believed on him for the saying of the woman,** which testified, He told me all that ever I did.* *So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days. **And many more believed because of his own word;** And said unto the woman, **Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.***

**John 4:46-50**
*So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death. Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe. The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die. **Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him,** and he went his way.*

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, **He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life**, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**John 5:37-39**
*And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. And ye have not his word abiding in you: **for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.** Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

**John 5:43-46**
I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only? Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me; for he wrote of me.
*
**John 6:28-29**
*Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God? **Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.***

**John 6:35**-36
*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: **he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst**. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.*

**John 6:39-40 **
*And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.
And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**John 6:68-70**
*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. **And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.** Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?*

**John 7:31-32**
***And many of the people believed on him,** and said, When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles than these which this man hath done? The Pharisees heard that the people murmured such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to take him.*

**John 7:38-40**
 *He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (**But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive**: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.) Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the Prophet*.

**John 7:45-50**
*Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him? The officers answered, Never man spake like this man. **Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived? Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him? But this people who knoweth not the law are cursed.*** 

**John 8:23-25**
*And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world. I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: **for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins**. Then said they unto him, Who art thou? And Jesus saith unto them, Even the same that I said unto you from the beginning.*

**John 8:30-32**
*As he spake these words, many believed on him. Then said Jesus to those Jews **which believed on him,** If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; And **ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free**.

***John 8:44-46***
Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it. And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not. Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?*

**John 9:35-38**
*Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God? He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him? And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee. And he said, **Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him*****.**

**John 10:25-27**
*Jesus answered them, **I told you, and ye believed not:** the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me. **But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep**, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me*.


**John 10:37-39**
*If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not. But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him. Therefore they sought again to take him: but he escaped out of their hand

**John 10:42**
And many believed on him there.*

**John 11:14-16**
*Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead. **And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe**; nevertheless let us go unto him. Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.*

**John 11:24-27**
*Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: **And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.***

**John 11:40**
*Jesus saith unto her, **Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?***

**John 11:41-43**
*Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me. And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, **that they may believe that thou hast sent me.** And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.*

**John 11:45**
*Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, **believed on him**.*

**John 12:10-12**
*But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death;
Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus. On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem*

**John 12:36**
*While ye have light, **believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.** These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

**John 12:37-40**
*But though he had done so many miracles before them, **yet they believed not on him:** That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, **Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?** Therefore **they could not believe,** because that Esaias said again, **He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them**.*

**John 12:42-48**
*Nevertheless among the chief rulers also **many believed on him**; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God. Jesus cried and said, **He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.** And he that seeth me seeth him that sent me**.***** *I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness. And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.***

**John 13:18-20 **
*I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me. Now I tell you before it come, that, **when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me**.*

**John 14:1**
*Let not your heart be troubled: ye** believe in God, believe also in me.***

**John 14:9-11**
*Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Show us the Father? Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works. **Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works' sake.***

**John 14:12**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.*

**John 14:29**
*And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe.*

**John 16:7-12**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.*

**John 16:27**
*For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, **and have believed** that I came out from God*.

**John 16:29-32**
*His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb. Now are we sure that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God. Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe? Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.*

**John 17:5-9**
*And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was. I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. **For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.***

**John 17:20-23**
***Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word**; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: **that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.** And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.*

**John 19:34-36**
*But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. **And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. **For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
*
**John 20:8**
*Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.*

**John 20:25-30**
*The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe. And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
Then saith he to Thomas, R**each hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed**. And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book*

**John 20:31**
*But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.*

Let me post this again:

**But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
**
In case you aren't clear about what it takes to be saved. It isn't knowledge of the law, or adherence to the law. It isn't turning from sin, it isn't your willingness to turn from sin. It isn't that you were chosen to believe when others aren't. It wasn't because of who you are or where you were born or into what family or what genealogy you have or anything else about you. 

As the Gospel of John, which is the only book of the Bible specifically written to the unsaved that they may BELIEVE that the Lord Jesus is the Christ, and BY BELIEVING ye might have life in His name. 

That's the Gospel of God. That is the record of Him who sent Jesus, the Son of God, to die for our sins, and to be risen up again on the 3rd day, as the firstfruits of the promise. And by believing this, have eternal life. Sealed by the Spirit, become a child of God. 

**1 John 5:9-12**
*If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: **for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son. He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.***

Anyone, I mean this, anyone who adds requirements to this belief on Christ Jesus for salvation, in any manner, isn't saved, and is bringing a false gospel. Let them be accursed. I say again, anyone who adds *anything* to this record given by God of eternal life in His Son, let them be accursed. It's another gospel. Let them be anathema.

Every damnable heresy that adds to this simple Gospel, that God so loved the world that he gave His only begotten Son, that Jesus is the Christ, that all who believe on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life, seeks to take the glory away from God, cheapen His grace and puts Christ to an open shame, because every damnable heresy seeks to make us the focus, to be special boys who deserve salvation in some way. 

Every single one. 

There are none righteous no not one. All of us deserve death and Hell for our sins. Even if you "turned from your sins," you are still a sinner. Even if you cleaned up your life. Even if you stopped smoking and drinking and fornicating. You still lie. You still know good and do it not. You still have foolish thoughts. You still war with the flesh. It is an impossible standard to put on people to tell them they have to turn from their sins to be saved. And it is unbiblical and a false gospel anyway. 

*For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.*

What the person who says you have to repent of your sins to be saved actually means is you have to be "as good as they are," or they will doubt your salvation. You have to live up to their standard, or it doesn't count. They are hypocrites. The worst hypocrites, *teaching for doctrines the commandments of men*. They preach against their pet sins and tell others they cannot come to Christ unless they follow these commandments of men. That believing on Christ isn't sufficient, and list vain and doubtful disputations as doctrines, their own inventions of righteousness, *and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.*

They are angry, bitter, they hold their knowledge of the truth in pride, if they have it at all. If they are saved, they preach Christ out of contention. They *give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith*. Turning aside to vain jangling. *Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.*

*This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.*

*Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.*

*For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.*

*Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself. For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's. For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living. But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God. So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God. Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way. I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

Let not then your good be evil spoken of.*

teachings.title: Grace cannot be earned
teachings.summary: Explains that grace is the unearned, unmerited gift of God, obtained by faith, and cannot be earned by any rite, action or sanctification.
teachings.text:
BTW the idea that you earn grace, obtain grace by some means of your own, or action, or rite, or through "sanctification" or anything else, shows a fundamental misunderstanding of what grace is.

Grace is the unearned, unmerited, undeserved gift given by God from His mercy and love. 

We don't deserve salvation but it is by the grace of God that we are saved. We obtain that grace by faith, the gift of eternal life. That unmerited, undeserved gift that we don't deserve, because we are sinners. That's what grace is. 
 
It's not a spiritual, magical "force" like Star Wars. It doesn't come in portions. You don't need reups and you cannot earn it. It is the favor of God to redeem you in Christ, despite you deserving death and Hell. It is an expression of His love towards us. 

**Romans 11:5-6**
*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But **if it be of works**, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

teachings.title: Guilt, Backsliding and the Good News
teachings.summary: Speaks to those overwhelmed by guilt, pointing to the forgiveness and new life in Christ and the way back for the backslider, and encourages parents of a rebellious saved child to show love with correction.
teachings.text:
A lot of times people can get overwhelmed with feelings of guilt, hopelessness at their circumstance or the damage they've inflicted in other people's lives. The ramifications for their sin and the myriad implications that go along with making it right. 

Old feelings and patterns of behavior that developed in trauma and continue to create it. Things learned as shields to deflect the collateral damage of your sin and the return fire of those around you. 

It's hard to recover when you know you're a piece of s*it and can't see a way out that doesn't involve even greater sin. 

Stumbling blocks. Hardened hearts. Snares and temptations. Pride. Guilt. 

The good news of Jesus Christ is that once you accept that He died for your sins, all of that is gone. Your spirit, dead in sin, is quickened, made alive, born again in a twinkling, and the Spirit of God seals you unto the day of redemption. 

The Bible says your sins are as far from you as East is from West. That God the Father throws them behind His back. He remembers them no more. The peace found in Jesus Christ will fundamentally change you. 

And if you're already saved, but backsliding due to the cares of this world, simply turn back to God in Jesus name and be forgiven. 

There's work to do. We don't have time for you to be weak and lost.

Oh, this reminds me. If you're a Christian parent of a saved child who backslides or rebels, consider the Old Testament. Especially the failures of men twice as righteousness in the faith at their worst than you are at your best. 

Always let your sons and daughters know they are loved no matter what, even in chastisement. Even with the rod. Even with banishing them without the camp. That they always have a way back and know it, terms that are fair, and that it's offered in love. Don't spare the rod, but don't forget mercy and grace.

teachings.title: Lent, Fasting and the Gospel of Grace
teachings.summary: Contrasts Lent with Biblical fasting, showing that fasting is private and never a way to earn or keep salvation.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 4:1-3**
*Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.*


Lent is the spiritual equivalent of making a New Years Resolution, where you publicly vow to give up something that you probably should anyway and usually fail to keep at it for more than a few weeks. 

The biggest difference is the false expectation of God to give someone grace towards salvation (which He gives freely to those that believe on Jesus Christ) for not drinking as much booze as normal, or giving up chocolates or Twitter.  

And then there is the abstaining from meat, rather than simple fasting in a Biblical way.

**1 Timothy 4:4**
*For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving*

**Matthew 6:16-18 **
*Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.*

Fasting isn't a way to earn salvation and it certainly isn't a way to keep it. It isn't meant as a means to purchase forgiveness or indulgences. It is a spiritual act, which like prayer should be done in private, with the intent of bringing you closer to the Lord. And it isn't done by skipping a meal, dessert or having a veggie pizza and fish and chips instead of a burger.

teachings.title: What It Means to Overcome
teachings.summary: Gathers the verses on overcoming the world and explains that to overcome, in this context, means to be saved by believing on the Lord Jesus Christ. Posted as preparation for Revelation 2 and 3.
teachings.text:
**John 16:33 **

*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world. *

**1 John 5:4**

*For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.
*
**1 John 5:5**

*Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?
*

*

teachings.title: The self-righteous and the wedding garment

teachings.text:
The term self-righteous is literally a designation for the smug, prideful people, puffed up, thinking their good works make them better than others, when we are all condemned in sin. When the only righteousness we have is His imputed righteousness, washed in the blood. 

They are self-righteous and think they are better than everyone else and are going to be judged as they judge, and be shocked when they are found wanting.

We have been invited to the wedding party. The wine and meat are prepared. Fatted calf slaughtered. Everything is ready. He's provided us with wedding clothes. Invited both good and bad. 

And some will come not dressed for the wedding, clad in their own garments, which are filthy rags. And they will be cast out into outer darkness.

teachings.title: You cannot be saved by repenting of sin
teachings.summary: Argues from 1 John 3:4, Jonah 3:10 and Romans 3 that turning from sin is a work and so cannot save, and that biblical repentance is a change of mind toward God and belief. Adds that a saved person should still turn from sin out of love for God, which is not repenting of sin to be saved.
teachings.text:
Periodic reminder that you cannot be saved, you cannot be justified in the sight of God, you cannot receive the gift of eternal life, through "repenting of sin."

The Bible says sin is the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4 - *Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.)*.

The Bible says turning from sin is a work. (Jonah 3:10 - *And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.)
*
And we know the Bible says salvation is not of works, least any man should boast. That if sin is transgression of the law, and turning from wicked deeds a work, then adherence to the law is a work of the law, by which no one can be saved.  

This is made clear, in no uncertain terms, in Romans 3: 

*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:

Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
*
Note that Biblical repentance is defined as turning from one thing, towards another, be it God repenting of punishment He intended to inflict on a people, Jews repenting of not believing Jesus was the Christ, or repenting of trusting in their dead works or Gentiles repenting of their faith in idols, repentance is always a turning towards a different belief or intent. 

The phrase "repent of sin" doesn't appear in scripture, nor does any similar implied doctrine regarding salvation. What we see over and over is belief, faith, that saved. What is mentioned is turning towards God and belief in His word, and away from whatever contradicts that word that one might believe in, in order to be saved.  

So, based on this, anyone telling you that you must repent of sin, turning from transgression of the law, in order to be saved is preaching a false gospel of works, and cheapening the gift of salvation given by God, paid for by Jesus precious blood, and adding to that perfect and priceless gift our own righteousness, what Paul calls "dung."

We must believe we are sinners in need of salvation to be saved. We must accept that God in His mercy, in grace, gave His Son Jesus Christ to suffer and die for all our sins, and that He rose Him from the dead, to show the promise of eternal life. This is the faith by which we are saved. 

If you are trusting in your ability to turn over a new leaf, to be reformed from sin, even your subjective "willingness" to "repent of sin", or anything else that you might do in order to be saved, other than believe, you're perishing. 

Jesus did it all. Paid it all. While we were yet sinners, we are redeemed in the blood. Clothed in white raiment, the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ. 

Admitting you're a sinner isn't repentance, it's a humbling understanding that we cannot be holy or righteous on our own. The Bible says that the law is a schoolmaster to teach us this lesson. That God reveals it to us in our hearts, our conscience, so that no man has excuse. But this isn't repentance. 

The Bible says that having been saved, and free from the law, our sins erased and at liberty to do all things, even those that edify not, we still should turn from the sin that we did while perishing under the law. Should we continue in sin, God forbid. 

But this again isn't repenting of sin to be saved. It is turning from sin out of love for God.

teachings.title: Whosoever believeth: the record of John 3

teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**

*14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

17 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God*.

If you don't believe that God so loved *the world* that *whosoever, *(that means anyone, anywhere),*  believes *(the only condition required) *will not perish *and *has eternal, everlasting life* (*has*, meaning is then in possession of, *eternal* & *everlasting*, meaning never to be lost because it is forever), then you don't believe the Gospel, and so you are *condemned*. 

There is no other means of salvation. This is the record. 

If this offends you, or you wish to add or take away something to this, you are perishing. Repent and turn towards God.

I think I got them all. There's other verses that deal with trusting and faith that would add to this but the concept of believe is mentioned over 100 times in the Gospel of John.

It seems important, and in fact is literally the only condition given for salvation by Jesus Christ himself in the entire book. 

If you sub to my channel, and don't scroll past the God stuff, you just got done reading the entire Gospel. Chapter by chapter. In context. 

In terms of salvation, of receiving the free gift of eternal life, believing God's promise and the perfect work of Jesus Christ, the Son of God is ALL one must do. 

Jesus Himself gives this message, it's not from an apostle or a prophet. Not from Paul. 

Jesus says He and His father are one. Jesus says He is the Christ. Jesus says He was there to be killed for our sins. Jesus gives us the trinity in John. 

Every single false doctrine about salvation or the divinity and purpose of Jesus life on earth is answered in the Gospel according to John, and put to rest. 

And no other scripture contradicts the doctrines found within

And if you believe that there isn't sufficient Doctrine given in this book to get someone saved, then you're calling God a liar. Because according to the inspired word of these scriptures in this book are specifically written to get people to believe and in believing, receive eternal life.

There's nothing about repentance of sin, there's nothing about losing it in fact emphatic verse after verse of Jesus saying verily verily I say unto you that no man shall be able to pluck him from my hand. That everlasting means forever. That he shall lose none. That all men are called to him by God.

Believe.

teachings.title: Repent means a change of mind, not turning from sin
teachings.summary: Says repenting in relation to salvation is turning from a false belief to believing God's word, and that turning from sin is something everyone tries for many reasons, none of which save. Uses Jonah 3:10 to show God repented and the phrase repent of sin is not in the Bible.
teachings.text:
Repenting in relation to salvation is turning from a false belief in something to justify us before God, or turning from unbelief to believing His word. It's a changing of mind. I don't know anyone who is counting on their sin to justify them or bring them to righteousness, so repenting of sin in this context is foolish.  

Everyone, saved and unsaved feels regret and shame for their sin and, when conscious of it, tries to turn away from specific sins, whether through conscience sake, guilt, trying to work their way to self righteousness, trying to please others, to avoid punishment or consequences of their sin, etc ... 

The reprobate doesn't turn from sin out of guilt or to please God, but often will to avoid tradeoffs and mitigate consequences and risk. A reprobate may quit smoking, drinking, abstain from more vile affections for fear of jail. 

Everyone turns from sin at various points in their lives. 

We have things like New Years resolutions, diet and weight loss industry, screen time monitoring apps, aids to quit smoking, swear jars,  #NoNutNovember, appeals to "common decency," etc...all expressions of God's law written in our hearts bringing us to try and turn from the harmful and wicked things we do, for a variety of reasons and motives, selfish and selfless. 

None of that saves. 

Only faith in the risen Christ and belief in the promise of God that Jesus is the sole propitiation for all sin can save us.

*But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them;
I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land*

**Jonah 3:10**

 *And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

Now this verse is not about spiritual salvation, it is about the physical salvation of the city of Nineveh who God had sent Jonah to be a prophet unto them and get them to repent of their wicked ways or he was going to destroy their city and kill all of them. Of course Jonah objects because they're not Israelites and he doesn't think that they deserve a warning then of course God corrects him on that but that's a story for a different time, what's interesting here is that we both see that repentance, or turning away from sin is viewed as a work by God, AND it shows that repenting cannot always mean "...of sin," because we see God who cannot sin repenting of the destruction he was going to visit on them having seen their good works 

So in one verse you have evidence that repenting of sin is a work, and that repentance does not always mean of sin, because God does it.

By the way this is the closest verse you can find in the Bible where repent of sin, or turning from evil ways, is mentioned. 

The phrase "repent of sin* doesn't appear anywhere in the Bible. And the concept relative to salvation appears nowhere in any of the Gospels or the Acts of Apostles or any of the Epistles. Where the term repent or even turn away, appear, it's always explicitly spelled out what they need to repent from, and turn towards believing God.

**Jonah 3:10**
 
A*nd God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

Here we get the biblical definition of repent, God changing His mind, AND the acknowledgement that "turning from their evil ways" ie "Repenting of sin" = works.

The Bible defines itself.

In before spergs conflate physical salvation of nations, in the world with eternal salvation of individual souls in the Spirit.

teachings.title: What repent means: Acts 26:20
teachings.summary: Shows from Paul's testimony in Acts 26 that repent means to turn from false beliefs and turn to God, and that works meet for repentance follow salvation. Distinguishes knowing one is a sinner from repentance, and says faith alone saves.
teachings.text:
To be explicitly clear so no one can misunderstand:

We must turn from false beliefs regarding righteousness, and turn to believing God's report, obeying the Gospel, by trusting in Jesus Christ alone as the sole propitiation for our sins. This is what the Bible says **repent** means. 

But before we repent and believe, we have to first recognize we are sinners in need of salvation, damned without Christ. 

This is *not the same* as repentance, although it could be *the reason* for repenting. 

Knowing you're going to Hell and that God is offering you a way out is sufficient to bring many to repent and believe. Knowing God is just and not a liar is also sufficient to bring one to turn from the unfruitful and believe. 

According to the Bible, all men know the law written in their hearts, that they are sinners and worthy of death, and in need of salvation. *That they have no excuse. (Romans 1:20-21).
*
I hope that clears it up for everyone.

In Acts 26, Paul gives his testimony to Agrippa. 

Many false teachers point to this chapter, and verse 20 specifically, where Paul says that after his acceptance of salvation in Christ, he began his ministry and "*shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.*"

What the subtle false prophet will do here is rhetorically ignore the clear meaning of the complete thought "repent and turn to God," remove the "and," and count on people not understanding what "do works meet for repentance" means. 

Repent means turn from. Nothing more or less. In this verse the context is clear: turn from whatever is keeping from believing God and turn towards God. Period. There is no mention of anything else here. If you were believing on something else to justify you, being a good person, worshipping idols and dead gods, turning from sin... anything else, turn away from that, repent, and turn to God. Not towards God. But fully turn to God instead.

AND, which as a conjunction here implies "then" rather than cumulative, do works meet, meaning worthy of, that aforementioned repentance. 

We are called once saved to do works worthy of that salvation. Reading Paul's epistles we see that is consistent with everything he wrote. Exhortation and edifying to act as one having repented and believed, and by faith been saved.

I would love to move on but this heresy persists and is spread by many in error, because false prophets appeal to our natural man nature that our salvation is in ourselves, in our hands, that we can maintain salvation by being self-righteous, that it's not a free gift from God.

BTW read all of Act 26, and see what Paul's testimonial of his own conversion entailed. He describes his false belief as a Pharisee, his persecution of those who had believed on Christ, that it was his thought, within himself to do these things. He believed he was right, in other words. And then he saw the light:

*13 At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

14 And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

15 And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

16 But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

17 Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

18 To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

19 Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

*Paul in his own testimony says he had believed one way, sees the light believes Jesus' word, and now believes on Him. Biblical repentance.

Further he explains his ministry to the Gentiles, to turn them, which is the meaning of repent, from dark to light. From Satan to God. For what purpose? So they would have to "repent of their sin" to be saved?  Or in turning to light, to God, be saved and *have forgiveness of sins and inheritance *of those who have also been saved, *sanctified *by the same faith Paul has. Not by their "turning from sin" but by their faith in God.

This is the Gospel. Anyone preaching another is accursed. Period. No matter what else they may get right, if they do not get this correct they are false teachers.

Now again I stipulate that man is by nature one who seems to square circles and close gaps when faced with seemingly conflicting ideas, to bring them into harmony. 

Because of this, many believers who have accepted Christ unto salvation and then are exposed to preaching that tells them that they must repent of their sins in order to be saved, again a concept that doesn't exist in the Bible, will automatically in their own mind, take that to mean "admitting their are a sinner and regretting their sins," which all saved Christians would likely say was part of their coming to belief. 

But it was their faith that saves them, not acknowledging they need salvation, not regretting their sin. But believing Jesus died and was raised again so that God can give us the free gift of forgiveness and eternal life. 

There can be several reasons one accepts God at His word, but it is that acceptance, turning from not believing to trusting Him, that saves.

And so those who mentally put "of your sins" after "repent," and think it means acknowledge/regret, are in error, but not to the point of it being damnable heresy. Not at all. They are taking a biblical concept, applying the wrong word to it based on ignorance and hearing it said by so many, and just assuming that's what it means. 

But those who preach that we must turn from sin to be saved or to keep eternal salvation, that it is a necessary step, where our actions factor in to salvation, are teaching a damnable heresy of works salvation, and they should be rejected.

teachings.title: Forgiveness in Christ for the sin of abortion
teachings.summary: Tells those burdened by an abortion that all sins are forgiven in Christ to those who believe, with Scripture on sins remembered no more. Rejects the teaching that such women must plead their case at judgment and that infants go to limbo.
teachings.text:
Any woman who has had an abortion or taken abortifacients for birth control (and any man who condoned and participated) may feel as though God cannot forgive them, but **that's not true**. All sins are forgiven in Christ to those who believe on His name. 

The Bible says God has made a covenant with those who believe, that "*their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*" He tells us in the book of Isaiah "*I am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.*" That our sins are "*As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us*" when we trust the good news of Christ and His resurrection, His blood which was shed for all sin.

There are wicked false churches teaching damnable heresies, that women who have sinned in this manner will have to go before Christ in judgment and "plea their case" before the innocents they killed by abortion or with abortifacients. 

This evil doctrine is from the pits of Hell, and taught by the same people who teach dead infants go to "limbo" when the Bible teaches us that they go to heaven, having not known sin.

This hopeless and dark view of the salvation of Christ is damning so many women who were desperate, caught up in the cares of this world, or twisted by circumstance into believing a lie, and so traps them in sin and keeps them from knowing forgiveness in Jesus. The good news. 

If you have been feeling guilt and torment for this specific sin you've committed, or any sin for that matter, know that the Bible says *God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.*

teachings.title: Faith in Christ alone, not a denomination or a tribe
teachings.summary: Says the free gift of salvation is received by believing the Gospel, and that a denomination, a tradition, a political ideology or an attempt to keep one's own salvation can become what people trust instead of Christ.
teachings.text:
I don't push a denomination, because in our scene and it's orbits, denomination becomes a short hand to identity, and it becomes an obstacle to guiding people to faith, or worse, it becomes what people put their faith in instead of Christ. 

But I promise you, if you accept God's free gift of salvation, confess with thy tongue that Jesus is Christ, raised from the dead and paid it all for your sins, believing in your heart that He's the only righteousness you need or can have, you'll be saved and if you read your Bible, God will tell you which church gets it right.

If you're on the fence and you don't know if you have salvation, you don't know today that if you died you're going to heaven not because of anything you've done but by believing God and taking him at his word, you need to hear the Gospel. It's good news unto salvation.

  How to be saved from Hell and go to Heaven when you die. Feel free to repost this or share with whomever. I pray it will be a help to you. God bless.

If you are coveting a past to retvrn to, rather than seeking to live a godly life, today, for Him?

teachings.title: Man's choice in the Bible: free will against Reformed theology
teachings.summary: Points to the first commandment in the garden, the freewill offerings and the choices of the Old and New Testament as proof that man has a choice to believe. Answers the Reformed use of Proverbs 16:9 and sets Titus 2:11 against it.
teachings.text:
"What must I do to be saved?" 

Repent, change your mind about what you place your trust in, and believe on the Lord.

"Sorry, I don't have free will. Gonna have to see if God makes me. Thanks anyway, arminian!"

**Genesis 2**
