*15 And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

16 And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:

17 But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
*
Special boys "show me in the Bible where man has a choice! One verse!" 

Literally the first interaction God has with man is giving him one.

A simple bible study on the choices made by man throughout the Old Testament and New, and their consequences for not believing the Lord dispels the notion that there is no free will. The fact that God puts emphasis on sacrifices being free will sacrifices, pointing to Jesus and our choice to believe in His, should be sufficient. But it's the point of the entire Bible. 

Random example pop to my head, the book of Judges where "every man did that which was right in his own eyes" is the theme. That's them choosing to do what's right in their own eyes rather than in God's.

If Reformed Theology was simply **Proverbs 16:9,** it wouldn't be damnable heresy. 

*A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps*

Instead that's the Motte and Bailey they fall back to when their false doctrines are attacked, "So you're saying the Lord doesn't direct man's steps?"

What will also often happen to these reformed special boys, when cornered with verse and logic, is they will demure, saying "oh I'm not a strict five point" or whatever and back down from whichever unsupported view that's been exposed, to maintain whatever other view isn't being discussed currently. Like arguing with a liberal, it becomes nailing Jello to the wall.

The calvinist giving their version of the "good news" is like a timeshare condo pitch that says "good news, you may have won a free weekend at one of our resorts..." It's just so obviously gross.

**Titus 2:11-12**

*11 For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to **all men**,

12 Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;*

teachings.title: Free will and the Calvinist "and"
teachings.summary: Says false doctrines are held by trading one false either/or for another instead of taking the Word as it is. Argues that denying man's choice denies the point of Scripture, and that Lordship and Reformed answers always add "believe AND...".
teachings.text:
What they do is position themselves within a theological false binary and endlessly rationalize their (false) positions based on what other (equally false) positions are, rather than just accepting the Word as is. 

When poked, they will invariably argue you're the opposing binary. It is a red-blue mentality applied to religion. It's how theological traps work (and all similar false binary rhetorical traps, too)

And because they can't escape from these prebuilt either/ors to see their own error, they can't reach understanding.

This is especially true in those who think they are clever special boys, because the snare is designed to hook their pride, and the larger their pride, the more entangled they become.

What those who deny man's free will in choosing to perish or accept God's word cannot explain is why, if it is His will who be given faith, (rather than God's will being "*all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth*"), why did He create all of Scripture as His testimony, and make spreading the Gospel, the Good News of that promise, the means of propagating salvation, "from faith to faith?" To having witnesses that His word is true?

They can't explain why there was His law in the garden, even one commandment, that Adam and Eve should have choice. That the entire OT is presenting the lineage of choice for both inheritance and blessing. Denying the will of man, denies the entire point of the Word, and ultimately that belief on that word is what saves us.

As for Reformed Theology and Lordship, they claim that their "surrendering to Lord Jesus," to make themselves "slaves to Him," (rather than servants, because slave denotes not having a choice), they aren't actually trusting in Him alone. They are trusting their corruptible flesh to perfectly obey, and instead of showing complete faith in God, putting it all on themselves.

That's not even getting into the blasphemy of claiming God dictates all manner of wickedness and sin, being an absolute sovereign of the world. (Reprobate James White claimed pedophiles rape kids because it is God's will, for example).

When asked how to be saved it's always "believe AND..." It is the "and" that damns them.

teachings.title: The Spirit reproves the world of sin: because they believe not on Me
teachings.summary: Reads John 16:7-11 and notes the KJV word is reprove, not convict, and that the sin named is not believing on Jesus. Warns that the newer versions' wording opens the door to repent-of-your-sin works salvation.
teachings.text:
**John 16:7-11**

*7 Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.

8 And when he is come, he will **reprove** the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

9 Of sin, because they believe not on me;

10 Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

11 Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged*.

Public Service Announcement: In false new age versions, they use "convict" rather than the precise term, "reprove" in this verse, so they can insert the false doctrine of "repent-of-your-sin" works salvation. Don't be fooled!

When Jesus says the Holy Spirit will reprove for sin, note what the sin is; not believing on Him.

teachings.title: No limbo: Old Testament saints were saved by faith
teachings.summary: Shows that Adam and all Old Testament saints went to Heaven by faith in God's word, and that Limbo and purgatory are inventions. Points to Christ as the lamb slain before the foundation of the world and the blood on the mercy seat.
teachings.text:
No they didn't. "Limbo" is an invention of the RCC. 

Saved Christians know that Adam, and all OT saints, went to Heaven, the same way we do; faith in God's word. Jesus went to Hell to pay the price for all sin, Adam's to yours, and beyond. He freed the saved in the Old Testament the same way He's freed us. With His blood. 

Repent and get saved today! It's a free gift from God, and no institutions of man can give it to you, or deny His grace to you.

The Bible says that Jesus Christ is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. That He was "foreordained before the foundation of the world." All believers were called upon to "inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The notion of Limbo comes from unsaved false prophets, like Clement of Alexandria, who not understanding simple salvation, sought to rectify the ways of God to the feeble understanding of a natural man, stating that "it's not right" that the Patriarchs, "should be condemned without trial," when the wages of sin has always been death. Natural man questioning God's judgement is the source of most heresy. 

The scriptures teach us that there are none righteous, "no not one," and that since the first generation of man, we have been justified by faith alone calling upon the name of the Lord. 

Heaven and Hell. Those are the two choices before every man. There is no limbo. There is no purgatory. There is no working your way to righteousness. There is only the blood of the lamb on the mercy seat. The burnt offering of Christ. Amen.

teachings.title: The vanity of riches before death
teachings.summary: Wise and fool, rich and poor all die, riches cannot ransom a soul, and only the fear of the Lord and redemption through Christ give hope in the day of wrath.
teachings.text:
Psalm 49 is a meditation on the futility of life, in the building of of riches, honor and name, when death awaits everyone, rich or poor, wise or fool.

This reflection on life's vanities ties to Solomon's writings in **Ecclesiastes**, from the call to harken to the preacher to the vanity of life and the only remedy, fearing the Lord and receiving His blessing.

**Ecclesiastes 2:16**
*For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.*

This echoes the same sentiment found in verse 10;

*For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.*

**Ecclesiastes 5:15**
*As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.*

Solomon learned at the feet of his father, and after careful study of all the things his wealth and power availed him of, with the wisdom above other men, granted by God's grace, he would come to the same conclusions David sang of.

The call to incline your ear to hear wisdom, to listen to the dark sayings and parables. To seek understanding is a major theme of Solomon's **Proverbs**;

**Proverbs 4:7**
*Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.*

David teaches us the same lessons in Psalms. The wisdom of God is most valuable, because in that knowledge we may find eternal life.

David expresses confidence in his salvation. He is not afraid when the time comes to be given the wages of his sin, the iniquity of his heels, the death that awaits us all, the consequences of our own making.

Why should we fear in the days of evil, that comes our own making? He knows his redemption is a gift of God. But the man trusting his riches has no hope at all in that day. They cannot redeem themselves or their brothers, and cannot pay the ransom due God for their sins.

Again, this idea that man's riches are worthless in the judgment, that they do nothing for the dead, is repeated by Solomon;

**Proverbs 11:4**
*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.*

**Proverbs 27:24**
*For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?*

Their way is folly. The wise man dies like the fool, like the brute, and all their wealth is left for others. But the precious redemption of the soul, that one lives forever and shall not see corruption, that is of God, through faith in the Lord Christ Jesus.

**1 Timothy 2:5–6**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.*

David laments the fact that worldly prosperity deceives the wealthy, their own riches fooling them into a false sense of security. This is the larger context of the preaching of Christ;

**Matthew 19:23–26**
*Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.*

The only hope of man, rich or poor, is God. Only in Him is salvation possible.

**Proverbs 15:16**
*Better is little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith.*

The blessings of this life are not a hope for the next. The praise of men is vanity before the Throne of an almighty and holy God.

Agur's  prayer in **Proverbs** directly addresses this wisdom;

**Proverbs 30:8-9**
*Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.*

teachings.title: Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance
teachings.summary: We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging the sin we are saved from, and David's psalm models praise, confession, deliverance and judgment in prayer.
teachings.text:
Having acknowledged all He has done for us, and encouraging ourselves and others to turn to Him for salvation through the blessing of the Lord, David's Psalm turns introspective. He confesses the sin that has beset him, and compasses him about with the repercussions of it.

*Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me.*

We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging what God is saving us from.

Just as David and Paul write of having the law written in their heart, and delighting in His word, they both lament the sinful flesh that requires a Savior.

**Romans 7:24–25**
*O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

We ask they the Lord deliver us. That it is His will that be done. That those who are moved to scorn, mocking our trust in the Lord be made ashamed.

That God use us to shame those that wish to do us evil, to His glory.

Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance, and destruction of those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. This is a model of prayer. That His will be done on earth as it is in Heaven.

And in the end, the joy of His salvation overwhelming us with gratitude and praise, that such a holy and Almighty God takes heed of our prayers and notices us. Loving us so much, while we are yet sinners. Thinking of us. Providing for us. Delivering us.

*Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.* Amen

teachings.title: Delight in the saints, not Lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Calling Jesus Lord is a saved believer's statement of fact, not the false gospel of Lordship salvation; our good works add nothing to God but are poured out in love and service to the saints.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 16** presents another sacred hymn celebrating the Lord's salvation, the eternal security of the believer, and the promise of the risen Christ.

The preservation of the saints is the hope of all who place their trust in God. Our very being cries out to Him for salvation, recognizing He is Lord.

Note here that this isn't "Lordship salvation," a false gospel that says you must "make Jesus the Lord of your life" to be saved. It is saved believers, already trusting Him to save us, recognizing that He IS the Lord, as a statement of fact.

David writes, *Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee; But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight.* The good that we do isn't for Him, it adds nothing to the holy and perfect God.

The idea that Jesus needs us to make Him Lord, that by our "turning from sin," we justify ourselves before God, is hubris. It's a false gospel.

The good we do comes from Him, and is poured out to the brothers and sisters, the saints. We benefit others, and they glorify God. We obey His judgements, to one another's profit.

**Matthew 5:16**
*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

We submit ourselves to the righteousness of God. We do not seek to establish our own righteousness, but to magnify His.

**Romans 10:3–4**
*For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

David's burden is for the saints in the earth, his delight is to the excellent of God. Just as we are commanded to.

**John 13:34–35**
*A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.*

While we should seek to live peaceably with all men, we should especially look with love upon our fellow believers.

**Galatians 6:9–10**
*And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.*

This is the message that we have heard from the beginning. It is our job as Christians. It is how we are to know one another. Not keeping to ourselves or seeking out own profit. Certainly not by hating our brothers.

1 John 3:10–11
*In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.*

This is the mind of Christ, to be servants, one to another. To delight in others.

The ultimate expression of humility isn't thinking less of yourself, but not thinking of yourself at all. And the humbleness of submission to God's righteousness should naturally turn to our service for others. Not to add to God's goodness our filthy rags, but to glorify His goodness in us.

teachings.title: Set me as a seal upon thine heart
teachings.summary: The seal on the heart pictures the unbreakable seal of the Spirit, and love that cannot be bought shows God's grace is unmerited, not purchased by works.
teachings.text:
We are in the final chapter of the Song of Solomon, and the opening verses are the woman, longing to openly display affection for her beloved, the way a sister and brother as family could, without being despised. Without the judgment that would come for a maiden to kiss and embrace a lover, even betrothed, in public.

We seem to have come full circle to the beginning of the song. The wedding hasn't happened, the separation and then regained relationship. It is as if she's been dreaming the experience from courtship to maturity, as told in chapters 2-7.

There are repeated stanzas, ideas and the chorus again in verse 4;

 *I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.*

The longing to be with him, and to experience his love, to be in his embrace, echos her plaintive desires in the first few chapters.

But here, after charging the daughters of Jerusalem again, they sing;

*Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved?*

They see the love-changed woman, who was the girl they had watched grow.

The woman professes her love;

*Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.*

The eternal and unbreakable seal of the Spirit, set upon our hearts, once we know Him and are known of Him.

The love of Christ is like an unquenchable fire, the floods cannot drown it. Noah found grace in the eyes of God. His love for man endured, despite *the* flood.

The love of God could not be purchased, even if a rich man sold all his substance for love, he would be despised. It is not found in riches and cannot be bought by our works. It is unmerited. Freely given.

The woman's brothers join the choir, seeing their sister still as the immature girl they have known. Wondering what they shall do for her now, at her betrothal. A reality that big brothers and parents face, when their daughter has matured.

They contemplate what they'd do metaphorically, if she were a foundational wall or a door in need of a frame. But she states that she is fully grown. She is a wall and the breasts of her maturity are towers. An allegory for the maturity to come to the Lord, and find His grace.

teachings.title: Mary needed a Saviour too
teachings.summary: Applies Romans 4 to Mary, saying she was redeemed by her Lord and Saviour and that the Catholic view of a sinless Mary denies the gospel of justifying the ungodly.
teachings.text:
What shall we say then that Mary our sister in Christ, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Mary were justified by works, she hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

They don't believe the gospel. That Jesus justifies the ungodly, and His righteousness is given. A new man created by the baptism of the Spirit. And our sins and iniquity He remembers no more. 

So Mary has to be born sinless somehow, and fully obedient to the law her whole life, just as Jesus was. They can't comprehend Mary being redeemed by her Lord and Savior.

teachings.title: All scripture, even Proverbs, is about Christ
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries the gospel that none is righteous, and all scripture including Proverbs is about Christ the Word, through which faith comes by hearing.
teachings.text:
*Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?*

There is none righteous, no not one.

*Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?*

As we have seen, the gospel message, the understanding that we are all sinners, that God has made provision for us in His grace, is found throughout the book of Proverbs. Is there any great wisdom? Is there any more perfect truth?

We are constantly instructed to walk in the way of the Lord and to seek after truth. The word of God being a light unto our feet. Jesus Christ IS *the* way, *the* truth and *the* light. He is the Word of God made flesh. To whom all the prophets gave witness. The promise made to man throughout history.

God's word is the Word. All scripture, given by inspiration, is the word of God and all scripture, including the Proverbs of Solomon, are the word, and all are about Christ.

*Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.* So there is no wonder that the Bible says;

Psalm 45:6 *Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.*

The infinite mercy and perfect truth make establishes the fact that His throne is forever.

*Man's goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?* The Lord calls all men to His way, to follow Him on the path of righteousness, and He uses His word to do so.

*The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.*

Because;
**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God*.

But those that are dull of hearing, who haven't the eyes to see, remain lost.

**Matthew 13:15-17** 
*For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.*

As Lord, we see the wicked scatter from His gaze, because He brings the wheel over them. We are told, "vengeance is mine, sayeth the Lord," or;

*Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee*

He shall save thee, from all evil. God values true weights and measures, the balances of trade, because He judges with perfect righteousness. Weighing every man. Just so, having an unjust balance is an abomination to Him.

The wisdom of Proverbs isn't only found in the daily application. The understanding that a man of integrity is blessed and his children as blessed after him. A good reputation from honesty is an inheritance. (And a warning that an inheritance can be squandered). Therefore a child isn't only judged by their father;

*Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.*

But more than this practical advice, we actually are given a glimpse into the mind of God. To see things as He sees them. That we may walk in His ways and live! Is there anything more valuable?

*There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.*

teachings.title: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination
teachings.summary: God hears the prayer of the upright but the wicked's show of piety and self-made sacrifices are an abomination, since they go about to establish their own righteousness instead of submitting to God's.
teachings.text:
The constant reminder from God to heed the wisdom of your father, to incline your ear to instruction, to prudently regard reproof continues to be hammered home.

Following after the way of righteousness is wise, but those that have forsaken the way of God despise correction and hate reproof. Scorners hate being reproved of their ignorance. They won't seek after the wise. They feed on foolishness, are destitute of wisdom, their plans come to naught for lack of counsel, those greedy of gain and their pride brings destruction to their house.

*The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.*

*The Lord is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.*

Having God on your side, accepting your prayers, working in your life is a treasure beyond measure. The wicked and their public display of piety, their self-righteous works and so-called fasts, the "sacrifices" they make, be it the Old Testament animal offerings, or the vows made today to "cut out sweets," or to "drink less" or whatever, are an abomination to the Lord.

*The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility*. The wicked may have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. They lack the humility that comes before wisdom.

**Romans 10:3**
*For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.*

The humility of submitting to His righteousness, the fear of the Lord, that we may gain understanding, being willing to receive reproof and correction, to seek after knowledge and study to be approved before God, that we may have a ready answer to all for our hope, this is the wisdom and the way we must seek.

*The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.*

teachings.title: The root of the righteous shall not be moved
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries a consistent gospel message: a man is made good by faith that comes by the word, and the root of righteousness is Christ, not Israel as dispensationalists claim nor Peter as Catholics claim.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 12** opens with another reminder that loving instruction and knowledge is precious, and the way of righteousness, while hating correction and wisdom is brutish and wicked.

And verse two reiterates that a good man - the just, wise, fearful of God who seeks after knowledge and walks in His ways, obtains favor from the Lord, but the wicked are condemned.

**Proverbs 9:10**
*The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding*.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

**Romans 5:1-2**
*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God*...

We see how a man is made good, by the fear of God and hearing of His word, by faith seeking Him and truth, and by faith we have access to His grace, we obtain the favor of the Lord, receiving His gift of salvation.

The consistent gospel message of Proverbs cannot be overlooked.

Wickedness cannot establish a man, but the root of Righteousness, that is Christ Jesus, shall not be moved. He is the "root of Jesse" and a "branch of righteousness" (**Isaiah 11, Jeremiah 23:5-6**), established as the foundational righteousness for all believers. Through faith, believers are grafted into this root, allowing them to bear the fruit of righteousness, by the precious seed of His word.

Romans 11:16-18 
*For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.*

Dispensationalists will claim the root is Israel, but it has always been Christ. Just as Catholics will claim Peter, "a stone," is the rock, which actually is the profession that Jesus is Christ. Because no other foundation can be laid;

**1 Corinthians 3:11**
*For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

All wisdom leads to Christ.

**Matthew 7:24-25** 
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

teachings.title: Original sin and babies
teachings.summary: Says original sin is not biblical and that the idea that babies are born guilty was created to keep people in the Roman Catholic church.
teachings.text:
Remember, original sin is not biblical. And the idea that babies are born guilty, and if they die they go to hell, was created to keep people going to the Roman Catholic apostate Church. 

Protestants continued to varying degrees supporting this. Even going so far to say that babies that die who aren't elect go to hell.

teachings.title: Like Job, our end better than our beginning
teachings.summary: Like Job, believers pass through trials from the Accuser, but by grace through faith our end at the adoption and resurrection will be glorious, joint heirs with Christ.
teachings.text:
A reflection on **Job** and his later end being better than his first, and the salvation of his (and our) Redeemer:

Like Job, we are born of woman and blessed by God to an abundant life, no matter our station, having life. When temptation comes, and the law enters, and sin slays us, the Accuser, Satan, does his worst to us (tempered by God's mercy).

We have trials, and tribulations. But, entering into grace by faith, we have the hope and promise of God in Christ that our end will be better than our beginning. That at the adoption, when we put on immortality and shed corruption, when we are redeemed, our end will be glorious, as we will be like Him. And like Lot's children, male or female, we are made joint heirs with Christ.

teachings.title: Reformed theology and unconditional election
teachings.summary: Argues that Calvinist election rests on a quality in the elect, contrary to the gospel of grace, and warns that Reformed teaching is creeping into Baptist churches.
teachings.text:
Notice that the underlying false gospel of the Reformed theology Calvinist, assumes they are selected based on God's will, because of a personal quality they possess. This is antithetical to the gospel of grace, which is the love of God for all men, manifest in the life, death and resurrection of His Son, Christ Jesus. 

It places a condition on their so-called "unconditional election." They say things like this in pride, trying to sound humble. 

They make themselves their own christs. Jesus isn't even necessary in the equation, because God would have chosen them anyway.

Reformed theology is the most dangerous apostasy creeping in to Baptist and evangelical churches today. It has been there, but is suddenly increasing in scope, with reports of solid IFB churches being subverted by online ministries and pastors creeping in, denying their doctrine is Reformed, while they sow seeds of it from the pulpit. 

Beware these wolves. They appeal to believer's pride to act as the soil their corrupt seed is planted in. The thorns and thistles these tares produce become the next generation in the church.

teachings.title: Romans on the Jew and the elect
teachings.summary: Quotes Romans 2, 5, 9, 10 and 11 and shows that Paul argues salvation is by faith, so Jews after the flesh are not the elect and dispensational promises to physical Israel do not follow.
teachings.text:
*Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God...Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God. For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid...

What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin; As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.

Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.

What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all

Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.*

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit....So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

 I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost, That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen. Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth. And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha. What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone;*

*As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you. But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me. But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.*

*I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work. What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.(According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway. I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy. 

Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness? For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office: If by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them. For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes. For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance. For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

It's impossible to get any notion of dispensationalism or a promise to physical Israel being saved from this text. 

Paul creates an airtight argument that salvation is by faith, that the adoption and promises by faith are for the elect, and that Jews after the flesh are not the elect and have not obtained it.

teachings.title: Seeing Christ in Job is no anachronism
teachings.summary: The Old Testament is all about Christ, so Job's Holy One and Redeemer is Christ and OT saints were saved by the same faith in the same Savior.
teachings.text:
Many argue that Jesus wasn't known in the Old Testament, that salvation by faith didn't exist. That it is an anachronism to see Jesus in Job, and *the Holy One*.

There is no anachronism when we see Christ in in the Old Testament. It is entirely about Him.

He is the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The same Word who was with God and was God, Who walked in the furnace with Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

He was the Rock in the wilderness.

Job’s cry a few chapters from now, “I know that my Redeemer liveth” being about Christ is not an anachronism or a theological reach; it is an inspired revelation.

When Job clings to the Holy One as his strength and hope beyond death, he is laying hold of the same eternal Christ who is the substance of every shadow, the end of every type, the answer to every promise.

The Old Testament saints were saved by the same faith, looking to the same Savior, the same redemption, if through a veil that has now been torn.

teachings.title: Job: faith in God before Abraham
teachings.summary: Job shows that men feared and called on the Lord before and outside Abraham's seed, so salvation by grace through faith was always offered to all people.
teachings.text:
The Book of Job begins with the introduction of a man in the land of Uz, the titular character; Job. Uz, from the biblical clues appears to be a fertile plane in the Arabian peninsula, near where Edom would be. The time frame, many believe, is during the era of the patriarchs; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

It would be good to note that, Abraham, or Abram, was a Chaldean, a nation who are mentioned here in this chapter located in what is modern Iraq. Where the seat of Babylonian power would be. And he was called out from the city of Ur there, to go unto Hebron by God.

And, as mentioned throughout his story and his sons', there were people in this post flood era who feared the Lord, and offered sacrifices unto him.

Of course we know about Melchizedek, King of Salem, and high priest, and the tenth of the spoils offered by Abram to Melchizedek. Many consider him to be a pre-incarnate appearance of Jesus.

All this to say that the idea of the worship of God originating with Abraham, and only his seed after the flesh, is incorrect. There were many following the flood and the dispersion of nations out from Babel, that called upon the name of the Lord for salvation, and sought to offer the blood as a picture of their faith in Him, as we see Job does for himself and his family.

One of the conceits of modern Zionism and dispensationalism holds that only the sons of Israel after the flesh were special, and that they invented monotheism. But throughout the Bible we find people who were not of that line, and not given to idols and false gods. It's important to understand that salvation has always been by grace alone through faith in the Lord, calling upon his name. And that salvation was always offered to all people.

We will see in Exodus the mixed multitudes that followed Israel into the wilderness from Egypt. We will see high priests of other nations that fear the Lord. There will be people like Ruth and Rahab and others who have the faith.

The distinction for Israel was that they were given the oracles of God. That they had the prophets and the word of God delivered directly to them, and given the law of the Lord that they may be perfect, complete, and a light unto the Gentiles. The other nations. Calling all men to repentance.

But we see the greatest man on Earth at this moment, according to God, who feared Him, eschewing evil, offering sacrifices to sanctify himself and his family. Without the law. Without the temple. Without a priesthood. Without the oracles of God, knowing by the faith of his fathers what was expected.

teachings.title: Belief as a state of being
teachings.summary: Argues that believe is a stative verb, so one cannot stop believing the truth without repenting of it, and quotes 2 Peter 3 on the unlearned wresting scripture.
teachings.text:
"Believe" is often misunderstood as an action, but it's generally a state of being. Like other "be" verbs (is, am, are), it reflects an internal condition—holding something as true in your mind. 

For example, "I believe in kindness" describes a mental stance, not an act you perform. While it can seem active in some contexts, at its core, believing is a state of conviction. A state of being. 

"Believe" and "be" verbs (like is, am, are, was, were) are typically classified as stative verbs when describing a state of being. Stative verbs express a condition, state, or situation that exists, rather than an action.

They express things like mental states, emotions, senses, possession, or existence, and typically don’t involve physical activity or change. Unlike action (or dynamic) verbs, which show something happening (e.g., "run," "write"), stative verbs indicate a steady, ongoing state. 
 
Stative verbs are rarely used in continuous (progressive) tenses like "am believing" because states are seen as enduring, not temporary actions. Saying "I am knowing" sounds unnatural and stupid compared to "I know." 
 
Understanding stative verbs helps in using correct grammar, especially avoiding progressive forms with verbs that don’t typically take them. It also clarifies why "believe"is generally a state of being—an internal condition—rather than an action.

Repentance, understood as a change of mind, is the pivotal means of transforming belief because it involves a deliberate shift in one’s perspective or conviction. Belief, as a stative verb, represents an enduring mental state, a settled acceptance of something as true. Without repentance—actively rethinking or rejecting a prior belief—this state persists, as beliefs tend to remain fixed unless consciously challenged. By engaging in repentance, one reorients their mind, replacing old convictions with new ones, thus enabling a fundamental change in belief.

This is why when someone says "I stopped believing Jesus was real and that God gave His Son," or "I stopped believing the gospel was by faith alone and joined the Catholic Church," what they are saying is the repented of the truth, the big capital-T Truth, to believe a lie. 

The Bible says this is not possible. We have the Spirit of truth, cannot be deceived (it's not possible), and cannot reject it. But even if it were possible, it is IMPOSSIBLE for someone to be brought again to repentance. That's what **Hebrews 6** says and I believe it.

I figure if a mountain of scripture isn't sufficient for some people, a brief English lesson might be. 

...*even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are **unlearned and unstable wrest**, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.*

teachings.title: The disciples' doubts were not apostasy
teachings.summary: Shows from John 6, Luke 24 and John 20:9 that the disciples believed yet did not grasp the resurrection, and that doubt differs from repenting of saving faith.
teachings.text:
The Gospels repeatedly show the disciples failing to grasp the necessity of Jesus' death and resurrection, even though they believed in Him for eternal salvation.

**John 6:68-69**
*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God. 
*
Their faith in Jesus as the Messiah and Savior was genuine, but their understanding of the Scriptures regarding His suffering, death, and resurrection was incomplete until after the resurrection, when He "opened up the scriptures to them" as described in **Luke 24:45-46**.

Jesus first explicitly foretold His death and resurrection after Peter's confession of faith (**Matthew 16:16; Mark 8:29; Luke 9:20**). The disciples' reaction shows they did not comprehend or accept it;

**Matthew 16:21-23**
*From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee. But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.

*Jesus explained to them, but they did not understand it. Peter's confession that Jesus was the Christ, shown to him by the Father according to Christ, the rock on which Jesus builds His church, was sufficient to save the apostle. Yet moments later Jesus calls him "Satan" rebuking Peter's offense at the idea of Jesus suffering death. 

**Mark 8:31-33**
*And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him. But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.*

Was Peter in unbelief? No. He just didn't understand the concept of what would soon follow. He was saved by faith in the things he knew, under the Old Testament. Without the indwelling and seal of the Spirit, they did not fully comprehend the gospel of the New Testament. 

**Luke 9:44-45**
*Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men. But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.*

As they approached Jerusalem, Jesus detailed His fate again, but the disciples could not fully understand.

**Luke 18:31-34**
*Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished. For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again. And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.

***John 12:16**
*These things understood not his disciples at the first: **but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him**, and that they had done these things unto him.

*It is a key point, raised again and again that they simply did not have it given them to understand.

**John 20:9**
*For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.*

And so, after the resurrection, you have scenes like the two pilgrims on the road to Emmaus (**Luke 24:13-32**). They didn't believe He had risen from the dead. They didn't know this was Jesus who spoke to them. Jesus says "*Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?"* and explains to them they should believe the prophets and expounded the Scriptures unto them, showing how His suffering and resurrection were foretold from Moses onward (**Genesis 3:15; Deuteronomy 18:15; Isaiah 53; Psalm 22:16-18; 16:10**).

They were believers, under the OT, who trusted that Jesus was the Christ but didn't understand the totality of what that meant, until it was given to them to understand. 

The same with the apostles who didn't believe Mary Magdalene's report. Not that they stopped believing Jesus was Christ, or stopped believing the word of God they knew and understood unto salvation. 

They just didn't believe a woman's story. Same as Thomas didn't believe them. He still knew Jesus was the Messiah, but he didn't trust their accounts that He had risen from the dead, because none of them really could understand that aspect without Jesus' instruction and the Spirit that then came and sealed them. 

These passages demonstrate that the disciples' faith for salvation was present early, but full insight into the Scriptures' prophecies about the Messiah's suffering and resurrection required Jesus' post-resurrection teaching.

People, who err not knowing scripture, will often take a verse out of context, or use a word that doesn't mean what they think it does in the situation, and apply it in isolation as a proof text for heresy and nonsense. 

We should search the scriptures to see if something is so. Rightly dividing the word of God. And ask more mature Christians if what you think something means, does, or has a larger context you might be missing.

And it shouldn't have to be said that the doubting Thomases among the disciples of Christ during that 3 days and 3 nights, never repented of their faith to believe on something else. 

They never became apostates. They didn't say, "Well Jesus is dead, I'm going to become a Pharisee." Or "God doesn't even be real!" 

Christians all have moments of doubt and lack of faith, but what they will never do is repent of that saving faith to believe a lie instead.

teachings.title: Believing is not a work, and the apostate
teachings.summary: Gathers Romans 4:5, Hebrews 3, Philippians 1:6, 1 John 5:4, Romans 10:13, John 15:6 and 2 Peter 2 to show salvation is not lost and that apostates were never saved.
teachings.text:
**Romans 4:5 **
*But to him that **worketh not**,** but believeth** on him that justifieth the ungodly, **his faith** is counted for righteousness.*

**Hebrews 3:12-14**
*Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end*

**Galatians 5:4**
*Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.*

It goes on and on and on and on...

**Philippians 1:3-6**
*I thank my God upon every remembrance of you, Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ*

**1 John 5:4**
*For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.*

If you believe that an apostate is able to come again unto repentance then your argument is with God.

**Romans 10:13**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved*.

**John 15:6**
*If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.*

You cannot lose your salvation once you've been born again. When you have trusted on Christ Jesus, believing the truth that you have eternal life as a free gift of the Father, you are quicked. Sealed by the Spirit. Held by the power of God. 

So what does this verse mean?

**2 Peter 2:17-22**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. **But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.***

Wonder what this could possibly mean? **🤔**

teachings.title: Against continual believism
teachings.summary: Answers the teaching that belief must be maintained until death, using John 3, Galatians 4, 1 Corinthians 15 and Hebrews 6 to show that vain faith means never having believed.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth** in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth** on him is not condemned: but **he that believeth not** is condemned already, **because he hath not believed** in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

Calvinism falsely teaches that election is unconditional, that grace is irresistible and that belief is conferred on people by force of God's sovereign will. That they are chosen to have faith thrust upon them. (Some Calvinists will say at that point, there's a choice, but generally, they reject free will).

Saved Christians understand that there is one condition for salvation, and that condition is to believe on Christ. To believe in the name of the only begotten Son. He that believes that the Father so loved the world He gave His Son, Who while we were yet sinners, died for us, and rose again that we may have eternal life in His name. 

This is Biblical repentance. **Acts 19:3-5** defines it for us. 

*And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with **the baptism of repentance**, saying unto the people, **that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.** When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.*

Repentance towards the truth, the Gospel of God, is to believe on Christ Jesus. And believe means to trust. 

Ephesians 1:12-14
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, **who first trusted in Christ**. In whom **ye also trusted**, **after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation:** in whom also **after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise**, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Repent>believe>trust is all one thing, the Bible says. This is the condition by which one is saved. 

"But what if I stop believing?" What if you stopped trusting that the Gospel is true? What if you repent again to something else? How? There is no biblical mechanism given where this happens, where a saved believer stops believing.

There are examples given for those who backslide, who lose the joy of their salvation, who walk in the flesh, who are carnal Christians, who don't feed the Spirit, and become castaways to the calling of God. Chastened, prodigal, all of these things are given us as examples for what may happen in the Christian life of saved believers. 

But there is only one doctrine given for those that claimed to have believed and then repented to believe, to trust on something else. That they never fully believed. That they believed in vain. That it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance. 

Paul, upon hearing the church at Galatia had those among its members who were being beguiled into adopting the law to be saved, who had repented of the faith he taught them to believe something else - he wrote to them and harshly questioned if they actually were saved. 

**Galatians 3:1-7**
*O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, **that ye should not obey the truth,** before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you? **This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?** Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? Have ye suffered so many things **in vain?** if it be yet in vain. He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.*

Note that Paul doesn't say "Well you did believe, so you're still saved," and then try and get them to change their mind again. He accuses them of not believing at all. 

**Galatians 4:4-11, 14-20**
*But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods. But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.*..*Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them. But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.
*
According to this new group of people claiming "Heresy!" Paul was a heretic to be marked and avoided. 

Also John then, according to these foolish men, would be a heretic, for teaching that if one goes out from the doctrine of the truth, it was to make manifest that they never believed.

**1 Corinthians 15:12-14**
*Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.*

Faith in vain is defined for us again here, where those that had heard the truth preached, that included the resurrection of the dead, now were saying the resurrection of Christ wasn't true. Paul says that this means their faith was in vain. Empty. Having no effect. Vanity is defined again and again in scripture to mean one thing, a belief or action that has no power towards salvation in God. Vain works, vain idols, vain beliefs. *All is vanity, sayeth the preacher*, but one truth: *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man*, and so we are called to *Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth*. To believe. To trust. To keep in remembrance. To turn away from vanity.

Finally, this strange doctrine being promoted by very foolish men says that it is not only **possible** that *those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance*, but that God actually will force repentance and impose faith again upon the apostate, before they die, so that they are kept saved by God's sovereign will. 

A form of Ultra-Calvinism. 

They claim, contrary to God's word, that those that *crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame*, those who go out from us and are manifest that they were not of us, will, by the sovereignty of God, be brought to faith, "believing again" just in time to not perish. 

Despite the fact that the Bible says this is impossible. Despite the fact that they claim to reject Calvinism. 

They so badly want to have the ability to reject God, kill the new man, break the seal of the Spirit, and still be "saved," they've invented a foolish and damnable heresy that tells people who reject the truth to not worry about it. They "believed" once, and that's good enough and if they trust in something else later, oh well. 

Paul wrote entire Epistles in the Spirit to warn against believing in vain. Telling people to keep in memory the truth of the Gospel he preached. 

Because once you believe the truth, once you repent, once you trusted on Christ Jesus alone to be saved, you have the Spirit of truth, and not the spirit of error, and cannot be deceived.

**1 John 4:2-6**
*Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.*

There is a heresy that is called "Continual Believeism" that teaches, among other damnable heresies (repent-of-your-sin, baptism for babies, etc) that "belief" is a work, an action. That "belief" isn't simply knowing something is true but requires ongoing, active faith maintained until death. A "perseverance of the saints," that makes a state of mind into a process. Just as they make repentance into a process. 

The new, foolish application of this heresy makes the same mistake those who actually endorse "Continual Believeism." They too make what is a change of mind and a knowledge that something is true into a process and a work. 

They make the same damned error. 

The ""Continual Believeism" heretics say that believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe or through unrepentant sin. 

The people taking that heresy and twisting it to mean that "believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe," but they will be forced to believe again, because they "had been saved."

It's two heads of the same damned coin and a misunderstanding of what believing is, simply repenting to the knowledge something is true, accepting something true as true, trusting on it being true. 

They turn it into an action, a work, and wrest with scripture to deal with it, rather than accepting that all those who have believed for salvation just know that what they trusted in is true, even if they doubt themselves, because it is the promise of God.

Call me Colombo, because one more thing; these fools are also applying the same logic Dispensationalists hold regarding the Jews. 

That a promise of God is a promise, and so that even though the Jews are unrepentant antichrists who rejected Jesus, they will somehow still be saved in the end because they had a covenant. That in the end, God will give them faith and they will believe, and so "all Israel shall be saved!" 

The covenant with physical Israel was conditional. They no longer have the promises because they broke the condition. They held the truth in unrighteousness, and did not wish to retain God in their knowledge. 

Salvation is conditional on belief, on knowing in our hearts that Jesus is the Christ. *If thou believest with all thine heart*...If you don't know that something is true with all your heart, you don't believe it. If you know something is true with all your heart, how could you ever reject it? 

It doesn't mean you have to continually work to believe. It doesn't mean you have to constantly remind yourself that it's true that the only way a man may be saved is by faith alone in the finished work of Christ. 

It just is.

If you come up with a doctrine that contradicts clear scripture, it falls on you to explain it and make it consistent. 

If you cannot explain Hebrews 6 and 1 John 2, to make it fit your opinion, then your opinion is wrong.

teachings.title: Believed in vain
teachings.summary: Shows from 1 Corinthians 15:1-2 that believing in vain means not keeping in memory what was preached, and affirms that everything that happens at salvation is eternal.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 15:1-2**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.*

This defines what believing in vain means. That if you don't keep in memory what was preached to you, you believed in vain. It means you weren't saved. 

Not that you have to be constantly rebelieving the gospel to be saved, but if you're saved you remember the truth that saved you. It's kept in your memory, because it's true. Simple as. 

If you've been saved a while, and lived a life and been backslidden and not walking in the Spirit, for any length of time, you understand. 

You might doubt yourself but you will never doubt the truth, once you know it. How could you? It's the truest thing in existence!

I believe in OSAS. Once sealed always sealed. 

I believe in OQAQ. Once quickened always quickened. 

I believe in OJAJ. Once justified, always justified. 

I believe in ORAR. Once repented, always repented. 

I believe in OAAA. Once adopted, always adopted. 

I believe that all of the things that happen when you're saved are eternal. That once you know the truth, you always know the truth. And the Bible says if you don't know that truth, and trust something else to be saved, you never trusted in the truth in the first place. 

Let God be true....

teachings.title: The Lord rebuke thee: Joshua made clean
teachings.summary: Joshua the high priest made clean without the temple pictures cleansing by grace through faith and points to Christ the Branch and corner stone, while railing against Satan is not God's way.
teachings.text:
**Zechariah 3** presents the prophet with a vision of the high priest Joshua, in the time of Zerubbabel and the restoration of the Temple in Jerusalem. And the angel of the Lord stood before him, and Satan at his right hand to resist him. To accuse him and tempt him.

The Lord rebukes Satan, the adversary, just as in **Jude,** where angels, even archangels, who all are mightier than man, don't bring railing accusations or curses against the Devil, but say "the Lord rebukes thee."

There are many who have built an entire ministry on the basis of "rebuking Satan," railing against the devil. Not resisting him, that he flees, but they themselves speaking evil of dignities, railing against things they don't understand. They often come with a false gospel, adding works or strange doctrines. Charismatics and charlatans.

But the Lord rebukes Satan here, saying that Joshua was an iron plucked from the fire. His instrument. Even as the Lord set His name on Jerusalem, so He had chosen Joshua to be His high priest.

In the vision, Joshua is arrayed in filthy garments. And those that stood before him are ordered to take them away, that the Lord would clothe him in a change of raiment. Making him clean.

Just as Jude writes of saving some by fear, pulling them from the fire, hating even the garments spotted by the flesh. Just as Jesus promises to clothe those who believe on His name in white.

For the priests of the Old Testament must be cleansed and sanctified, made holy by diverse washings and sacrifices, but Joshua, without the temple and without the purification rituals was made clean by grace through faith by the living God.

Joshua is given a fair mitre, a head covering for the office, and fine garments, as the angel of the Lord stood by.

And again, we are given a conditional promise to the high priest, *Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by.* The angels around him.

Then he is told through the prophet, that the Lord will bring forth His servant, the Branch, a promise of Christ Jesus. He says He will lay before Joshua a stone, that rock of salvation as Christ is called;

**Isaiah 28:16**
