*Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.*

As in **1 Peter 2:6-9**
*Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light*

The image of Christ as the foundation, the corner stone, perfect and square, and the sanctification in Him of the royal priesthood, carrying over from the Old Testament, done away with, and given to a new priesthood of believers, washed clean in the blood.

The Lord of hosts says, *I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree.*

That blessed day, at the coming of the Lord of hosts. Amen.

teachings.title: Salvation by faith, national promises by works
teachings.summary: Individual salvation was always by grace through faith, but God's national promises to Israel were conditional on their obedience, and they failed and were cast out.
teachings.text:
While spiritual salvation was always by grace through faith for individuals, without any other conditions, the national promises were always contingent on works.

Separation, sacrifice and ritual cleansing to maintain the presence of the glory of God, which we saw earlier in Ezekiel, went out from the Temple, and here in these prophecies, promised to return, if they got right. And the Law was perfect and glorious to that end. The fault wasn't with that covenant, but with the people.

**Hebrews 8:6-8**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah*

The moral law and commandments, which are still in effect today in the NT, were a schoolmaster to lead us to Christ for salvation. Same then as today. Even the law written in our hearts, for the Gentiles without the advantage of the oracles of God. All have sinned and fallen short, so we need a spiritual redeemer.

But the laws of sanctification and reconciliation for the physical nation were not only doable, but God gave pretty explicit instructions on how to maintain it, which some of the time -  during the period of the Wilderness, the entry into the promised land, here and there during the time of Judges and Kings, they managed to keep. And had God's blessings upon them.

Israel was meant to be a light unto the world. Showing all nations that if they did these things and sought after God, they would be blessed as well. Eventually, it would lead to the culmination of the time of Christ, the BRANCH, The Lord, the King of Kings, coming to establish all of the end times promises of the Kingdom given to the people. In the city He chose to place His name. In the line of David as promised.

And they would not.

So, when Jesus did come, the leaders of the Jews were unable to deliver a people meet for repentance. They, being teachers of the Law were blind guides, thinking that whatever promises they had, were deserved being "Abraham's seed." That their added rituals and Pharisaical cleansings meant they deserved both the spiritual salvation and the restoration of their earthly kingdom.

And rather than being ready for the Kingdom, they were instead cut off and cast out.

**Matthew 8:11-12**
*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

teachings.title: The one test of a false teacher
teachings.summary: Says the one criterion the Bible gives for a false believer or teacher is whether they add works to the gospel, not behavior after being saved.
teachings.text:
The one criteria the Bible gives for identifying a false believer or false teacher is do they add works to the gospel. 

Not behavior after being saved. Not by how good they are. Not if they turn over a new leaf. Not if they clean up their life. Not by how righteous they act, what church they go to, or any other thing, but what they trusted in.

teachings.title: Original sin, infant baptism and grace
teachings.summary: Argues that teaching original sin leads to baptizing babies as a work for grace, and that anything added to grace makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
The false teachings of "Original sin" are the root of most damnable heresy. The false teachings of it immediately stir the maternal to ask "What about my baby??!!" From there it becomes about works and cult-control

As soon as you are water baptizing babies because moms are freaked out about being told that if their kids die, they might go to Hell (Or maybe limbo,) you've put faith in a rite and a priest and a church. Not Jesus. And not a just God.

And the churches that teach this damnable heresy have convinced you to do a work for grace that's not in the Bible. 

From that point on, their people have accepted a lie, and so they will be invested in maintaining the lie, even when there is no scripture teaching it, at all. Even when they are shown why the handful of out of context scripture that they are told actually teaches baptism of babies is wrong. Spiritual blindness because of fear and pride.

Doing something to "receive grace" makes grace no more grace. 

Grace is the unearned and unmerited favor of God. Work, laboring, receives a wage, not grace. Anything that adds anything to create merit or to be deserving in any way, means you are going to receive your just wages. 

Death and Hell.

teachings.title: Calvinism and election
teachings.summary: Says Calvinism makes election rest on foreknowledge or God's sovereign will rather than grace, reads Romans 9 as about nations, and cites Ephesians 1:4-5 for predestination in Christ.
teachings.text:
Even so, Calvinism falls into the same heresy, making the election not of grace, but of foreknowledge and predestination, God choosing who is saved based on His "sovereign will." That they are elect because of something God saw in them. Some merit.

They also use **Romans 9**, which was written about nations of people, the very scripture dispensationalism uses to justify its own heresy towards Jews, except changing the election from a physical nation to another innate quality; their usefulness to God. 

**Romans 9:10-13**
*And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;) It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated*.

Again, Paul is writing about nations, not individuals, and drawing the comparison between the children of promise through Isaac, and the inheritance of that promise through Jacob rather than Esau. 

Paul goes from **Genesis**, the first book of the Old Testament, through **Malachi**, the last to make his point, and that point is not that God pre-ordains who will be saved and who is condemned.

Rather God pre-ordains that His promise will be kept, and those that partake in the conditions for that promise, are heirs to it. In this case, the election of grace through faith in His word. 

**Romans 9:22-24 **
*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

God predestined that those who believe on His promise will be given the gifts of that promise, being longsuffering towards the unregenerate Jews, that His mercy may be shown to all who believe, in Christ. 

For all men are called; The Bible says:

**John 12:32**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.*

And again:

**2 Timothy 1:9**
*Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.*

And:
**2 Peter 3:9**
*The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
*
All are drawn, all are called. God's will is that no man perish. It is to His purpose that we avail ourselves of the grace given the whole world, whom He loves. *That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. *

But by making the election not of grace, but sovereign will, and not to all men, but the select few, they make the promise of God to no effect. That whosoever believes isn't whosoever, but the preselected few, drawn by irresistible grace and unconditional election. 

"Unconditional election," is an oxymoron, used as a fig leaf to say "actually, we aren't special boys. We are randomly chosen, basically." An election without conditions is not an election, not a chosing, but is a random decision. It is a false humility used to hide their pride. 

They don't believe in grace, but in their own worthiness. Even if they say they don't know why they are special, only that they are. 

**Ephesians 1:4-5**
*According as he hath chosen us **in him** before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us to be adopted his sons by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.*

All who trust Christ are predestined in Him. That election of grace given the whole world, is predestined in Jesus according to the will of the Father. It is Christ Who was chosen before the foundation of the world. Not the special boys who believe themselves to be their own little christs, making grace no more grace.

teachings.title: Entering the rest in Hebrews
teachings.summary: Shows from Hebrews 4 that only those who believed the promise entered Christ's rest, and that sin does not lose salvation while those who reject the truth for their own works were never saved.
teachings.text:
*Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you **should seem to come short of it.** For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached **did not profit them, not being mixed with faith** in them that heard it. For we which **have believed** do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world. For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works. And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest. Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and **they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:** Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts. **For if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day**. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. **For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his**. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest**, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.***
...
***Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.** But exhort one another daily, while it called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. **For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;** While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, **harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.** For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? **And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.***

**Hebrews** teaches clearly that only those who have believed the promise, and entered into the rest of Christ Jesus, are saved. 

It does not say if we sin, we lose salvation. It doesn't say if we forget our rest, we aren't saved. Paul writes that those without faith unto salvation, who heard the word and yet turned to their own works, and hardened their hearts, never entered into that rest. 

It isn't our faith and confidence in ourselves that saves. We aren't condemned, even if we forget who we are, made new in Christ.

But if one were to fall away from the truth, and reject the offer of rest to do their own works after knowing better, they were never saved and they will be condemned. Apostates, as **Hebrews 6** goes on to describe.

teachings.title: Calvinism makes grace no more grace
teachings.summary: Argues that election by a chosen purpose introduces merit, so the TULIP doctrines undo grace and are self-refuting.
teachings.text:
Rebuking a Calvinist, and it occurred to me that they make grace no more grace. If grace is entirely unmerited, but God "chooses" someone for His own purpose, that introduces merit. That person then has a predetermined purpose, and value, or God wouldn't have chosen them. Thus they are needed and inherently that's merit.

Even if you introduce the concept of limited free will, the Calvinist who doesn't hold to irresistible grace, and says "if not me, then He could use someone else," they are simply making a pool of merit, shared across a group. 

To make irresistible grace work in a limited atonement system, you'd have to then deny their other doctrine of God's sovereignty, and say it's random. Which of course isn't what election is. No one is elected by random. There are candidates, considered for their qualities, and chosen. A sovereign god, who micromanaged creation, couldn't leave it up to chance anyway. 

Calvinism, especially the TULIP doctrines, are self-refuting.

teachings.title: Falling away and those never saved
teachings.summary: Explains from Hebrews 6 and 1 John 2:19 that one who truly trusted Christ does not fall away from the faith, while backsliding and doubt differ from rejecting the truth. Adds that doctrine comes from clear scripture, not parables.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:4-6 **
***For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened,** and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, **to renew them again unto repentance**; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.
*
No one, once saved, who has trusted on Jesus, and the promise of God, baptized of the Spirit and sealed unto redemption, having the spirit of adoption, knowing with all your heart that Jesus is the Christ, Whom the Father promised, will ever doubt that truth. 

We may backslide, doubt our own salvation and commitment to Christ, even deny Him to others. Doubt God's grace for us. Even forget the joy of our salvation. Have fear, little faith, get caught up in false doctrines, etc...

But you will never fall away from believing that Jesus is Lord and God is real, and that salvation is by grace through faith, to believe in your heart that something else is true. 

If someone chooses atheism after having full knowledge of salvation, they were never saved. They believed in vain. They had head knowledge, but didn't trust in their heart. And if they do reject the truth, it is IMPOSSIBLE for them to come again to repentance.

**Proverbs 26:7**
*The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.*

Take your doctrine from clear scripture, not trying to wrest one from parables.

teachings.title: Was Mary good?
teachings.summary: Answers that Mary, like every believer, was made good only in Christ and called God her Saviour in Luke 1.
teachings.text:
Was Mary good?

I'm not good, either. 
But in Christ I am made good in Him, and saved by so sweet a Savior!

Just like my sister Mary. 

**Luke 1:46-47**
*And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.*

teachings.title: Preaching Christ from Micah
teachings.summary: Christ could be preached from Micah as Philip preached from Isaiah 53, since the Old Testament is entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith.
teachings.text:
Continuing a thought from the study of Hosea; Christ could be preached to unbelievers through the book of Micah, just as Jesus was preached to the Ethiopian Eunuch by Phillip, using **Isaiah 53**. Micah, like the other prophets, preached judgment for sin, the holiness of God, the truth of His mercy and His Messiah, and redemption by faith in His word, and a call to sanctification and separation for us once saved.

We are blessed to have the clear Gospels, but you can see how there were always a righteous remnant. 7,000 who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal. How the Old Testament was entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: How you can know you are a child of God
teachings.summary: Answers that assurance rests on the promise of God who cannot lie to all who believe on Christ and call on His name, not on our desire or willingness to obey.
teachings.text:
The answer is "Because God Who cannot lie promised before the foundation of the world that whosoever believes on Christ Jesus, calling upon His name for salvation, has eternal life, and are sealed and regenerated by the Spirit that you may KNOW you are a child of God. 

MacArthur makes it of herself. Her desire. Her willingness to obey God. All of these things that any Christian may struggle with at times. 

He makes it of her because he doesn't believe that God's grace extends to all, that it is conditional of accepting the free gift, and that we may know we can trust God's word.

teachings.title: Repent ye: John the Baptist's call to believe
teachings.summary: Repent means to change your mind and believe, not to stop sinning, so those John baptized confessing their sins had believed and were saved, baptism being the answer of a good conscience, not its cause.
teachings.text:
Repentance Moment:
**Matthew 3:1-12**
*In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?*
*Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.*

Repent ye; for the Kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Repent means to change your mind, to accept new information as true and have a change of heart, a conversion.

Here, John the Baptist is saying "Reconsider what you know and believe me." He is not saying "get your life together and stop sinning, the Kingdom of Heaven is here." They were baptized in the water confessing their sins, because they believed him, and were saved.

While false gospels that add works to salvation may disagree, Bible believing Christians who know water baptism is an answer for a good conscience before God, and not the cause of it, should be able to understand this context.

John further chastened the religious leaders of the Jews, who came down to see him and his work, making the paths straight for the Lord. He asks them who has warned them to flee the wrath to come? Where are their followers come to be baptized before the coming of Christ? Where is their fruit meet for repentance? If they had preached the coming of Christ, they would have followers ready to accept the truth that the Christ was come. But this generation of vipers did not. They were trusting in being seed of Abraham.

The water baptism of repentance, the sign of believers, was a prelude for the baptism of the Spirit in Christ. A baptism of fire. Amen

teachings.title: The false gospel of infant baptism
teachings.summary: Explains that baptizing infants is a false gospel, since baptism is an outward sign of belief and infants do not carry sin they have not committed.
teachings.text:
The damnable heresy of paedobaptism, the false belief that if an infant is sprinkled with water, initiating them into a denomination, that they are cleansed from sins (that they haven't committed), is accursed, being another gospel. A false gospel. 

This heresy gives parents the mistaken idea that their child would otherwise be cast into Hell without a human authority giving them some form of absolution. 

That the water baptism that is given by God as an outward sign to men that someone has believed on Christ is what regenerates the saved, and not the baptism of the Spirit, as the Bible teaches. That infants carry sin. That God judges the innocent who have not the understanding of good and evil, right and wrong, or the capacity to commit it. 

That the gospel of God is a series of transactions and works instead of a loving relationship between Him and His children. 

Anyone who teaches that infants need to be baptized are not saved.

**Acts 8:26-39**
*And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.

Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him. The place of the scripture which he read was this, **He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth.**

And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus.

And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?

And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.*

The most comprehensive example of soul winning and the baptism of believers in the New Testament is given here, in **Acts 8**. Water baptism of new believers is mentioned several times in the narrative given in the Acts of the Apostles, but while the order of operations remains the same, the story of Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch is the most detailed. 

We are shown that an unsaved person searching for truth will have opportunity to be given what he seeks. That saved believers will come I their life to preach the word of God. That a saved Christian must lead them through scripture to faith. That faith comes by hearing the word of God. 

And, importantly, we learn what is required to be water baptized, as an ordinance to testify of their found faith, that you *believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God*.

The only examples given are all of adults. And all are believers first, the water baptism being an answer to their good conscience before God, as Peter writes. Not the cause of that good conscience, which is found by the regeneration of the Spirit, being baptized into Christ, spiritually, by faith.

teachings.title: Every works religion redefines repentance
teachings.summary: Observes that religions from Catholicism to Calvinism to Hebrew Roots agree in denying that repentance is a change of mind, and so teach a false gospel of works.
teachings.text:
Every religion that teaches that eternal life is not a gift, that you have to turn from sins to be saved, that denies eternal security of the believer, salvation is a "process," that "faith without works is dead" means you aren't saved without works, or that salvation is not offered to all men...every flavor of religion from Catholicism to Calvinism, to Hebrew Roots to Evangelical Protestantism to CI and 7th Day Advantists...they all agree with each other that "repentance" doesn't mean a change of heart/mind/understanding. 

They would condemn each other in a circular firing squad yelling "HERETIC!" over their other doctrine, but they all agree with a false gospel of works. Self-righteousness. Of earning eternal life, and denying that we are saved by grace through faith in Christ, are sealed by the Spirit and held by the power of God the Father.

teachings.title: To obey is better than sacrifice
teachings.summary: False religion offers its own righteousness and costly works instead of believing on Christ's righteousness, which God calls rebellion and witchcraft.
teachings.text:
*Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.*

This is so hard for people trapped in false religion to grasp. They believe their own righteousness must be offered in sacrifice, even if it means going against the command of God to believe on His Son's righteousness instead.

They will dress it up as Saul did. That they are offering the best. Buildings made of marble and images laid with gold, and sacrifices made to idols representing, in their minds, Christ. Doing all these works that they reasoned for themselves as good. That their logic of men and vain traditions came up with, often through compromise and fear of the people.

God despises it. It is witchcraft. Rebellion.

teachings.title: Calvinism does not match John 3:16
teachings.summary: Sets limited atonement, unconditional election and denial of eternal security against the plain words of John 3:16.
teachings.text:
If you believe in "Limited Atonement," you don't believe the Gospel.

*For God so loved **the world*** ***that he gave his only begotten Son***...

If you believe in "Unconditional Election," you don't believe the Gospel.

...*that **whosoever believeth** on Him*...

If you don't believe in eternal security, you don't believe the Gospel. 

*...**shall not perish but have eternal life**.*

teachings.title: Underused scripture for eternal security
teachings.summary: Reads Ephesians 1 and Acts 13 as support for eternal security and justification by faith alone, not of works.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 1:3-14**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace; Wherein he hath abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence; Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him: In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will: **That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.***

**Acts 13:38-39** 
*Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: and by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.*

Underused scripture for eternal security and salvation by faith alone, not of works.

teachings.title: Leprosy as a picture of sin
teachings.summary: Notes that leprosy in scripture pictures sin in the unregenerate man and its healing pictures saving grace through Christ.
teachings.text:
All throughout scripture, the disease of leprosy acts as a picture of sin in the unregenerate man. And the miraculous healing of leprosy, a sign of the saving grace from God. Being healed by Christ. It serves as a like image of our spiritual self, consumed by sin. 

And it takes hold of people in nations that are turned away from God.

teachings.title: The true purpose of God's commandments
teachings.summary: Beyond being a schoolmaster and for the lawless, the law's real purpose is to show the saved God's will for a successful life, not to earn salvation.
teachings.text:
*Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper withersoever thou goest. This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

This is the true purpose of God's commandments. This is how the law is relevant to those saved by the law of liberty, by grace through faith in Christ Jesus.

Yes the law is a schoolmaster that brings us to understand we need salvation. Yes the law of for the lawless, that they may be punished according to the will and perfect judgement of God.

But it's real purpose is for a righteous people to know the will of God for their lives, and in keeping it as best they can, have a prosperous and successful life in service to our God.

Those that make this obedience to the law their gospel, and seek to work their own righteousness as a means of achieving or maintaining their salvation, miss the point and whatever gain they receive is offset by their constant doubts and fears. Not having faith, they please not God. Their filthy rags of their own righteousness give them nothing but hopelessness.

This isn't a prosperity gospel. There is no promise of riches and earthly wealth. But true success in our walk with Christ. Being taken care of, all we need, that we may store up riches in heaven. That we may be saved and all our house. That we may win souls and edify the brethren.

Amen

teachings.title: Meditate therein day and night
teachings.summary: As with Joshua, believers are saved by faith and blessed in this life by loving and keeping God's word, so be strong and not afraid.
teachings.text:
Beginning the **Book of Joshua**, the narrative of the capture of Canaan by the Israelites, the land given them by God for their rest, led by a deliverer named Joshua, a Hebrew variation of the name Jesus. A picture of the Christ to come.

We read the Lord speaking to Joshua as He had Moses, and reaffirming the promises made in His word, upon which Joshua trusted. By faith the people would possess the land for an inheritance, which God had sworn unto their fathers. The Lord's promise is the same to those of us who believe;

*I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee*.

The captains of the tribes give their loyalty to Joshua, to lead them in Moses' place. And God reminds Joshua of the promise made in the covenant with Moses, that if they obey His commandments, and follow His law, turning neither to the right nor the left, that they shall prosper. That by meditating day and night upon His word, and letting His law depart not from their mouth, they will have good success.

This promise is to us as well. That if we love His word and keep it in our hearts, His law upon our lips, meditating on it day and night, we will prosper and have success in this life.

Like the Israelites, we are saved by faith, delivered by His mighty hand into the promised land, but we are also blessed in this world by keeping His commandments. That it be well with us. This is the hope of God, the good news of His Gospel. The same faith that saves us today, and the same obedience that blessed those who keep His law. So be not afraid.

*Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

Amen

teachings.title: Once saved, always saved
teachings.summary: Gathers John, Jude and 1 Peter passages to show that the believer is kept by the power of God, and urges trust in the risen Christ.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life*.

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life*.

**John 6:37**
*All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.*

**John 10:27-29**
*My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand.*

Romans 8:38-39
*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,  Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

**Romans 11:29 **
*For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance*.

2 Corinthians 1:21-22 *
Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God; Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts*.

**Ephesians 2:8-9**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, least any man should boast*.

**Ephesians 4:30-32**
*And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption. Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.*

**Philippians 1:6**-**7**
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.

***1 John 5:10-13***
He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.
*
**1 Peter 1:3-5**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that **fadeth not away**, reserved in heaven for you, Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.*

**Jude 1:24 ***
Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy*

There is no doubt that salvation...once we have heard the gospel, repented towards faith in the promises of God, been born again in Christ, our dead spirit quickened, our flesh nailed to the cross, inwardly a new creature, sealed by the Spirit unto the day of redemption, made by God to sit together in heavenly places. Kept by His power to an inheritance incorruptible through faith unto salvation, a promise given without repentance of eternal life, made co-heirs with Christ, adopted by God, the Spirit testifying within us that we are sons of God, our spirit crying out, 'Abba!" Once we have not only tasted of the heavenly gifts and heard the calling, but have trusted in the record and obeyed the Gospel of God...there is no doubt that we shall stand in the grace of God and continue in faith until the end of the world. Amen

Once you are saved, you are always saved, or else God is a liar. That eternal security He has promised is the hope we have in Christ. The rock of our salvation. 

Do not doubt Him that is able to deliver you. Let go and trust in the risen Christ.

teachings.title: Choose life
teachings.summary: Reads Deuteronomy 30 and Joshua 24 and urges the reader to choose life, embrace truth and follow Christ.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.

But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

From the beginning, God has offered us a choice. Without that choice, the evil in this world makes no sense. As the Calvinists teach falsely, their god is the author of evil. But our God provides us the choice between good and evil, life and death. 

Throughout the Bible, from Adam and the tree, through even the Millennium Reign, God allows man a choice. 

Of those that choose life or choose death, God may elect some to serve a purpose. To perform a task. To serve as an example. But the choice of life and death stands before all men. 

When the unsaved ask, "If God real, why bad things happen?" We have the answer; because man chooses death over life. 

Calvanism has no answer other than to profane God and blame Him as the heathen do. 

Without that choice, none of the scriptures make sense, none of the judgments of God are righteous. It all becomes a play, a Punch and Judy show of cruelty. 

Choose life. Embrace truth. Pick up your cross and follow Him. 

**Joshua 24:15**
*And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.*

teachings.title: Repent of sins teachers are least forgiving
teachings.summary: He observes that churches teaching repentance of sin as a condition of salvation become self-righteous and unforgiving, having lost grace and humility.
teachings.text:
As an aside, in my experience, churches and people who teach repentance of sin as a condition of salvation tend to be the least forgiving.

They take pride and hope in their own righteousness, and need to compare themselves to the sins of others so that they can make themselves feel holier. This is the sin of self-righteousness. Something that used to be widely understood in Christian circles. But with the rise of things like lordship salvation and repent of your sins heresy that grace and mercy and humility has gone out the window in many congregations today. They become respecters of persons. They give themselves some credit for being freed from bondage in Egypt rather than understanding, it was by the grace and mercy of God.

Something to keep in mind

teachings.title: Release of debts a picture of salvation
teachings.summary: The release of servants and debts in the seventh year pictures salvation in Christ, so we should forgive debts as God forgave ours and send others away blessed.
teachings.text:
I covered the law of jubilee before, in [Leviticus 25](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/11512). It is worth noting again that the redemption of the servant and the forgiveness of debts, like the Hebrews being freed from bondage in Egypt, are pictures of the salvation found in Christ Jesus. We are called upon to release people of their obligation to us, in time. That if they haven't paid us back by the 7th year, to forgive them their debt, as God has forgiven ours.

*And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to day.*

And as a servant, not just sent away at the end of the term, but sent away with blessings and furnished to succeed on their own. Not as you took them in, but *wherewith the Lord thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him.*

Just as God does every believer.

Think not too highly of yourself. Remember your fallen state. Remember that God has sealed you as the servant who will not leave your side. As the pierced ear signified here in the law. We are sealed by the Spirit, to be His servants forever.

teachings.title: Why the law cannot save
teachings.summary: Keeping God's law is for our good but not for salvation, since no one can keep it all; the law is a schoolmaster bringing us to Christ to be justified freely by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
We should also remember that obedience to the civil laws of God are for our benefit. For our good always. That it be well with us. That it prolongs our days and that we are preserved alive. Not for salvation. Not for our own righteousness.

The law is a schoolmaster, teaching us our need for salvation in Christ.

**Galatians 3:24-27**
*Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

Because;

I*t shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.*

If we observed to do **all** these commandments, it would be our righteousness. We would have to glory.

**Romans 4:1-12**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: and the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.*

But knowing that it is impossible in our flesh to observe all these things, we understand that it is God's glory that His mercy is revealed.

**James 2:10**
*For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.*

**Romans 3:10-12**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.*
*They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

As Paul writes a few verses later, *There is no fear of God before their eyes.* But as Moses writes here in **Deuteronomy 6**, under the same Spirit as Paul, we are to learn the law of God and keep it in our hearts, in our minds, *That thou mightest fear the Lord thy God*.

And in that fear, that respect and love of the Lord, we may know we have His mercy towards us:

**Romans 3:23-26**
*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

teachings.title: Remember thou wast a servant in Egypt
teachings.summary: Remembering we were servants to sin freed only by grace, believers should show the same mercy to others, even strangers, that they may come to Christ.
teachings.text:
*And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the Lord thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.*

The spiritual application of this understanding, that Jesus is the Sabbath, that our works contribute nothing to our salvation should be coupled with remembering that we were servants to sin. That we were in bondage in Egypt. That before God brought us out from the ministry of death and into eternal life by His mighty hand, we were as slaves, just as the Hebrews were.

And the extension of the Sabbath to those who are our sons and daughters, our employees, and even to strangers, is to show the same mercy given us who were once servants, that they may come to know the truth in Christ.

Never forget that we were servants in Egypt, and only are free by the grace of the Lord. Have charitable love for the unsaved that they may be lifted out of bondage as well.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: Matthew 16
teachings.summary: Explains that the rock in Matthew 16 is the confession that Jesus is the Christ, not Peter or a denomination, and what the gates of hell not prevailing means.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 16:13-18**
*When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am? And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets. He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, **Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.** And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and **upon this rock** I will build my church; **and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.***

Catholics cite verse 18, stripped of context, claiming that Simon Peter is the "rock," rather than the testimony that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Despite "Peter," or *Petra*/*Cephas* meaning a small stone. (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*). 

What they also miss is that it is this confession of the faith that Jesus says the gates of Hell shall not prevail against. The "i*t*" in that clause refers back to the "*rock*," which refers back to the Gospel, the truth of Who Jesus is. 

All those who believe on that truth are part of Jesus' church, and the gates of Hell cannot prevail against that confession; believing that Jesus is Christ. 

If we strip the Biblical context away, and try to make sense of it as Peter being the rock, and the church being a physical denomination on earth, what in the world does the phrase "the gates of Hell shall not prevail against" actually mean? 

There is no other reference to "gates of Hell" in scripture, other than Jesus possessing the keys to death and Hell at His resurrection (the Gospel). 

How exactly would Hell's "gates" prevail over anything? How does a doorway to Hell prevail against a church? It becomes a non sequitur in the hands of the natural man, and while it sounds epic, it carries no actual meaning in that incorrect context.

teachings.title: The Passover open to every stranger
teachings.summary: The Passover pictures salvation in Christ offered to anyone, the unclean and the stranger alike, with those who refuse cut off, and after salvation we follow the Lord.
teachings.text:
We are in **Numbers 9**, and we see this the 3rd Passover, held in the wilderness and the Lord tells Moses not to forget the ordinance that He has established, using the Passover in Egypt and the physical salvation of Israel as a picture of Christ and the individual salvation of man. I've done larger studies on the parallels and processes [before](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9752). But it is always good to note that it was a reminder of Christ to come, just as the Lord's supper is a reminder of Christ for us now.

Here, God provides Moses with a few guidelines given circumstance. That the ceremonially unclean and those sojourning participate in Passover just the same, that strangers among them that wish to are invited, and those that don't participate are cut off and bear their own sin.

The parallels are pretty clear as to how this corresponds to individual salvation in Jesus. Anyone. Even the unclean. Even those afar off from God, get to participate in the sacrifice and the blood. Even the stranger among them. The sinner, the worldly, the Gentile...all are invited to take part in the salvation by the blood, in the faith of Jesus Christ.

And those who don't are cut off and made to pay for their sin.

It is that simple. People try to overcomplicate salvation because they want to make it about themselves or to make it a sensual experience that they can "feel," or see. Because they lack faith, which is the evidence of things unseen.

And then we are called to follow Him.

Just as the movement of the Tabernacle and the camps was dictated by the movement of God upon them, the pillars of smoke and fire. At the commandment of the Lord they moved. At His command they rested.

And so it is to be in our lives, that after salvation we follow the Lord.

teachings.title: The prodigal son and biblical repentance
teachings.summary: Reads Luke 15 as a picture of the Father's love for His children and of repentance as turning toward Him, not sorrow, willingness to work, or making Him lord.
teachings.text:
**Luke 15:11-24**
*And he said, A certain man had two sons: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: and bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.*

In this beautiful picture of the Father's love for His children, which teaches God's unconditional love for those that are His, even when we backslide, even when we despise our inheritance and go after the world in sin. Even as we served other masters and feed the swine. That no matter what, we may return to the Father. 

More, we see that even though it may be important for us to feel the need to be full of sorrow and remorse at having gone astray, and to want to work it off, to be worthy of the Father, God isn't interested in any of that. Only that you turn towards Him. 

We see the father runs to meet the son. He ignores the son's groveling. Even before the son gets it out the Father has hugged and kissed him. He doesn't even get a chance to offer to work off his sins, the Father sends for him to be clothed in the best robes, given a ring and shoes. To be made whole in the gift of the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. And a joyous feast is called to celebrate. 

Blessed is the man to whom God will not impute sin. Blessed are we who have been forgiven.

When the son *came to himself*, is the moment of repentance. That he needed salvation from the state he was in. Being hungry and without, led him to it. 

It was that turning towards the Father that shows repentance. Not his sorrow and regret. Not his willingness to work, or wanting to make his father his lord.

It was his coming towards the father, who seeing him afar off ran to meet him. 

That is biblical repentance. It's all God asks of us. That we turn to Him and allow Him to clothe us in righteousness that we did not earn or expect or deserve. And to rejoice, celebrating our reconciliation.

teachings.title: The redemption of the firstborn
teachings.summary: The shekels paid for the firstborn beyond the number of Levites picture the price of our redemption, paid by Christ, God's firstborn Son.
teachings.text:
God's original plan for the children of Israel was that their firstborn sons would be given to Him in service to the Lord, and the firstborn cattle as sacrifice, thus a picture of Christ Jesus. But the children of Israel failed almost immediately after being led from Egypt, worshipping the golden calf;

**Exodus 32:25-29**
*And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:) Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour. And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.*

This incident changed the plan, and instead a generational priesthood was created from the Levites, under the charge of Aaron.

And so this left an accounting due the Lord.

Here we see at the poll of men, numbering them by tribe, that the Levites were fewer in number than the firstborn sons of Israel, and so a reckoning was due. And to offset the difference, a collection of 5 shekels was made for each son. God will always receive His due.

The redemption of this time is a picture of the redemption in Christ of believers. The cost, His life and death and blood. The burnt offering of His firstborn Son. And the resurrection the promise made in Him.

There is always a price for redemption. And the price for righteousness is Christ, His imputed righteousness on all who believe.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.summary: God has not cast away His people He foreknew, meaning the believing remnant like Paul and the seven thousand, chosen by grace and not works.
teachings.text:
Paul had just concluded that they are a disobedient and gainsaying people. God tried.

As Christ put it in **Matthew 23:37**;

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

So, what then? Are they all cut off? God forbid, for Paul is *an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.* They cannot be all cut of simply by being Israel after the flesh, or Paul wouldn't be saved.

*God has not cast away his people which he foreknew.* We have already seen that Paul has already written in **Romans 8** that those who believe, God foreknew. That same foreknowledge of believers. This is a conditional statement. It's not "God has not cast away His people," but His people that are saved.

And to make this point clear, Paul quotes Elijah, who was cursing Israel for their unbelief and seeking the prophet's life. God's reply to Elijah is that there was a remnant of Israel who were saved by faith, who had no bent the knee to Baal. Who were still faithful.

By comparing his present time to Elijah's, Paul deliberately specifies that there is a remnant, just as he himself is a remnant, according to the election of grace.

That is, a chosen people by grace, believers. Even of the Jews at that present time, as he himself is proof of.

*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

With this aside, Paul lays the final nail in the coffin of the idea of works based salvation. The election of grace is to the glory of God, boasting excluded. Unmerited, but accessed by faith, as we have shown in earlier chapters.

teachings.title: John 6 does not support Calvinism
teachings.summary: Shows from John 6 and John 12 that all men are drawn but not all believe, so the passage does not teach election of individuals to salvation.
teachings.text:
BTW John 6 does not support Calvanism. 

For we know that it is ALL who will be drawn. But not all believe. 

*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw **all** men unto me.*

**John 6**
*43 Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.

44 No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.

45 It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me.

46 Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father.

47 Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.

48 I am that bread of life.

49 Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead.

50 This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.

51 I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.*

The life of the world. Believe.

teachings.title: Joint heirs with Christ, not with Jews
teachings.summary: Believers are adopted sons and joint heirs with Christ, while unbelieving Jews in the flesh cannot please God and have no claim to the promise.
teachings.text:
Paul is transitioning from the previous arguments, to build upon them that salvation is by faith. By the Spirit and not the words or by the deeds of the flesh. But again, in contrasting the law of the flesh with the law of faith, Paul shows how the promises and inheritance are to those that believe. That believers are adopted sons of God, crying Abba, Father. That the Spirit itself bears witness to this adoption. That we are the children of God, and those without Christ are none of His.

We are heirs of God, joint-heirs with Christ. Not co-religionists with Jews. Not co-heirs with them. But with Christ. And unbelieving Jews have no claim to the promise.

Unbelieving Jews living by the law of the flesh die after the flesh. It is only by the Spirit of Christ that the deeds of the body are mortified, made dead. To no effect. Because we live, made alive by the Spirit.

But Jews are dead in their flesh. Not of His. Not children of God having not the Spirit of adoption. Not heirs of God or co-heirs with Christ, because they reject Him. They are carnal. They have the spirit of bondage. They are of the flesh.

*So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.*

Similar to **Hebrews 11:6**;
*But without faith it is impossible to please him...*

The unregenerate Jews are of the flesh and have not faith. They cannot please God. The Bible says it is impossible. The wrath abides on them to the uttermost.

But the dispensationalist will say they will come to believe. They will come to faith in the end. "God isn't through with His people."

And yet the same dispensationalism they profess claims they will be reinstituting the works of the law. The sacrifices and the ordinances, which we know is the ministration of death. It is the law of the flesh, and by this law it is impossible to please God.

The contradiction of their heresy cannot stand up to the scrutiny of the word. *Let God be true and every man a liar.*

teachings.title: Abraham justified by faith, not circumcision
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before circumcision, so the promise comes by faith and fleshly Jews have no claim on the Abrahamic covenant apart from Christ.
teachings.text:
Building upon the conclusions reached in Chapter 3, we see in **Romans 4**, Paul uses scripture to flesh out the ideas and demonstrate the truth of his argument. The veil lifted, so that by the reading of Moses a believer may understand God's word.

He begins with the understanding that Abraham was not justified by his works or by circumcision, but by his faith. Abraham believed God and it was counted for righteousness.

And when Abraham believed, it was decades before the institution of the carnal ordinance of circumcision. A practice giving an outward sign for the continuation of the people chosen to bear Abraham's seed, which is Christ.

While **Romans 4** is frequently cited to demolish the heretical argument that we are saved in any capacity by our own works, it is primarily an argument against the Judaizers who think to themselves to say they have Abraham as their father.

But as John the Baptist says in **Matthew 3:9**;

*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It wasn't circumcision that saved Abraham, but faith. It wasn't even his willingness to sacrifice Isaac. All the great works of faith by Abraham may be reason to glory among men, but not before God. They may be reckoned for reward out of debt, but not of grace which is freely given to those who believe, to the glory of God.

As David wrote, Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Those who do no works, but have believed on Christ, that faith is counted for righteousness.

It is an accounting. The only thing that is reckoned for forgiveness of sin and salvation from death, is faith.

And so, if this blessing came by faith and not circumcision, there is no profit in circumcision.

And if the righteousness of Abraham came by faith, there is no profit in being able to call Abraham your father after the flesh.

The promise of God, that through his seed all nations shall be blessed, and that seed should be made heir to the whole world, was not made to Abraham, or to his seed through the law. Meaning his physical descendants, who under the law are inheritors.

The promise to be made heir was through the righteousness of faith.

This excludes unconditionally any claim Jews would have on the Abrahamic covenant, except by faith in Christ.

*For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect*

If dispensationalist Zionism were true, that by the law Jews are heirs to Abraham's promise, *then faith is made void and the promises made of none effect.*

Saved Christians who believe that Jews are the inheritors by this promise, are like Esau, selling the promise for pottage. Despising their inheritance.

teachings.title: No replacement, only the covenant to all nations
teachings.summary: Jew and Gentile alike are saved only by faith with imputed righteousness, so there is no replacement theology and no other dispensation, only the covenant to Abraham for all nations.
teachings.text:
So, in 4 chapters we see that there is no difference between Jew and Gentile, all are under sin, all condemned, with the law or without.

We see that all who are saved from that condemnation are saved by faith in the blood of Christ Jesus. By believing God's promise. By the imputed righteousness of Jesus, our own sins are not counted against us. Without works. Not by the law. Not by circumcision. Not by being physical heirs of Abraham, but spiritual heirs in faith.

There is no replacement theology, only the continuation of the covenant made to Abraham, which is to all nations.

There was no other dispensation given. There is no future dispensation to be had.

teachings.title: A trail of blood of believers
teachings.summary: Saved believers stand in an unbroken line of faith, bearing fruit after its kind from Abel through the apostles to today, linked by a trail of martyrs' blood persecuted by Rome and the false church.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 1:11**
*And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.*

**Matthew 21:43**
*Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.*

Matthew 7:16-18
*Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.*

**Philippians 1**:**4-11**
*Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace. For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ. And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment; That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ. Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.*

**Romans 1:16-17**
*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.*

I am a saved Christian. Born again by the faith that was shared to me by another saved Christian, who in turn believed and was converted by yet another saved. Christian. A line of succession going back to the beginning of the world. That the just live by faith and bear fruit after its own kind.

A line of believers stretching back to Adam. To Abel. To Seth and Enos.

The same faith of Abraham who believed the Lord and it was counted upon him for righteousness. The same faith that makes up the record of the "Hall of faith," in Hebrews chapter 11.

The same faith preached by John, the Baptist in the wilderness, taught by Christ Himself during His earthly ministry, given to the apostles as the keys to overcome death and hell. Preached on the day of Pentecost. Given to the Jews and to the Greek. The salvation that is by calling upon the name of the Lord. By believing on the finished work of Christ Jesus as the propitiation of our sin.

And, like the blood of the prophets from Abel to Zechariah, and of Jesus and the Apostles, and of the believers persecuted by the Jews and the Romans, a trail of blood that links believing Christians today to those that were martyred for the same faith in the same Gospel of grace and reconciliation. A trail of blood that continued through the persecution by Constantine's cult, through the dark ages, during the Reformation, under Bloody Mary, and that will mark the great tribulation to come.

teachings.title: Lot and the Corinthians: sanctification does not decide who is saved
teachings.summary: Explains sanctification and separation as service for edifying the brethren, and shows from Lot in 2 Peter 2 and Paul's greeting in 1 Corinthians 1 that sinning believers are still called saints and righteous.
teachings.text:
The point of sanctification and discipleship is to edify the brethren and the point of separation is to be more useful to God in winning souls and being a blessing to others by being blameless and as much as possible, peaceful with all men. 

If you have been blessed to be able to devote more time and more energy to the word, to winning souls and ministering to the faithful as a servant of God, healing the broken hearted with the baptism of faith in Christ, rather than hold it as a standard of piety like a hypocrite, use the opportunity to bear fruit with gladness, longsuffering and patience and receive those weaker in the faith that they can, by your ministering, be disciples that they may do great things for the Lord.

**2 Peter 2:6-8**
*And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

Just Lot, that righteous man, with a righteous soul, who is celebrated in the New Testament by God as such, dwelt among the filth in ACTUAL SODOM, the most wicked city ever to exist, where there was only one just man. 

But some yahoo with a works salvation false gospel is going to call Lot a "believer" with scare quotes, and imply he is less saved somehow, less of a "Christian" because he had to be physically carried out of Sodom by angels, while another guy has a double wide on a hobby farm and so he's more righteous somehow. 

Hypocrites.

**1 Corinthians 1:1-9**
*Paul called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both their's and our's: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ; That in every thing ye are enriched by him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge; Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you: So that ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall also confirm you unto the end, that ye may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Paul is writing to the church of God in Corinth, to those who are called to believe saints, who received grace of God through Christ, and peace with the Lord, sanctified in Him, and Who shall confirm them unto the end; eternal life.

He says that they are blameless in Christ. That being confirmed unto the end, he is assuring them that they are once saved, always saved. The testimony of Christ confirmed in them. 

Paul is writing this epistle with *Sosthenes our brother*, the same Sosthenes who, in Acts 18 accused Paul before the Roman magistrate Gallio, the deputy of Achaia, Because *Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.*

Sosthenes was Crispus' replacement as chief ruler of the synagogue, and when he brought Paul before the deputy to accuse him, Gallio ignored him and the Greeks beat the rabbi. 

The next time we see him, Paul is calling him a brother in Christ. He's recorded in this epistle as the scribe for the Apostle. 

Really consider all of this, and then understand the context of why Paul is writing to them, to chastise them for multiple sins and divisions. Pride and even fornication amongst them, worse than even the heathens. A list of sins he calls them out for. 

Paul, who persecuted the fledgling churches, helping to kill the saints, dictating to a man who was once the chief Rabbi in the synagogue of Corinth and who had accused Paul trying unsuccessfully to have him punished by the government, to a church full of divisions and boasting, a man sleeping with his stepmother, and all kinds of other issues in the church....

.... And he opens it with that greeting!. 

Go read it again. 

He doesn't question their salvation. He doesn't make them doubt it. He reaffirms the gospel by which they've testified, and through which they've received the grace of God and been called to be saints. Who were not lacking spiritual gifts. 

Really makes you think. 

Really puts things into perspective, especially when you have someone claiming to be a man of God, berating believers as being insufficiently pure enough for him. Who don't meet his standards. Questioning their salvation when he himself preaches a false gospel.

Hypocrite.

teachings.title: Repentance from false beliefs about God
teachings.summary: What people most often repent of is not their sins but their false beliefs about God, His judgment and their own righteousness, turning from dead works and believing the gospel.
teachings.text:
And this ties into the renewed theme of the week; repentance.

The thing most people "repent of" isn't their sins. Most people know sin is bad and hate it and don't like themselves for it. These Jews in Jerusalem for the fast knew in their hearts they were in sin, just as people do today. They have a conscience and the Spirit convicting them, least they be reprobate.

What people most often repent of are the false beliefs they have about God. About His  judgment. About their own righteousness or how they can escape punishment for their sins.

"Oh I thought idols would save me."
"I thought the law would save me."
