"I thought maybe hell wasn't real."
"I didn't know my works weren't enough."

It's literally what they are being called to repentance from in NT scripture. The Jews thinking by their being Abraham's seed they were going to inherit the kingdom no matter what. That they could achieve their own righteousness by works of the law and keeping the traditions of men. That the Kingdom of Heaven was theirs on this earth. That the Messiah would be political. A man of war. That circumcision availed them.

The Greeks believed their dead idols and false gods, that they superstitiously bowed to and served, would save them. That God wasn't real. They worshipped the created more than the Creator who is blessed forever, amen.

Jews and Greeks alike didn't believe Jesus was the Christ. They sought a sign, and wisdom. But the power to be saved was in the word of God. The Gospel preached and believed. Repentance from dead works and vain traditions and towards God. Reconsidering the way to the Kingdom of Heaven, and believing.

Just as in Jeremiah's day. Just as it is today.

teachings.title: The reprobate doctrine in the old and new IFB
teachings.summary: Says the old IFB and the new IFB teach the same reprobate doctrine, that God's offer of salvation is not available forever, so believe now.
teachings.text:
The OIFB taught the Reprobate Doctrine, focusing more on before God gives up on somebody, the NIFB focuses more on the consequences of after. But it is the same doctrine from the same Bible and says the same thing; God's offer of salvation is not available to all men forever. There comes a time when it is too late, reprobate! 

So don't delay, don't put it off. Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and be saved.

*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, And in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation*.

teachings.title: Metanoia: repentance is a change of mind toward God
teachings.summary: Explains the word translated repentance as a change of mind and heart toward God and belief, and argues that adding "of sin" came with modern versions.
teachings.text:
*Metanoia*, the Greek word translated in our King James Bible as "repentance," is a changing of the mind. “Meta” comes from the root for “after” or “beyond,” while “noeo” is “to think.” So metanoeo means to reconsider or to rethink something. At its root, repentance is about changing one's mind. 'Metanoia' literally means to 'change your mind, to change direction' …has nothing to do with guilt or shame. 

So, when John the Baptist calls his audience to repent, he is telling them to understand the Kingdom is at hand and to have a thorough change of heart and mind regarding salvation and the coming Christ. To reconsider and believe. To be convicted in the Spirit. To turn towards God. 

This has always been its meaning and no one changed it until modern Bible versions in the 20th century began to append "..of sin" and delete the instances of God's repentance, to begin pushing the Devil's favorite damnable heresy, works salvation. 

That's why in scripture, again and again, repentance and belief are used in tandem to express conversion, by believing on Jesus and receiving the gift of eternal life promised by God. 

This is the Gospel of the Bible and how men have been saved from the time of Seth. The notion that it was changed or twisted in the 1980s to something other than that is not only biblically and linguistically wrong, it is absurd.

" In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Feel bad about sinning and try not to sin: for the kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

Hey that sounds like works...

teachings.title: Judaizers bringing the free back into bondage
teachings.summary: As Judah took back the servants they had freed, false teachers and works salvationists seek to bring those set at liberty in Christ back under the yoke of the law and the traditions of men.
teachings.text:
Just as the Jews of Jeremiah's day, there are Judaizers, who seek to turn those the Lord has sought to set at liberty, to return and be brought into subjection, to be servants and handmaids. To return to bondage.

Literally, during this siege of Judah. Spiritually now, in the time of the reformation, whereby we are set free, at liberty in Christ.

And God witnesses this and promises their swift destruction.

**2 Peter 2:1**
*But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction.*

Just as God slew and put in chains the people of Judah who refused to allow their servants the liberty their lord commanded, even while beset by armies and with the preaching of destruction in their ears, they couldn't let go of the power they had over brethren. So too, false teachers knowing the judgment of God and the fires of Hell that will await them, cannot help but try and bring those set at liberty back under their thumb.

Ultimately, works salvationists are seeking to control people. To be the arbiter of their freedoms. To decide who, in their carnal mind, is worthy or righteous, so that they can condemn everyone who follows them. It's wicked as Hell.

And the works of the law, commandments of men and vain traditions they seek to yoke people to is not of God, who would that all men be free in Christ.

teachings.title: Eternal security and salvation by faith alone
teachings.summary: States that those who deny eternal security or salvation by faith alone are perishing, and offers John 6 and Romans 8 as the proof of the believer kept.
teachings.text:
If you don't believe in the eternal security of salvation, or that you're saved by faith alone and given the gift of eternal life through the grace of God, then you are perishing and you are going to go to hell.

John 6:39-40 
*And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may **have** **everlasting** **life**: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**Romans 8:38-39**
*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

teachings.title: Sanctification is not justification: works that bless others
teachings.summary: Distinguishes sanctification and discipleship from justification, noting that works God leads believers to are a blessing to others and that fruit inspectors who judge them are not walking in love.
teachings.text:
People who conflate sanctification and discipleship with justification, or take a calvanist view of discipleship, that says you *will* show works, almost always they mean personal works of self-improvement. That you clean up your life or you're not saved. 

And the ironic thing is that those saved by Christ alone, not of anything we've done in the flesh, and who walk in the spirit know that the works God brings us to aren't of ourselves. They're almost always a blessing for others. Most you don't even realize you've done and few people if any recognize it, beyond maybe the person you helped. It is in these acts that we come to grow in love, and the thorns of our heart that leads us to sin are removed. 

But that's a personal choice to choose separation and doesn't affect a person's salvation. 

Hypocritical fruit inspectors never gain that spirit of love from being blessings to others because they are always comparing themselves to others, to justify themselves before men and God. Being holier than thou makes you resent and look down on others. Not love them. 

And so, they aren't used of God, they aren't even saved. The good acts they do or the leaf they turned over are in vain. Filthy rags. And the thorns of their heart remain. Their later end is worse.

teachings.title: Repent: behave, or believe?
teachings.summary: Asks whether Jesus' call to repent in Matthew 4:17 means cleaning up one's act or believing that salvation is at hand, to fit the gospel of grace.
teachings.text:
Here's one. (Assuming you denounce works salvation, and believe it is by grace through faith alone, sealed unto redemption)

**Matthew 4:17**
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.*

Would Jesus be telling the Jews of the gospel of grace by say to them "**Behave**, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand," *or* "**Believe**, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand?" 

Which way of saying it fits the gospel? 

Would He be telling Jews to clean up their acts, or to believe they need salvation, and that that salvation, promised by God, was at hand?

teachings.title: The sabbath rest and spring feasts picture Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath rest pictures salvation by Christ's finished work rather than ours, and the spring feasts were fulfilled in Christ's death, resurrection and Pentecost.
teachings.text:
Now we are here in Leviticus chapter 23, and in it God provides the basic terms of the sabbaths and holy days to be kept by the children of Israel.

Understanding that sabbaths means rest, and that the prohibition of doing work on the sabbath is a picture of Christ Jesus, and the rest we enter into in Him. That we are saved by the rest given to us by the Lord and not our own works. That if a child of Israel works on these days, he is cut off, just as anyone trusting in their works for salvation is likewise cut off from the Kingdom of God. It is an undeniable truth that is repeated over and over again throughout the Bible, from the creation through Revelation. We are saved by Christ's perfect work, not our own. Not by being a "good person" or contrite or "trying to avoid sin" or how well we make "Jesus the Lord of our life."

Jesus paid it all in full, and the Spring feasts of Passover, unleavened bread and Pentecost all serve as ordinances to the Isralites as a picture of Christ.

I covered much of this in the Gospel studies, recently in [a study of Luke](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9753).

It is fascinating and amazing how God set this before the people and thousands of years later, we see it pay off with Jesus, the Passover lamb, slain on a sabbath, in Hell for 3 days and nights, all sabbaths, and risen again, only to ascend into Heaven on Pentecost, the feast of the first fruits held 50 days after Passover. The day in which the disciples went out to the multitude of gathered Jews preaching the Gospel in every tongue. The 5,000 saved that day being the first fruits of the spring harvest.

teachings.title: Liberty from sin to walk in the Spirit
teachings.summary: Salvation by grace without works frees believers to be sanctified by the Spirit, which is why faithful Baptist churches bear the fruit of separated lives.
teachings.text:
This is the practical application of the law, and the spiritual application for those of us at liberty from sin in Christ, we see the pattern of what is right in God's eyes, that we may be sanctified by Him through the Spirit.

Because of the weakness of the flesh and the failing of sinful man, we need a savior. We need Christ, and through the grace of God, we are given Jesus to do what we couldn't. That by faith in Him we have remission of sin and peace with God. And in that peace, paid for entirely by the blood of Jesus, we can then be sanctified by the Spirit.

We are to standfast in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free. Not being entangled again with the yoke of bondage. Our unrighteousness done away with by the grace of God to His glory. His mercy being a revelation from Heaven through we who are saved that others may see and come to the knowledge of the truth, and repent towards God. Believing on Christ, to be set at liberty as well.

Despite some, who have crept in privily to spy out liberty, and who slanderously report that we say "let us do evil..." The liberty we have from sin, the blessing that God will not impute sin to us, is to allow us to then walk in the spirit and not fulfill the lusts of the flesh. To strive for the mark that God calls us towards, that we may be conformed to His use, that His will be done. That we be sanctified. That we be holy because He is holy. And in that sanctification, we can bring others to Christ, being a light unto the world as Israel was to be to other nations.

This is why, if we take an honest look at those who preach salvation by grace through faith, without works, without depending on our own selves to turn from sin, or change our lives, or "make Jesus our Lord," but by acknowledging the truth of God, we see so many who are living for God today.

We see those set free in Christ turning from sin, walking in the Spirit, doing great things for the Lord. Not sanctification to gain justification, but sanctification to become vessels fit for His use. That we may be blameless before men. That we may be justified before men, who may say, as in **James 2**, show me your faith by your works. That we may lead others to the truth.

And so, you see independent fundamental Baptist churches that are soul winning, studying to be approved, comparing that which they received with scripture to see if it is so. Engaged in the edification of the local church and reaching out to the poor, the brokenhearted, that they may find peace with God.

Fundamentalist Baptists are often the most separated, actually allowing the Spirit to work effectually in them to remove thorns from their hearts, and to feed the new man, starving the flesh.

This is not to say all Baptists or even a majority of Baptist churches are perfect. This is not to say that just by being Baptist, you become justified or holier than anyone else, or that only a Baptist Church can achieve this.

But the fruit of the more stedfast Baptist churches is undeniably a more separated people doing great works for the Lord.

teachings.title: Lordship salvation is a false gospel
teachings.summary: Requiring people to make Jesus Lord of their life or repent of their sins to be saved makes man his own savior and is another gospel.
teachings.text:
Lordship salvation is a false doctrine, put forth by vipers that say you have to "make Jesus the Lord of your life," or "boss of your life," in order to be saved. That you have to "repent of your sins" and try to "avoid sin," or you cannot be saved.

This is wicked as Hell.

To be saved we must understand that we are sinners and incapable of justifying ourselves to God. This is only part of accepting salvation, and part of Biblical repentance that is taught in nearly all independent fundamentalist Baptist churches. It is a part of the truth we must believe to actually trust on Christ for our salvation.

But the idea that our salvation rests in any way with our ability to turn from sin makes the person their own savior, robs the glory of God, and puts Christ to an open shame.

People who are giving a false gospel that includes "turning from your sin" or making Jesus the "boss of your life," are false teachers and are bringing another gospel.

Jesus is Lord, and God sits on His throne whether you believe or not. Whether you backslide or whether you go soul winning and Bible reading daily and attending church 3 times a week.

The humility and humbling of ourselves comes from the recognition that we are sinners, deserving death and Hell. Our salvation is in accepting that Jesus died for us, and we are washed clean in the blood. Not in how well we strive to live a perfect sinless life.

teachings.title: The Romans Road gospel presentation
teachings.summary: The Romans Road with John 3:16 uses scripture to explain simply that all have sinned, Christ died for us, and whosoever believes and calls on the Lord is saved.
teachings.text:
*For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on him shall not perish, but have everlasting life.*

*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;*

*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one*

*Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned*

*For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.*

*That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.*

*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

This is the "Roman's Road," a short but direct use of scripture taken from the epistle to the Romans, as well as **John 3:16**, the most recognized verse in the Bible, and used by evangelists to win souls to the Lord for generations. It uses the word of God to explain the simple Gospel of salvation, that by hearing, a person may believe unto righteousness.

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

It is not the only means of giving the Gospel, but it is one of the most effective. It covers all the bases. Many times we may have to turn to other scripture to overcome objections or questions, but for the average person this is sufficient to explain Biblical salvation.

God loves the world and gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on him shall not perish, but have eternal life. Everlasting.

That we need salvation because we all sin. That the punishment for sin is death and Hell. But the gift of God is eternal life in His Son. That while we are sinners, Christ still died for us. That if we believe this in our hearts and trust on God's promise, calling upon His holy name, we will be saved.

That's the Gospel.

teachings.title: The remnant of Israel and the false gospel of Zionists
teachings.summary: Uses 1 Kings 19:18 to show that in Old Testament days only a remnant of Israel was saved by grace through faith, answering the claim that all of fleshly Israel will be saved in Romans 11.
teachings.text:
**1 Kings 19:18**
*Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.*

The dispensationalist Zionists who claim to be Christian but offer a false gospel for Jews, and another for Gentiles, Make it out as if when Paul writes, *all of Israel shall be saved* that he's talking about Israel of the flesh. 

But as we see under the Old Testament, There were periods where of the millions of Israelites, there were as few as 7,000 people who had called upon the name of the Lord for salvation and were saved by grace through faith. 

The strait is the gate in narrow the way and few there are the find it.

teachings.title: Confession: admitting our sin before God
teachings.summary: No one can be saved without confessing they are a sinner, and pride against confession is what drives people to works religion and false priestly confession.
teachings.text:
*And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing*.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*

Confession, the act of admitting guilt, of revealing your own faults and iniquities, is a fundamental act of humility in the Christian life. It is the realization that leads to repentance towards the Gospel, the understanding that yes, we have sinned before God and His standards are just and right, for He is holy, and we ask for mercy and salvation knowing in our hearts that we deserve death, for we have earned it. The wages of sin.

A soul that sins and doesn't confess their trespass to God, can't avail themselves of the sacrifice. You can't get saved without this acknowledgment. You can't accept salvation without knowing you need to be saved.

And as we covered in Romans; all men know. By the wrath of God revealed from heaven upon the ungodly. By the conviction of the holy Spirit, reproving the world. By the conscience we have, the law written in our hearts. So that we have no excuse. Everyone knows.

But few confess.

It is humiliating to be found out. It is one of the first sins we commit affirmatively, lying about something we have done. We seek to avoid punishment, but more so, our pride has us seek to avoid being exposed. Especially since so many sins are petty and embarrassing. Coveting. Lusts. All come from selfish and disgusting places. Admission that we aren't "good" is a hard nut to crack.

This pride and dishonesty, lying about sin to God, to others, even lying to ourselves, is the biggest stumbling block to accepting the Gospel.

Either a person will deny that God is real, that His judgments are right, that they aren't absolved by technicality, that the Bible doesn't *really* say that.

*Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?*

It is that lie that Satan uses to tempt us, from Eve on. And like Adam and Eve, hiding in the bushes from God, covering their sin with their own works, blaming someone else, even blaming God, as Adam did, we see the cope humans will cling to to avoid that humiliation of confession. Even before the eyes of God, in His presence.

This pride against confession is what draws people to a works-based false religion.

The idea that they are "good people" because they keep ordinances and receive sacraments, even the false half-hearted "confession" to a "priest," being absolved not by faith but by vain repetitions of prayer, given as punishment.

People seek to be absolved in any way possible short of actually acknowledging their sin.

And we see in our study of Leviticus, God provided the framework in the law that if anyone could follow it without falling short, they could theoretically be saved. It is the ultimate works religion, the only one God endorsed, and He did it to show that we need salvation in Christ. That all will fall short.

Even in the paradise of Eden, with one commandment only, man sinned.

We are given the law as a schoolmaster to bring us to the understanding that we need Jesus. And by the law, the understanding that to receive Christ we have to admit we need saving. That our righteousness is as filthy rags. That we sin, and God's judgment is just and right.

And so we must confess we are guilty under the law to be saved, and once saved, we confess our sins that God may work through the Spirit indwelling us to remove those thorns in our hearts.

We study the scriptures, and often learn that things we have done in the past were actually sinful. And like the Hebrews, once we have that knowledge we need to confess and seek atonement in faith through the Lord.

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.*

teachings.title: There is no liberty outside of Christ
teachings.summary: True liberty comes only from salvation in Christ, not from any constitution, and only God blesses a nation through those who keep the faith.
teachings.text:
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage*.

This 4th of July, Independence Day, remember that the blessings of liberty come from the liberty found in Christ. There is no liberty outside of Christ.

It isn't an abstraction that can be grasped and measured. It isn't a concept to be understood and maintained in a secular setting. It has no meaning without the Gospel, the beautiful law of Liberty.

*But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.*

America secured the blessings of liberty through the faith of the founding stock. Not their masters. Not their king, not in the men that replaced him. Not in their documents. It isn't to be found in the Constitution. No parchment has or can grant liberty, or the blessings that come from it. Only salvation by grace through faith in Christ Jesus can.

And only God may bless those who maintain the faith and live it out, regardless of where or when.

And those blessings that abound to the faithful can continue and grow to the benefit of everyone in their nation, regardless of their faith. But the only way to secure those blessings is in the Lord;

*Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.*

teachings.title: The word is nigh thee
teachings.summary: Salvation is simply confessing Jesus as Lord and believing God raised Him, with no works or sacraments, so we must preach it.
teachings.text:
And so, Paul using Deuteronomy, familiar scripture to the believing Jews receiving his epistle to the churches at Rome, shows that the receiving of the law through Moses was the understanding of Christ.

And that understanding of Christ is put into one of the most beautiful passages of scripture, testifying to the salvation that is by faith on Jesus, and the truth of the nature of the Gospel.

*But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

That's the simplicity of the Gospel. That's all of the law of faith. This is the righteousness of God that we obtain through Christ by faith, summed up. Complete.

There is no other way to Him except by this. There are no works, no special boy status, no secret traditions, ordinances, sacraments or other deeds of the law. And knowing this, then we must preach this glad tiding, this good news, that others may by the power of God's word, hear, believe and confess unto salvation.

*How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!*

teachings.title: Predestinated in Christ, not chosen to believe
teachings.summary: Predestination in Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 is in Christ, not God choosing who will believe, since God will have all men to be saved and draws all men, so Calvinism and limited atonement are doctrines of devils rooted in pride.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 1:3-6**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved*.

So what is this that is predestined? The saved? Or Christ Jesus by whom we are saved?

Calvinists read this and **Romans 8**, and place the emphasis on themselves, rather than Christ, and so, they claim, that God picks who will believe. This doctrine of devils, like all false gospels, is based on putting themselves before the Lord. Just as works salvation is predicated on the person's own righteousness, not Christ's, the special boy doctrine makes it that they are the elect, not of Jesus perfect work, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world, that all who believe on Him will be saved, but by God's "sovereign will."

But we know that God's will is not for a chosen few.

**1 Timothy 2:3-4**
*For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.*

If God exerted His sovereign will, we would all be saved.

As Jesus says,

*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

Every one.

Limited atonement is a doctrine of devils. It is based on pride.

So we know that all who believe are predestinated in Christ that they will have eternal life, sealed by the Spirit, and if they walk in tha Spirit, will be conformed to the use of God, that we may become separated, to be servants of the Gospel.

And so continuing the theme of Romans 8, the context of which is the works of the Spirit.

That while we are yet in the flesh, knowing the day of redemption will free us from that wretched state, that the Spirit helps heal our infirmities that led us to sin and conforms us to His will, so long as we walk after the Spirit, not feeding the flesh with the things of this world. That the Spirit within us acts also as an intercessor to bring our needs before the Father, so that His will be done in us.

And so, the good news;

*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

Who is called? Who is drawn to faith in God's promise?

**John 12:32-33**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me. This he said, signifying what death he should die.*

All men. But few will answer this call, and seek to be transformed to fulfill His intended purpose for us. The harvest is great but the laborers few. Strait is the gate and narrow the way and few there be that find it. Every name of every person born of water upon this earth is in the book of life. But their names are stricken from it when they die in sin, unbelieving. (Or reprobates, twice-dead)

No where in the Bible do we see names added, only erased. God's foreknowledge, knowing of the end from the beginning, means He knows who will answer the call. It doesn't mean He selects them.

teachings.title: O wretched man that I am
teachings.summary: False prophets use Romans 7 to teach repent-of-your-sins works salvation or sinless living, but they deceive themselves and produce only fruit-inspecting hypocrites.
teachings.text:
*O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?*

Some false prophets use Romans 7 to teach a works-based, repent of your sins salvation. They use similar verses to teach that if you have sin you aren't saved. They will even claim they themselves are without sin.

**1 John 1:8**
*If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.*

**Revelation 22**
*But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.*

These people are vipers. They have a false gospel. They produce no fruit, just bitter people unable to ever come to perfection, and trusting in their own works to save them.

Or worse, they make hypocrites, "fruit inspectors," who spend their time being holier than thou and touting their own righteousness, and glorying in their separation, but who never do the actual works of the spirit. Who can't win someone to Christ. At best, if they believed at one point, they create nothing but wood, hay and stubble.

But most aren't believers and just bring filthy rags before the judgment seat of Christ, saying *Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?*

And He will say to them, depart from me I never knew you.

teachings.title: The wages of sin and the gift of God
teachings.summary: Eternal life is a gift not a wage, and the saved, made servants of righteousness, earn rewards judged by fire at the judgment seat while never losing salvation.
teachings.text:
*Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.*

We are free to serve God being pardoned by His grace. To work for righteousness, as its servant out of love for Him that justified the ungodly, while we were yet sinners.

We who deserved death now are servants of life, unto God and should act like it. Note also in his appeal to walk in the new man, we are never told that we should lose the grace we standfast in. Rather, that we have our fruit unto holiness and the end everlasting life. We now earn rewards in the kingdom heaven, vs earning the wages of sin which is death.

*For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Gift vs wage. We do not earn gifts. A wage is debt owed. In sin, our debt is paid by death and hell, but in Christ we are given grace, a free gift, salvation and liberty that we may serve Him. And in that service we earn holiness, towards the righteousness of God, rewards.

**1 Corinthians 3:9-15**
*For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We see here that as laborers for God, working as husbandmen in His vineyard, servants of His righteousness, that we will be judged as laborers, and earn rewards for our works. Each deed we do that is built up on the foundation of Christ will be judged by fire, and those of no spiritual importance will burn like wood, hay and stubble, but those of lasting impact, especially the salvation of souls, will be manifest as gold, silver and precious stones. And though some of our effort is burned by fire, as a loss, not being of real value, we ourselves are still saved, yet so as by fire. The same fire that reveals the fruit of our labors will be to us who believe a refining fire, but to them without hope, destruction in eternal torment.

*For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.*

God repays. Be it the wages of sin with death or rewards in the kingdom to come.

teachings.title: Their throat is an open sepulchre
teachings.summary: Romans 3 and Psalm 14 show that none is righteous and that false teachers, like the Pharisees, devour people with a deadly false gospel.
teachings.text:
And so, Paul is writing to the churches in Rome, many of the congregation are saved Jews, surrounded by reprobate pagan excess and put upon by Pharisees among their own people.

He established that the Gentiles were beholden to the same Creator. He established that the law wasn't sufficient to save the Jew. He established that all are under sin.

And so we begin to get to the meat of things.

*There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.*
*They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

This is quoting **Psalm 14**;

*The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good. The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, and seek God. They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one. Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread, and call not upon the Lord. There were they in great fear: for God is in the generation of the righteous. Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the Lord is his refuge.*

*Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! when the Lord bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.*

The workers of iniquity, those whose *mouths are an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lip*; those teaching men false doctrines, their words are like the stench of death, of an open grave, because that is what their false gospel brings. It is poison.

They eat the people up as bread, that they don't call upon the name of the Lord and be saved.

This should sound familiar.

**Matthew 23**;
*14 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.*

*15 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.*

*16 Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!*

*17 Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?*

*18 And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.*

*19 Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?*

*20 Whoso therefore shall swear by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon.*

*21 And whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.*

*22 And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.*

*23 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.*

*24 Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.*

*25 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.*

*26 Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.*

*27 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.*

*28 Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.*

*29 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,*

teachings.title: Reprobation and the false gospel of repenting of sins
teachings.summary: Argues that denying the reprobate doctrine leaves Christians unable to explain or guard against open reprobates, and ties that denial to a works gospel that makes salvation depend on reforming oneself.
teachings.text:
The lack of understanding regarding reprobation, and the rejection by God of those who make the truth of God into a lie, is why modern Christians are ill-equiped to deal with the threat of sodomites.  (And I mean saved believers, not just apostates calling themselves Christian. Obviously the false churches can't resist the devil because they are of him)

If you don't believe that sodomites are that way because they have been given up, given over, cursed by God, abominations, conscience seared, never able to come to the knowledge of the truth, fit to be burned, plucked up by the roots, dogs and swine, hard hearted and proud, haters of God, sons of Beliel...then you can't explain who they are and how they behave, identify their threat and defend your family and communities from them. 

You will always be open to their creeping in unawares to lead people to damnation. You will always find excuses for them, because of your hope they may "repent." Ultimately, the denial of the reprobate doctrine is rooted in misplaced empathy and our fleshly nature being contrary to the judgment of God. It's the same impulse as the Pitbull Moms.

This is the evil fruit of the corrupt tree that is the false gospel of "Repent of your sins"-works salvation. The idea that anyone can be saved if they can "repent," or rather reform themselves, turn over a new leaf, clean up their act.

It brings people to believe that regardless of the nature of man, it isn't God's grace that saves but rather being worthy for that salvation. They see their own righteousness as their salvation, and see their own prideful judgment of others, and tolerance for the wicked as a good work. And so, if a sodomite "changes" because these self-righteous "Christians" got them to "repent," they must be super-duper saved. It is hypocrisy and the pride of the holier than thou. 

"Oh, you don't have compassion and love for these poor sinners, the homosexual? You're not a very good Christian! Don't you know we are told to "Judge not," hmm?" It's pride and foolishness.

teachings.title: Jesus will judge every man by his works
teachings.summary: Christ will judge all by their works, the dead unto the lake of fire and the saved not for justification but for rewards in the kingdom.
teachings.text:
Jesus will judge every man for their works.

You heard me. The Lord Jesus Christ will judge every man according to his works.

*I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom.*

The dead, the unbelieving and disobedient.

**Revelation 20**
*11 And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.*

*12 And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.*

*13 And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works.*

*14 And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.*

*15 And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

The quick being those alive in Christ. Saved by faith in Him alone. And when we are judged, it isn't for our justification, Jesus paid that price for us. God extended His grace to us that our sins and iniquities are forgotten.

**Hebrews 10:17**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

**Psalm 103:12**
*As far as the east is from the west, So far hath he removed our transgressions from us.*

**Romans 3**
*23 For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;*

*24 Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:*

*25 Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;*

*26 To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

Amen.

But what about those works Jesus will judge, if it's not for justification, if it's not to be a propitiation for our sins so we don't have to pay the price of death and Hell, but have eternal life with Him, then why is He judging our works?

**1 Corinthians 3**
*9 For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building.*

*10 According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.*

*11 For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

*12 Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;*

*13 Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.*

*14 If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.*

*15 If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

God rewards us for our works in the Kingdom of God. He pays His laborers. He judges us by how we do His will. By the charity, the love we show others. By the edification of His congregation. The building up of those saved by the good news that Jesus paid our debt to the law that we may be alive in grace.

Amen

teachings.title: Thou hast the words of eternal life
teachings.summary: Peter understood that Christ's words, not literal flesh and blood, give eternal life, so those who teach literally eating Christ's body for salvation are not saved, and John 6 does not teach Calvinism.
teachings.text:
*Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will ye also go away? Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.*

So we see that Peter understood the lesson. Peter was saved by faith, speaks the truth of what Jesus was conveying; that Jesus has the words of eternal life. Not the literal flesh and blood to consume to obtain it, but the words that by faith grant the believer eternal life, because Jesus is the Christ, the son of the living God.

This teaching is an excellent way to separate the believer from those who aren't. Jesus uses it to divide, to alienate and offend those who don't understand the spiritual application because they are there to have their bellies filled, or to see wonders, not because they seek salvation.

This still applies today. People who take any sort of literal view of actually eating the body and drinking the blood of Jesus to gain salvation are not saved and have not come to the knowledge of the truth. They are not called according to God's will, because they aren't seeking to know or understand it.

Don't get that twisted, though. This isn't an appeal to Calvinism. Again, **John 6** is a stumbling block for the unbelieving who use the "called" to teach their limited atonement damnable heresy.

*For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

teachings.title: Today shalt thou be with me in paradise
teachings.summary: The thief on the cross shows salvation by faith alone, and Christ's promise of paradise shows He is God in heaven, not that He skipped Hell for a waiting room.
teachings.text:
We see the story of the thief on the cross, told again in Luke. The one mocking Jesus, the other recognizing His being Christ, calls upon His name, saying *Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.*

*And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.*

This is a beautiful example of salvation by faith, that even heretical cults that teach a salvation of works admit is an example of justification by faith alone. They claim it is an exemption, but it is the only way to salvation, offered to us as an example that there can be no doubt.

Others use the saying of Jesus to indicate that Jesus didn't die and go to Hell for 3 days and nights, but instead went to some waiting room in Hell called "paradise." This is contrary to scripture and to the very act with which we believe on for salvation. Jesus died for us. Jesus became sin for us. Death and Hell are the punishment for sin, and Jesus was the burnt offering, the substitution for ourselves, God's only begotten Son. Jehovahjireh.

What then?

Simply that Jesus is also God.

**John 3:11-13**
*Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things? And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven.*

The Son of man which **is** in heaven, is the same as the man Christ Jesus sitting before Nicodemus at that moment.

Jesus being fully God was also fully man. He was made flesh and dwelt among us. But He was always with God and was God.

*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.*

And so there is no great contradiction or doubtful disputation found in this verse. Paradise is Heaven and God is the God of the living. In death, is Hell.

*And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.*

teachings.title: False gospels of works and salvation by faith, not identity
teachings.summary: Warns that churches teaching a gospel of works are doing Satan's work however much they get right, and reminds that we are saved by faith in Christ as individuals, not by ethnicity, denomination or party.
teachings.text:
I often hear ecumenical people make a big deal about accepting all churches who call themselves "Christian." That we are wrong to point out that these denominations of men that bring a false gospel of works are not only as wicked as the atheists and the Jews, but even more wicked for how they mislead people. 

They say these churches "at least get some of it right" and expose people to Christ and the scriptures, and many like the Lutherans, even pay lip service to salvation by faith alone. So, they say, what is the harm? That we should fellowship with them and save our ire for non-Christians. 

But ultimately, all that bring a false gospel of works, that salvation is either bought or kept by our labors, and not a free gift given by God's grace, paid in full by Jesus' sacrifice, are doing the work of Satan. 

And being of Satan, they will inevitably seek to convince those fooled by their false doctrines into accepting reprobates into their congregation. Setting wolves among the sheep. 

And ultimately, having damned souls with heresy and exposed the innocent to the wicked to be their prey, and making them twofold more the child of Hell than themselves, they will exalt the antichrist when he comes, that those trusting in these religious leaders and their institutions of men will be deceived. 

It is the entire point of the false church of the Whore of Babylon and her harlot daughters. 

If this offends you or makes you angry, consider why. What are you trusting in to save your soul? What God tells us, faith in Christ who died for us and is risen? 

Or following vain traditions of men and your own filthy rags of self-righteousness? 

Is it your identity as a member of a denomination? Or your understanding of being a sinner, deserving death and Hell, spared by the mercy of a loving God?

We aren't saved by our identity. By who we think we are. There are no 'special boys.'

We aren't saved by our genetics, by our ethnicity, by our denomination, by our political ideology, or by the party we belong to. We aren't saved because of anything we do, or deserve. 

We are saved by faith, despite all that. 

We all have individual souls, and are saved or damned based on our free will choice to believe or not. Individual soul liberty. You as a person must believe in your heart that God's word is true. It's not something you can "fake it till you make it." It isn't something you gain from osmosis, being around others who are saved. 

No one can share of their oil, you must prepare your lamp yourself. 

Now nation, family, and all other collective bonds, ordained by God, with roles and responsibilities, are something you can love, cherish and support. But not in place of Jesus and not above Jesus and certainly not as a means of receiving Jesus.

teachings.title: Ye are they which justify yourselves before men
teachings.summary: The covetous Pharisees derided Jesus because they justified themselves by works before men, missing that the law and prophets were given to bring them to salvation in Christ.
teachings.text:
*And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.*

We see the transition here in chapter 16 of Luke, from Jesus addressing His disciples, to the Pharisees, who hearing His preaching, derided Him. They were covetous, the Bible says.

Covering means to resent those with something we lack coupled with the desire to possess that which isn't ours to have. Covetousness, which is idolatry according to scripture, is a sin because by its very nature shows a lack of gratitude towards God, and makes us bring evil towards our neighbors. Here the Pharisees are hearing Jesus preach on serving God rather than Mammon, not taking care for the things of this world, but rather laying up treasures in Heaven, and Luke, writing in the Spirit points out their covetousness. This preaching offends them. Preaching against sin brings two reactions in those that hear; conviction and repentance towards the truth or despising the messenger and the message, and doubling down in sin.

The Pharisees derided Jesus. Insulted Him. Called Him names and mocked His teachings, that had cut them to the quick.

And Jesus says to them; *Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.*

He says they follow the Law, but since John the Baptist and his preaching of the Kingdom and Christ's coming, the Law is not profitable, salvation is here.

They sought to be made justified by the works they did and the outward appearances they kept up, and by appealing to the justification before men, and when the Gospel of reconciliation is preached to them, where the praise of men matters not, but the humility and faith of a contrite heart towards God saves, they derided Him. They despised the gift.

Like Jesus said to His disciples in the previous verses, the Pharisees couldn't be trusted with the things of this world, they certainly won't be trusted for the things of the world to come.

Jesus says the Law and the prophets were to bring men to salvation when the kingdom of God is preached them. That they be fruit meet for repentance. The Law as a schoolmaster, the prophets giving witness.

Jesus says it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the Law to fail. This has a double meaning, that God's law is perfect and eternal, in its purpose until the kingdom is full and perfect, and the old heavens and earth are passed away. Burnt up.

But more, here, Jesus is saying how hard they cling to the letter of the law, despite their rejection of the kingdom nigh unto them, even as Heaven and earth pass away to make way for the Kingdom. It should have prepared these men to enter into it. Instead it has left them without. They are adulterous to the faith of the prophets. They missed the point of the Law they justified themselves by. They don't see the Christ before them, and missed the point that there are none righteous, no not one. All have come short of the Glory of God.

And so, Jesus tells these covetous and hypocritical "holy men" a parable, the story of Lazarus and the rich man.

We are introduced to a certain rich man. Often in Jesus preaching he uses "a certain man" to indicate someone who is a particular type of person, that we the audience would readily recognize and know. This certain man was rich, dressed in finery, and ate not just well, but sumptuously. We get the picture here, he is very rich. And by implication, someone when covetous Pharisees would see as one justified by the reckoning of man, the way they see themselves. An exaggerated version of their ideal, and in the context of their derision against His preaching on serving Mammon.

And Jesus contrasts this certain rich man with Lazarus, a poor beggar which was laid at the gate of the rich man seeking the crumbs that fell from his plate. Moreover, Lazarus was full of sores, suffering physically, humiliated by the dogs licked his open wounds. Dogs being unclean to the eyes of the Jews. A more pathetic figure couldn't be painted.

teachings.title: We are the elder son
teachings.summary: The prodigal son parable is addressed to the Pharisees as the resentful elder son, and many long-saved Christians likewise despise new converts and add works to the gospel of grace.
teachings.text:
Here in Luke chapter 15 we see that again, the Pharisees and scribes murmured amongst themselves, judging Jesus for the publicans and sinners that were drawn to hear His preaching. And again, Jesus shows them in parable that He is come to bring the lost sheep home. He has come to bring sinners to repentance towards God, not the righteous. A physician treats the sick.

And Jesus tells how much joy there is in Heaven when one sinner turns towards God that they may be saved. He offered the example of the lost sheep, and another of a lost piece of silver, and the rejoicing of those who had found what was lost, comparing that to God the Father and His angels rejoicing over every saved believer, even the most wicked and wretched.

To drive the point home, Jesus tells what has become one of the most iconic parables in scripture. The Prodigal Son. This story of falling and forgiveness, the love of a father for a son thought lost to the world, and the joy at his being restored home is well known even outside of Christian circles. It is an archetype used in secular stories, referred to throughout the culture, and the phrase "prodigal son" part of our lexicon.

The tearful joy of the Father at having his son returned to him, all that he'd done forgiven in an instant, has been a moving inspiration to millions seeking redemption in Christ. The lesson that no matter how far we fall, we are still welcome home by God, Who celebrates our return with joy has helped heal so many similarly lost, and brought them home through Christ.

It has moved me to tears to read it over the years. First as a sinner, come to God saying "Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before you, And am not worthy." But especially as a father of grown children, being able to relate to that kind of heartache and love. The shift in my life's perspective, changing the meaning and adding depth to my appreciation of Jesus' words.

But that's not who the parable is addressed to here. It's not addressed to the repentant sinner. It's not addressed to God the Father, for certain. It's addressed to those Pharisees and scribes, ostensibly righteous men, who are casting judgment on the sinners who're called by faith to Christ.

They are the elder son. The son, who by nature didn't rebel and stayed, doing the work on the farm for the father, who was there while his brother went after whoredoms and drunkenness. Who stayed true. And who, feeling entitled by his works came to anger at his father, resenting his brother and refusing to celebrate his return.

How many saved Christians today are like the elder son? Many who grew up in Christian homes, given the advantage of hearing the Gospel regularly, attending church where the Bible was preached, seeing the testimony of their own family, their parents, friends and congregants living out their Christian walk before them, and who, seeing new converts coming into the church, babes in Christ saved from a life of indulgence and sin, often scarred and broken, traumatized by the damage done in their lives and seeking to be healed, and came to resent them? To be holier than thou? Hypocrites? Fruit inspectors?

It's happened. It was the case of the Pharisees, many of whom were not saved by faith but being so immersed in the culture of the religion believed they were righteous by their own works and in a place to judge others. The beam in their eye blinding them.

Even those long-saved, but grown prideful, forgetting their previous state and losing sight of the mercy God showed them, the grace given to their underserved salvation. Thinking they are better than.

These are often those who seek to add works to the gospel of grace. Who push Lordship and outward signs of turning from sin before things like longsuffering, charity, instruction. Who have the leaven of the Pharisees in their hearts, which is hypocrisy.

teachings.title: Discipleship, not salvation: count the cost
teachings.summary: The hard sayings on discipleship are not about salvation, which is by grace, nor are they automatically true of every believer; forsaking all for Christ is a serious calling every saved person must weigh.
teachings.text:
This passage can be a downer. Jesus gets real, and many people misunderstand what's being said. Many mistakenly think this passage and others like it are about salvation, not discipleship. This error cuts two ways.

Some believe that He is describing a works-based salvation, that the works of discipleship are a way to earn righteousness and sanctification, and by this false belief fail to achieve either.

But even more common mistake, including among saved Christians, is that Jesus is describing the saved, just as they are. That by belief unto redemption that they have picked up that cross. That by nature of their being given eternal life by God's grace they have forsaken the world. That discipleship comes naturally with being born again, and they have nothing left to do but maybe go to church once in awhile and read some scripture-poasts on Telegram here and there. (Or arguing with heretics online). These passages become meaningless self-congratulatory "inspirational quotes." That when they give up some sin or another, they've picked up their cross.

It is deeper than that, and far more serious a matter to be willing to forsake everything for Christ. To be His disciples. And we should count the cost, soberly and with great care.

This isn't an admonition, I am in no position to judge, I am really only coming to count the true cost of this myself, after many many years of being saved. It is a place that some never come to, or try in youthful exuberance only to fail, but later, in maturity successfully achieve. Jesus wasn't trying to discourage us from being His disciples, but dividing the chaff from the wheat, being honest with those of us who remain.

Every born again believer is called to be in service to Christ. It is time to consider the cost.

teachings.title: Penance is an affront to the gospel of grace
teachings.summary: Lenten penance contradicts salvation by grace and the finished work of Christ; fasting is to grow in God's will, not to pay for sins Jesus already paid.
teachings.text:
Another "Lenten" reminder that the concept of penance for sin is in direct contradiction with salvation by grace, and a slap in the face to the finished work of Jesus Christ, who died and suffered Hell for our sins that we may be forgiven.

Fasting is meant to help a saved Christian better understand the will of God that their faith grows, that they may accept it and do that will, to the benefit of others. To feed the spiritual new man by neglecting the old man of the flesh.

It is not to give "penance" for the sins Jesus already paid the price for, in a selfish effort to obtain forgiveness which is given to us freely by the grace of God.

The Bible says telling people to abstain from certain foods as a means of holiness is a doctrine of devils. The idea of penance doesn't exist in scripture. In fact, it is an affront to the Gospel of grace.

Reject these doctrines of devils and rely on the perfect work of Christ alone as the propitiation for your sin.

teachings.title: The people justified God, being baptized
teachings.summary: Those who were baptized justified God, vindicating His word by an outward sign of faith, while the Pharisees showed their unbelief by refusing; baptism itself does not save.
teachings.text:
And when the messengers of John departed, Jesus begins to preach to the crowds about John the Baptist. Praising him, but reminding them that to be saved, in Heaven is an even greater thing than even being the greatest prophet among men that ever lived.

I get the sense that what Jesus is doing is shoring up John's reputation least any think his doubt was an indictment of the Gospel he had preached. And the crowd responds. The Bible says:

*And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.*

Now note the word choice here. Most times when we read "justified" we think of being absolved, the remission of sin and absolution from guilt and punishment by grace through faith in Christ.

But note here Luke says the people who heard Jesus, including the sinners like the publicans (who Luke uses often to contrast with the Pharisees, both men of power, secular and sinful vs who are supposed to be holy and righteous), but he writes these people who heard Jesus preach and His praise of John and his ministry JUSTIFIED GOD, being baptized in the baptism of John.

I think this is a key point we shouldn't miss.

Clearly God is not being absolved of sin here. Justified is also used in a legal sense, meaning vindication. That the evidence is sufficient to prove the argument being made. To show that they believed the report, accepted the witness, agreed with the argument, they were baptized, justifying God.

*But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.*

You see how the act of baptism by believers justifies God, while the rejection of His counsel, not believing Him, not having that faith, is evidenced by their not being baptized.

How faith is made perfect, complete, by an action that is an outward sign to man of the heart of the person, just as the refusal to act shows the abundance of the heart of those who didn't believe.

Baptism itself doesn't save. It is a manifestation of the faith, the substance of things not seen, that can be seen of men. And by not justifying God, the Pharisees show they do not believe.

teachings.title: Mary was saved by faith alone
teachings.summary: Luke records no immaculate conception; Mary was blessed and counted righteous by faith like every saint, so those who worship Mary miss God's grace.
teachings.text:
I would note that the gospel of Luke is the most thorough regarding the nativity of Jesus. It's what Linus quotes from in the Charlie Brown Christmas special. It's often what we think of and read from at Christmas time. And as Luke writes, this is a *declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us.*

And so we should notice what is absent. Those things which are not commonly believed among the first century Christians to whom this gospel is addressed.

There is no mention of the immaculate conception of Mary. There is no indication she was born without sin. While she exclaims in the Spirit that future generations shall call her blessed, it isn't because of a special quality of her's, but by the works of God to whom she's a servant. Mary does the will of God through faith, and in faith is blessed among women to be chosen to bear the incarnation of Christ Jesus. This is the grace that God bestows upon her for her faith. For her willingness to believe.

Just like the Old Testament saints, Mary believed and it was counted upon her for righteousness. She was saved by faith alone and chosen because of that faith.

The Bible says that without faith we cannot please God. Mary could not please God without faith. Zacharias and Elizabeth could not please God without faith. None of them could be righteous absent their belief that God has provided them remission of sins in his mercy. Given the gift of salvation from His grace.

Removing this concept from the gospel, those that worship Mary missed the entire point and so they cannot understand God's mercy and they cannot receive God's grace.

teachings.title: The law of God is perfect: its purpose, grace and judgment
teachings.summary: Argues from a string of passages that God's law is righteous and unchanged, that it shows us our sin as a schoolmaster, and that the old covenant, not the law, was done away in Christ. Closes by asking whether grace is a license to sin (Romans 6) and urging meditation on the law of God.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:*

**Romans 2:11-16**
*For there is no respect of persons with God. For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.*

**Romans 10:4-10**
*For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them. But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

**Ezekiel 36:25-27**
*Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.*

**Psalm 119:165**
*Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.*

**1 John 5:3**
*For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.*

**1 Timothy 1:9**-**12**
*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,* For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with *mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

**John 16:7-11**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;
Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

**Galatians 3:16-25**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.

Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.

Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.*

**Romans 3:10-28**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: Their feet are swift to shed blood: Destruction and misery are in their ways: And the way of peace have they not known: There is no fear of God before their eyes. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.

Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. 

Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.*

**2 Corinthians 3:5-17**
*Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God; Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious? For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth. For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious. Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: And not as Moses, which put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.*

**James 2:9-12**
*But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors. For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all. For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law. So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
*
**Psalm 19:7-8**
*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul;
The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple;
The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart;
The commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes;*

**Romans 7:22**
*For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:*

**Romans 8:7**
*Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.*

**Romans 8:4**
*That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.*
 
**1 John 3:3**
*And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.*

Now this is a lot of scripture, and I struggled to pare down to only this, but it's to buttress the point, the argument I make; regarding the righteous nature of God and His law, grace and judgement, and especially His love towards us. 

Having established without controversy that God is love, that because He is love by necessity, He hates sin and the wicked who live by sin, because He is holy. Righteous in all His ways.
