That He is faithful to His promises and consistent in His judgments. That God is not a respecter of persons. That all who have sinned deserve death and Hell. But He is full of mercy and grace, so that God, because He so loved the world, gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believes on Him shall not perish but instead have everlasting life.

Knowing all this, then what purpose is the law? If all sin (and sin, the Bible says, is transgression of the law), and all have fallen short, deserving death, is God's law just? Is His judgment fair? 

This is an argument many make; "God made us imperfect and without knowing it we sin and damn ourselves. How is that fair? And what about those who never hear about Christ? They don't stand a chance. How is that fair?"

But the Bible tells us that the law of God is written in our hearts. That His wrath is revealed to us by creation itself. That we are without excuse. 

The Bible tells us that whether it was the Hebrews given the perfect law of God inscribed in stone, that they may know His will and the glorious covenant given them that if they kept the whole of the law they would be made righteous; or the heathen that had only the nature of God's law written in their conscience, and the revelation of His judgment by the natural law written upon all creation, all fall short. 

**Hebrews 8:6-7**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.*

But the fault of the old covenant wasn't in the law, which is perfect, but, the next verse says, the fault was with them. Thus the need for a better covenant;

*Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

So we see that the law wasn't done away with, but the old covenant. Not because God's law was unjust but because we are. That in His mercy He provided us a new covenant. A better testament. The Gospel of liberty in Christ.

And so the law serves His purpose to reveal to us the truth of our condition; that we are all sinners and in need of salvation. The law serves as a schoolmaster. 

And in these later days, the Holy Spirit has been sent to convict the world, that all may know they've sinned by His reproof. 

Because the New Testament isn't that the law no longer is in effect, but that those who understand they are deserving death repent towards God and believe on the Son that they may be forgiven. Redeemed by His blood, cleansed from sin and made righteous. That we will be judged not by our own works, but by Christ's and His righteousness imputed on us that we may be partakers of the promises made. We are condemned by the law but at liberty in Christ. 

God in His mercy extends His grace to all. 

And so, the law stands. Glorious and just. Unchanging. Perfect. And those who walk after the Spirit, the inward man quickened, we delight in His law. We love His judgments. 

But those perishing and those who may be saved by faith but living carnally, after the flesh. Feeding the old man; hate His judgments. They don't wish to consider His law. Because it convicts them afresh, daily.
The unsaved pricked in the heart by the Spirit, the saved chastened by the Father, who scourges His children. 

And so they say things like "that's Old Testament law. It doesn't count any more." Cope. Picking and choosing which of the 600 plus commandments given by God in the Old Testament are invalid based on their own rationalisation. Leaning on their own understanding. 

But it's hard to kick against the pricks.

But we know the immutability of God, that He tells us *I am the LORD, I change not.*

The Bible says; *For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.*

**Hebrews 6:17-18**
*Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed  it  by an oath:  That by two immutable things, in which  it was  impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us.*

**James 1:17**
*Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.*

**Hebrews 13:8** 
*Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.* Amen.

The perfection of God's law hasn't changed. The numerous commandments given that no man has fulfilled, other than the man Christ Jesus who in the flesh knew not sin. 

Be it the hundreds given through Moses, or the 10 originally written in stone, hewn by the hand of God Himself. Or the summation of the whole of the law in two commandments, given by Jesus. The judgment of God stands. 

Yes, the carnal ordinances, dietary laws, diverse washings and ceremonial sacrifices that served as a picture of Christ to come are done away with in Him. The sabbath and the holy days, finished in Jesus. But these were not the same as the commandments by which we come to know sin. 

The single law of Eden existed for the same purpose, that Adam and Eve having received paradise would know sin, and by free will choose to fall and lose everything, that they would be made righteous in faith in God's promise, given by God's grace, and thus glorifying God.

So, what then? If we understand the nature of God, the purpose of His law, the fallen state of man because of our inability to keep all of the law, even one command, the gift of salvation in Christ and the good news of our liberty from death and judgment, are we who believe free to sin? 

Is salvation a license to offend the immutable and perfect law of God? The Bible is clear;

**Romans 6**
*What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

2 God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?

3 Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?

4 Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

5 For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:

6 Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.

7 For he that is dead is freed from sin.

8 Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:

9 Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.

10 For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

11 Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

12 Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.

13 Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

14 For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.

15 What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.

16 Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

17 But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.

18 Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

19 I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.

20 For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.

21 What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

22 But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.

23 For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Understanding this; that we are freed from the debt of sin, purchased by the blood of Christ, we become servants of righteousness. We are free from the burden of the law and no longer slaves to sin, if we walk after the new man. To this end we are called to His purpose. 

Our old man will sin. The lusts of the flesh still exist, even as our spiritual new man is at liberty. But we are encouraged to walk in the Spirit that we may better serve our purpose, which He has crafted us for. 

Yes we are at liberty due to the grace and mercy of God. But we must mortify our members, crucifying ourselves daily. Walking in the word. Feeding the new man. Separation. Sanctification. Love. 

And in doing so, glorifying God.

I don't know if I conveyed what I mean very well. The Bible gives us the nature of God, man, the law, salvation and the perfect judgment of God that stems from it all. That's my point. And from this we can draw the conclusion that His law is perfect. It stands today. It serves a purpose in the New Testament, as much as the Old. It existed before Moses. It will be what rules the Millennial Kingdom. It will be the books by which the dead are judged by before the White Throne. 

It is perfectly fair. It is holy. It is righteous. Despise not the law of God, but meditate on it day and night.

teachings.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
teachings.summary: Justified before God by Christ's blood, believers show their faith before men by works, while those who make works their justification damn themselves.
teachings.text:
Now, the expression of faith is found by obeying the will of God. By this a man's faith is justified before men. Just as the OT saints listed in **Hebrews 11** believed and their faith was counted for righteousness, and by faith their works showed to others the power of God's promises.

So too, we are to live our faith. For faith without works is dead, being alone. We may be justified by the blood of Christ before God, but if we hide that faith under a bushel, or we bury that which we've been trusted rather than gain an increase for the Lord, our faith is fruitless. Dead.

The exhortation of James 2 to live out our faith and in doing so, help those in need, sharing that faith that they may come to the same and live, is a beautiful reminder of our calling.

Those that twist it to make works their means of justification before God, damn themselves and put Christ to an open shame, for their dead works are without faith. Disobedient to the Gospel. Perishing.

teachings.title: Too late, reprobate
teachings.summary: Reprobation is real and comes after God has repeatedly led a man to repentance and been rebuffed, so readers must accept the free gift of salvation now because the Spirit will not pursue them forever.
teachings.text:
I sincerely pray that everyone who comes to the channel today takes the time to read the scriptures I posted here, and study them out for themselves. Comparing scripture with scripture. Proving all things.

In two different epistles, one to Gentiles and the other to Israelites, God inspires Paul in the Spirit to lay out His doctrines that we may know and understand Him. It isn't gnostic revelation, but God reasoning with man that we may be able to go on to perfection, throughly furnished unto all good works. Telling us directly that we may know His will. And in both books, after establishment of the primary doctrines of Christ, we are given the explanation of the reprobate doctrine.

It is also one of the primary doctrines taught in Peter's letters, and Jude. It is the subject of many of Christ's sermons, especially Matthew 23. It is talked about in the OT, and shown us in Exodus as Pharoah goes through the process of hardening his heart until God hardens it forever.

Reprobation is real and it happens after God has repeatedly led one to repentance, only to be rebuffed. There is a point where it is too late, even if that point is death.

If you do not know for sure, today, right now, that you are saved. That you have eternal life. That you have been adopted by God into the promise of His kingdom, please consider His word. Don't wait. Now is the time. Accept that free gift. Repent from your dead works and vain traditions and accept the free gift of salvation paid for by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

Because the Spirit will not pursue you forever. It can become too late. And reprobates live a hell on earth of misery and filthy affections, until going finally to the Hell that awaits them, to be burned forever. Too late, reprobate.

Don't let this become you.

teachings.title: Today If Ye Will Hear His Voice
teachings.summary: As unbelief kept Israel out of the promised land, unbelief keeps men from God's rest, which is entered now by faith while the call lasts.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 again builds on the previous; **Hebrews 3**
*For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief*.

*Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.*

Therefore, because, their unbelief in the desert prevented them from entering the promised land, so too fear your unbelief keeping you from entering into the promised land, the rest in Jesus, the better country; the Kingdom of Heaven.

By drawing the comparison to the Hebrews fleeing Egypt with those called coming out of bondage of the law and sin, Paul shows God's grace and His judgment parallels with Exodus spiritually. That it was a picture of Christ that so many Hebrews failed to believe and so died in the wilderness.

For we which have believed do enter into rest. Note the tense. Salvation comes by belief at the moment we call upon His name. At that time we are freed of bondage and given rest, and it is done by the work God finished from the foundation of the world.

**Genesis 2:2**
*And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.*

Paul argues that **if** God says (again quoting **Psalm 95**) *If they shall enter into my rest,* that we can reckon that this is a possible thing, offered by God, **and** those whom it was first preached didn't enter their promised land due to unbelief, **then** we can know we will enter into His rest by faith, and be kept out without it.

And further, as the Spirit moved Paul to write in **Psalm 95**; *Today if ye will hear His voice*, the offer is limited. We have but a short life to believe. A window of His calling, that can pass by death or prolonged neglect to hear His voice. To ignore it. To not retain God in their knowledge. Harden not your hearts when being called.

 *(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

God is reasoning with man, giving us the good news and His terms. Providing examples of what He means, and the if-then logic of it all that none have excuse. Harden not your hearts, hear His voice, NOW is the day of salvation. Believe or be shut out of the promise; never enter into His rest.

teachings.title: Made a Little Lower Than the Angels
teachings.summary: Christ the Creator was made flesh and tasted death for every man, freeing believers from the devil's power of death and the fear of it.
teachings.text:
Having established Jesus as Christ, the redeemer, higher than the angels, Creator and the Son of God, our salvation to whom all the prophets gave witness, Paul builds upon this truth with the implications of our faith.

Since Jesus is, therefore we should give greater heed, pay closer attention to the things spoken of by God, in diverse manners by the prophets to the fathers and by Lord Jesus Himself. That every transgression of the law (for sin is the transgression of the law) shall receive a "just recompense." Death and Hell. Just as the angels who rebelled will be all brought in subjection and cast into that lake of fire promised in Revelation, so too will man be if they neglect the good news of salvation, spoken of by the Lord and confirmed by those who witnessed Jesus ministry, and by signs and wonders of God, and through the gifts of the Holy Ghost given the disciples and Apostles.

He's saying, "Look, we know who Jesus is not only by reputation but by scripture, the prophets, His followers who got it directly from Him, and we know about the fate of those angels who rebelled, Whom Jesus is greater than as He has them under subjection, so we need to listen and believe."

But Jesus was also a man. Citing scripture, Paul notes how God made Jesus a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, that He may taste death for all men. That the Creator became as the created that he may bring us to glory. That He, as the captain of our salvation was made perfect, complete, by the suffering of the cross and death as a sin offering.

For in Christ, we believers are His brethren, His brothers. Sanctified in Jesus we become as one with Him, sons adopted into the promise of His glory by the Father. Who Jesus is not ashamed to call brethren.

Again and again, citing scripture that his audience would know, primarily the Psalms of David which teach so much doctrine, he lays out the case for his argument. By taking heed we are the children of God by the partaking of Jesus flesh and blood through His death. And by His resurrection, steal the power of death from the devil.

Satan was a murderer from the beginning. His goal is to ensure every man faces death and Hell like him. To sin, and in sin, be condemned. This is the power of death the devil possesses.

But Christ's triumph granting salvation to all who believe, and eternal life to never taste death, delivered us. Set free from the bondage of the law, which by fear of death we try and fail to save ourselves. But in Christ, liberated from that fear knowing we won't die for our sins, as they are forgiven in Him.

And so, to provide this salvation Jesus took on the form of man. And in all things He was like us, tempted of the flesh that He may know our struggles and understand our pain, that He may serve as the propitiation for our sin and succour, comfort us, in our temptations and afflictions.

This is so important to understand.

That God so loved us, that He so regarded man, that He allowed the express image of His person, His only begotten Son, through Whom all things were made and under Whom all things will be brought under subjection, to be made lower than the angels, to be made flesh and blood, to be tempted and suffer and made sin for all, that we may have eternal life. Liberated from the fear of death found in transgression of the law by our redemption in His perfect work. Just as the prophets and scriptures promised. Just as those who came before believed on for salvation.

This is the good news. This is the Gospel.

teachings.title: The White Throne Judgment of the Dead
teachings.summary: The great white throne judges the damned blotted out of the book of life, who go to the lake of fire, and only faith in Christ escapes that judgment.
teachings.text:
Here we are given the Millennial Reign in fewer than 15 verses. The binding of Satan in Hell. The saints ruling and reigning the earth in judgment with Christ for that period. Those that sacrificed the most for the cause of Christ given more authority. Until the little season where Satan is given freedom to convince the living humans on earth who resent the rule to rise up against Jesus and the saints. They are destroyed in a moment by fire. Death and then the judgment.

The Great White Throne judgment is of the dead. The damned. Great and small, whose names were blotted out of the Book of Life. Judged by the books of the law, the scriptures of God. His precepts. Written in our hearts, His wrath written in all of creation, that man may have no excuse. And they all have the second death, the lake of fire, the final place of Hell and death, to be tormented for eternity.

Remember, no where in scripture does it say any of one gets written into the Book of Life. It was written before creation, and contains every one that lives. Who are then blotted out if they be reprobate or die without the testimony of Jesus. We can only escape the judgment by faith. Accepting the free gift of salvation given by grace from God.

**Matthew 7**
*21 Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.*

*22 Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?*

*23 And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**John 6:40**
*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**Ephesians 2:8-9**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

**Titus 2**:**12-13**
*For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: The Fall Feasts Picture the Second Coming
teachings.summary: The fall feasts of Leviticus 23 picture Christ's second coming, and their commanded rest from all work pictures salvation by grace without works.
teachings.text:
The Levitical feasts are also important to understand for our study of Revelation going forward. They are a picture of Christ. Last Easter I gave a rundown of the ways Jesus fufifiled the spring feasts, Passover, the feast of unleavened bread and Pentecost. These were a picture of His first coming. Likewise, the fall feasts God commands in **Leviticus 23** represent Christ at His second coming. The timing, the harvest, the gathering. The blowing of trumpets. The dwelling in houses made by God, while singing His praises. All point to end times Bible prophecy. ("Booths" were tabernacles, tents, made from branches and boughs, rough cut and gathered from nature). The timing of things mirrors events in Revelation, as we will see.

One incredibly important point of the feasts, these Sabbaths; NO WORK was to be done by the people. This is the reinforcement by God of His grace in giving us a free gift of salvation in Jesus, who is the Sabbath. Three days of no works, 3 Sabbaths in a row, from His crucifixion to His resurrection, Jesus doing all the work. And like the Spring feasts, the convocations or gathering of the congregation/church, there is no work allowed, for Jesus did it all.

*For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people.*
*And whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people.*

These are those unsaved who are appointed to wrath. Notice it is both the unbelieving, those not afflicted by the atonement made by the sacrifice, and those who do any work who are cast out and destroyed. So too will it be in the second coming.

We should all be familiar with **Matthew 7:21-23**:
*Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**Romans 4:6-8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

**Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.*

teachings.title: The Scarlet Thread
teachings.summary: Traces the scarlet thread from the hand of Zarah in Genesis 38 through Rahab in Joshua 2 and the genealogy of Matthew 1 as a picture of the blood of Christ.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 38:28**
 
*And it came to pass, when she travailed, that the one put out his hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.*



**Joshua 2:18**
 
*Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee.*

"The Bible also mentions scarlet thread or scarlet yarn as part of the tabernacle’s curtains (Exodus 26:1) and the high priest’s ephod (Exodus 28:6), along with threads of gold, blue, and purple. Scripture does not comment on the significance of those colors in the curtains or ephod, but some commentators surmise that the gold, blue, and purple foreshadow Christ’s glory, heavenly origin, and kingly position, while the scarlet thread represents Christ’s atoning work on the cross through the shedding of His blood."

**Matthew 1** genealogy from Abraham to Joseph, husband of Mary shows the scarlet thread running through the Bible from these instances. And* Judas begat **Phares** and Zara of Thamar; and **Phares** begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram..And Salmon begat Booz of **Rachab**; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse.*..on to Jesus.

The Jews today sell the scarlet thread that represents the blood of the lamb, the sprinkling on the doorpost of Passover, the thread of Rehab, on the judgment seat of the temple in sacrifice, pictures of the blood of Jesus and our salvation. They give it to Kabbalist shabbos goys, Gentiles who have fallen under their away. They sell it on the steps of the Roman wall where their temple was destroyed by God in 70AD, to unwitting Christian tourists in exchange for conning them out of shekels. Making what they claim to be a house of God into a place of merchandise. Blasphemy and corruption.

teachings.title: Do ye not hear the law? The bondwoman and the free
teachings.summary: Paul's Hagar-Sarah allegory warns that adding works of the law to faith puts men under bondage, while salvation is God's free gift that cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
And so with this better understanding of the allegory, of recognizing that the entire Old Testament is about Christ Jesus and salvation by faith alone in him, to redeem us, offered by God the father in love and grace, we can understand the righteous anger of Paul writing unto the Galatians.

The Church of the Galatians being swayed by judaizers into accepting another gospel, one of bondage to the law. Whereby they were being told that they must circumcise, keep the days and the months and the dietary laws in the carnal ordinances to be saved. Being dragged back to Hagar, the Bond woman and rejecting Sarah and the son of the promise. Of faith.

And Paul writes, "*O foolish Galatians! who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?"* The Apostle is angry, he says he fears them. He says that he doubts their salvation, which he had labored with them and questions if it was in vain. Paul saying that only an unsaved person who didn't believe the gospel of Faith he presented them would be susceptible to the judaizers dragging them back under the law and away from the liberty of Christ.

*My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.*

 *Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?*

*For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.*

*But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.*
*Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants.*

He says that he's willing to go through this again with them that they may come to Jesus. That they seeking to be brought back under the law, he says don't you even hear the law? And this is what prompts his use of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory. As a teaching moment taken from scripture that they may understand the difference between salvation by faith alone and the bondage of the law.

This is the same message we can give to those claiming Christ who have added works of the law to the salvation given in the simple Gospel of reconciliation and faith.

These judaizers and those bewitched by them will claim that, "Yes it's by faith alone but you have to do the works of the law to be saved. You have to adhere to our vain traditions. To our carnal ordinances. To our dietary restrictions. You don't expect to just be handed salvation? Do you?"

And so they bring people to be the seed after Hagar, not Sarah. And like Ishmael, they do not receive the inheritance which is given by faith in God's promise, not by heirs according to the law.

Just as Sarah was barren from birth, and brought to old age, it took a miracle of God, visited upon her, to bring her the promise. Not by anything she did, for she was not capable, but in God all things are possible.

This is the lesson. *Do you not hear the law?*

If you're trusting in your own works, if you're sewing your own fig leaves, if you're offering the fruit of your garden, instead of the firstling of the flock, if you're committing adultery with Hagar to produce your salvation, repent. Hear the law.

Salvation is given us by God, in His grace, through His Son, Jesus Christ, killed for our sins, a burnt offering, raised from the dead, that we may be redeemed in faith and sealed by the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption. A free gift that once accepted cannot be lost. Eternal life. Heir to the Kingdom. Sons of God.

teachings.title: Paul received no gospel from man
teachings.summary: Paul received his gospel by revelation, not from men's traditions, and anyone preaching another gospel of works is accursed.
teachings.text:
Notice, Paul writing to the Galatians in the Spirit, God inspired scripture, says this TWICE. For emphasis.

And what was it he preached to the Galatians?

*For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ. But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.*

 *For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:*

*And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus. Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.*

*Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not. Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia; And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ: But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed. And they glorified God in me.*

Don't miss this, Paul makes it emphatically clear he didn't learn any secret traditions of man from any Apostles. He wasn't told what to say by anyone else. He, knowing the scriptures and having by the grace of God the opportunity for salvation in Jesus, was given all to preach to the heathen.

He explains how, after 14 years the issue of Judaizers and the circumcision brought him to go to Jerusalem and talk to the local church there, run by James BTW, and they agreed to send letters out denouncing the judaizers adding works to salvation, and affirming the Gospel:

*Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

This is the Gospel. And ANY MAN bringing any other Gospel, especially of works and rites for salvation, IS ACCURSED.

teachings.title: Does everyone sin?
teachings.summary: Answers from Romans 3:23 and 1 John 2:2 that all have sinned and need Christ as the sole propitiation, and that believers have eternal life that cannot be lost because they are sealed by the Holy Spirit. Quotes 1 John 1:9-10 and 2:1.
teachings.text:
"Does everyone sin?" 

The Bible says *for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God,* and so we need to be saved. We need Christ to be the sacrifice, the sole propitiation for our sin. *And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.* Past. Present. Future. We are forgiven in Christ. The Bible says if we believe, *We **have** eternal life. *Everlasting. That can never be lost or taken away, because by the holy Spirit of God we are *sealed unto the day of redemption.* 

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.*

Amen

teachings.title: Faith cometh by hearing, and rightly dividing the word
teachings.summary: Says critics of biblical fundamentalism take symbols literally while denying plain scripture, and explains that God's word is the means by which the Gospel converts souls however it is communicated. Notes that even believers can fall into traps when they fail to rightly divide the word, as over whether one must call on the Lord's name to be saved.
teachings.text:
I often find people like this who call biblical fundamentalism too literal, failed to understand the spiritual aspect of scripture and themselves take what is symbolic or a picture of other things and draw literal interpretations from them while denying clear scripture that means exactly what it says.

Most aren't saved. 

In this case, the Bible says that Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God. The emphasis here is on the scriptures being used as the means of conveying the Gospel to the lost. The Bible has power. God's word is used to convert souls. How God's word is communicated to a person, most commonly audibly, is irrelevant to the fact that it is God's word that brings about faith in a person. Only a fool would take it to mean that the deaf can't get saved. It's just as foolish as saying the mute can't be saved because they can't call upon the name of the Lord. 

Some who are saved fall into similar spiritual traps by not being able to rightly divide the word of God. There's a rift in believers I know over whether you have to actual call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, rather than just believe in your heart. It becomes a semantic and autistic spiral of foolish assertions, and dividing the word of God takes a backseat to silly hypotheticals. 

Anyway, the so-called "doctor of divinity" in this tweet thread is an unsaved vipers teaching that you can save people with your own words, or actions, rather than God's word and Christ's actions. It's wicked and no wonder he makes such a stupid defense of it.

teachings.title: Romans 9:22-24, vessels of wrath and mercy
teachings.summary: Reads Romans 9:22-24 as one question about God's longsuffering with the vessels fitted to wrath so that the riches of His glory are known on the vessels of mercy. Says not all are Israel that are of Israel, and that God always intended to offer salvation to the whole world.
teachings.text:
**Romans 9:22-24 **

*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

All one question. What if the vessels fitted unto wrath, (Gentiles), He endured with longsuffering that He might make known the riches of His glory on the vessels of mercy, even us (Jews)? 

They are not all Israel that are of Israel. 

God in His providence always intended to offer salvation to the whole world.

teachings.title: Chanting Christ is King is not being led to Christ
teachings.summary: Warns that chanting Christ is King while trusting in works to be saved leads to perdition, quoting Matthew 7:21-23 and Titus 1:10-11.
teachings.text:
Chanting "Christ is King" and trusting in their works to save them isn't being led to Christ. It's being led to perdition. 

*Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
...
For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.*

teachings.title: Enoch walked with God
teachings.summary: Enoch, translated by faith and prophet of Christ's coming, is the example of walking separated and pleasing God, and the patriarchs picture the steps of coming to Christ.
teachings.text:
**And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.*

**Hebrews 11:5**
*By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.*

**Jude 1:14-15**
*And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.*

I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation.

Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God.

That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men.

But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord.

We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death.

But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus.

**John 8:51**
 *Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.*

So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death?

In **John 3**, Jesus says "*no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven,*" referring to Himself.

What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly.

Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story.

But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death.

And that's really all that matters.

teachings.title: Coats of skins: the first promise of Christ
teachings.summary: In Genesis 3 God promises the seed who bruises the serpent's head and covers Adam and Eve with skins by shed blood, a picture of Christ's imputed righteousness.
teachings.text:
So having sinned and fallen, God the Father who loves man, offers the first promise of Christ, while laying out the consequences of bringing sin into the world.

To the devil, that old serpent, *Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.*

I plan on expounding on the seed of the woman/seed of the devil, Revelation 12 and how this promise is fulfilled in Jesus in another post.  But note that the seed who bruises Satan's head, and whom Satan bruises the heel, is Christ.

To Eve, *I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

Women know pain and complications of childbirth in ways few creatures in creation can. And their season of fertility, more frequent, and their conceptions, multiplied. And by their nature, they shall desire their husbands will.

This last part deserves its own post as well. Both the meaning and implications of this desire, and how man's failure subverts and damages relationships, twisting this God given inclination in woman. (I would also note modern Bible versions change this verse to have opposite meaning, and how that undermines everything).

And to man, through Adam, we are punished;

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

The consequences of sin is death. We return to the ground whereof we were made, after a lifetime of labor to feed ourselves and survive. With the very things of nature we had dominion over, turned against us. Struggle. Death. The wages of sin.

But here, in **Genesis 3**, at the very beginning of mankind as a fallen creature, loved by God, He covers our sins.

 *Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.*

Shedding of blood for the remission of sin. Covered by the righteousness of the lamb, slain before the foundation of the world. God gives them this gift, freely. Of His own handiwork, not ours.

And so we are now, still naked. Still in sin. Our nature, made manifest in Adam, to choose struggle and death over obedience. Unable to cover our shame by our own works, and needing instead the gift of God, the blood of Christ, covered in the spotless coat of the lamb, slain without blemish. Given the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ as a gift from a loving and merciful God.

This is the Gospel. This is the same faith, as received by Adam, and passed on to his descendents, who call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, and becoming sons of God.

 *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Amen

teachings.title: The trap of works religion and faithless religion
teachings.summary: Works-based religions keep people trapped in sin by trying to justify themselves, while faithless Sadducee-like religion is equally a trap, and Christ calls men to repent of both.
teachings.text:
The hopelessness in hypocrisy of works-based religions, like much of what is considered modern Christianity. Like what is called Judaism. Like what is the religion of the Pharisees. This is such a snare and a trap, as it keeps people mired in their sin, unable to come to forgiveness while they're in their flesh. Because our flesh, our natural man, our old man willfully sins. It's our nature. And as long as people are trapped in a cycle of trying to justify themselves to God by turning from their sin, or engaging in ceremony and sacrament, denying themselves the healing power of Jesus, they become trapped. This stumbling block and snare keeps so many people from even attempting to get right with God.

And the faithless religion of the sadducees, which denies the power of God, the promise of Heaven, the Resurrection in Christ and forgiveness of sins, is equally a trap.

Many who rationalize their way into atheism, reform theology, Calvinism, the catechism of the Roman Catholic church, or the so-called apostolic traditions of the Orthodox, who don't take a literal view of the Bible while adopting the trappings of it, seeking to become righteous in their own wisdom and knowledge, rather than the wisdom and knowledge of the Lord.

These false ways and spiritual traps are what Jesus came to call sinners to repent of that they may be healed. That their sins be forgiven, that they may sin no more.

teachings.title: The ten virgins and the oil of the Spirit
teachings.summary: The oil is the Holy Spirit and the foolish virgins are professing Christians who never received Him, and none can borrow another's oil once the bridegroom comes.
teachings.text:
Matthew 25 continues the Olivette Discourse between Jesus and His disciples, where in the previous chapter He had laid out much of end times prophecy, and His warning and instruction to be watchful and mindful, like a good servant keeping the house while the Lord was away, so as to not be taken unawares at His return. And so, by way of parable, Jesus expounds on this doctrine.

The first, the parable of the 10 virgins, 5 wise, 5 foolish, awaiting the bridegroom, with their lamps. The 5 wise have lamps filled with oil, the 5 fools never bothered, and caught unawares are shut out of the marriage. And in their pleading the Lord says, "Verily I say unto you, I know you not."

The oil is the Holy Spirit, the lamps, our hearts. The foolish virgins, the unsaved who, knowing full well of the bridegroom's pending return were lazy, slumbering.

At His return, the foolish virgins beg the wise for some of their oil, for shared righteousness, but it is not the wise's to give or share. Each must get their own from Christ. And so, the foolish were locked out in the darkness, wailing.

There are many calling themselves Christian who never received the oil, never accepted the Spirit, and tarried and slept while the master is away. Like the virgins, they may well have lived chaste lives, turning from sin, present in the chambers, but never coming to the truth and repentance to be saved.

They believed they could purchase the oil, and return. Be given another chance. But once the wedding feast starts, it's too late.

teachings.title: Godly sorrow and the Corinthians' repentance
teachings.summary: 2 Corinthians 7 shows already-saved believers repenting of sin after Paul's rebuke, and teaches that godly sorrow can lead to repentance unto salvation while worldly sorrow works death.
teachings.text:
Is there a biblical example of repentance from sin? Of turning from, with fresh information changing ones mind, turning towards the correct action in regards to stopping sinful behavior? Yes.

But it's not regarding getting saved (not directly), but of those who had already believed getting right.

In 1 Corinthians, Paul wrote to the saints in Corinth regarding the open fornication among them, and their taking one another to court for petty disputes, among other things. He ripped into them, that they ought to know better and to repent of it, to think better of it. To come to the realization that it is wrong and hurt their ability to do God's will in sharing the gospel, while they had such sin among them.

And in 2 Corinthians, written a year or so later, Paul tells us by way of praising them, that they had repented of it.

**2 Corinthians 7**

*4 Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.*

*5 For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.*

*6 Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;*

*7 And not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.*

*8 For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.*

*9 Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.*

*10 For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.*

*11 For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.*

*12 Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.*

*13 Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.*

Note in verse 10, Paul is giving us a general rule, that godly sorrow, that is sincerely being sorry at a wrong you've done, leads many to the repentance of belief that is salvation, while the sorrow of this world to death.

In other words, being sorry you were caught, sorry you're in trouble, sorry you're paying a price for it, sorry that God has chastised you, this is worldly sorrow, and in it is death, because it isn't genuine, it's selfish.

Paul says, godly sorrow, truly understanding the harm done to others or to God by our transgressions, can lead to repentance towards salvation, a change of mind that cannot be repented of. Faith in Christ, that cannot be lost once gained. Once saved, always saved.

But to the Corinthians, who had already tasted the good word of God, tasted the heavenly gift, and the powers of the world to come, partakers of the Holy Ghost, as they'd already come to repentance unto salvation. The Bible says, *it is impossible...to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

So Paul isn't telling the Corinthians that their turning from the sin he pointed out among them is how they were saved, for they were already, but makes this comment as a part of a larger point, regarding their acceptance of his rebuke.

teachings.title: Trent's anathema on faith alone
teachings.summary: The Council of Trent's curse on justification by faith alone puts the Catholic Church against the Bible, which teaches salvation by grace through faith without works.
teachings.text:
The Council of Trent, on salvation by faith alone:

CANON IX.-If any one saith, that by faith alone the impious is justified; in such wise as to mean, that nothing else is required to co-operate in order to the obtaining the grace of Justification, and that it is not in any way necessary, that he be prepared and disposed by the movement of his own will; let him be anathema

CANON XII.-If any one saith, that justifying faith is nothing else but confidence in the divine mercy which remits sins for Christ’s sake; or, that this confidence alone is that whereby we are justified; let him be anathema.

The Bible is anathema to the Catholic Church. Jesus Christ Himself, and Paul, Peter, James, all heretics and anathema to them.

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**Romans 11:6**
*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

**Romans 3:20**
*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
 *For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.*

**John 3:16**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

teachings.title: Hail Mary and what grace really is
teachings.summary: Explains that grace is the unearned gift of God, so the idea that Mary was sinless would make her blessings a wage rather than a gift. Says misunderstanding grace leads to the false doctrines of the immaculate conception and perpetual virginity.
teachings.text:
Hail Mary, full of grace. Blessed are thou. 

Grace is the unearned gift, the blessing of God to those who do not deserve it. The idea that Mary was sinless would mean she was as holy as God, and not in need of His grace, as she'd be like unto Him. His blessings would instead be wage, rather than gift. 

The lack of understanding what grace is, being unsaved and perishing, not believing the gospel of reconciliation and grace and so not having been so blessed, being ignorant to His mercies, leaves those who speak blasphemies about Mary wide open to thinking grace is a quality of her's, rather than given of God. And thus the false doctrines of her being conceived immaculate, sinless, a perpetual virgin, who's flesh was not left to perish, etc ..

teachings.title: Do you believe the record?
teachings.summary: Quotes 1 John 5:10-14 and asks whether the reader believes God's record that eternal life is a gift in His Son alone. Says that to think it can be lost or earned is to call God a liar.
teachings.text:
**1 John 5**

*10 He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.
*
11 *And this is the record, that* **God** **hath** **given** **to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son**.

*12 He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

13 These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.

14 And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:*

Do you believe that record? That salvation is a gift, given by God or eternal life, everlasting, never to die or see Hell, in Jesus, alone. Can't be lost. Can't be earned by other means. Paid for by Christ. 

If you think it can be lost, or must be achieved or maintained by your own works, or that it's not knowable, that you can't have confidence in this gift, then you're calling God a liar.

teachings.title: Work out your own salvation is not doubt
teachings.summary: Work out your own salvation does not deny assurance, since Paul in the same epistle is confident God will perform the work He began in them by the gospel.
teachings.text:
Philippians is one of my favorite epistles, for it's clear meaning and beautiful prose. It is easily understood and straightforward doctrine on sanctification and doing works of the Lord.

However many works-based false teachers use the "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" line to teach that you cannot be assured salvation, and that we must do works to be saved. This out of context understanding is contrary to scripture, even scripture within the same epistle. In chapter 1 Paul says:

*For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now;*
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.*

He has confidence in them, that they partake in the same grace that saved him. This is only conditioned on their having fellowship in the same Gospel he preached to them, not on their works, and with not doubt that God works in them.

It is another case of reading the whole of scripture and comparing it with itself, saving us from bad doctrine.

teachings.title: What scripture says about Mary
teachings.summary: States that Mary died a natural death and entered Heaven by faith through grace, the same way as all saved believers. Says every other teaching about Mary is extra-biblical and that a church celebrating it is apostate.
teachings.text:
Mary's body died a natural death and was buried. Her spirit, quickened by being born again in faith through grace allowed her, a sinner, to enter into Heaven the same exact way all saved believers do. 

Every other extra-biblcal heresy regarding Mary is based on grifters and conmen, centuries after her death making up tales. 

Any church that celebrates this heresy is apostate.

teachings.title: One gospel preached by Paul and the apostles
teachings.summary: Galatians and Acts 15 show Paul preached the same faith-alone gospel the apostles agreed on, against the Judaizers then and Hebrew roots and works teachers now.
teachings.text:
The letter to the Galatians regarding the false gospel of works brought to them by judaizers, specifically that they must keep circumcision to be saved, contrary to the gospel of grace Paul had won them with.

Paul in chapter 1 and 2 establishes his bona fides in this, that he preaches the same Gospel the Apostles have, not having learned it from them but the Spirit, and confirming it much later, following the meeting with the elders and the council in Jerusalem, written about in **Acts 15**, which followed a similar incident of judaizers preaching circumcision in Antioch.

If you recall, James, the half brother of Jesus Christ and Peter agreed with Paul that this burden of the carnal ordinances of the law must not be required of the Gentiles, least they frustrate the faith alone Gospel they stand by, that saved them.

*Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.*
*And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.*

*Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.*

This, in one accord, James agreed; *James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me:*

*Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things. Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.*
*Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God: But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.*

There was an idea that Paul changed the nature of the Gospel, removing works from it, and this is something that persists to this day, especially with very online pseudo-Christians, who are taken in by those adding works to salvation, or worse, Hebrew roots heresy, adding the specific ordinance of circumcision and other physical requirements to the faith. But in Acts, and here in Galatians, for example, we see that there has been one faith preached, consistently and that Paul was approved of by the 'pillars' of the early church, even to the shame of Peter, having been being a respecter of persons regarding the Jews in Antioch, and his repentance before Paul, James and the others in Jerusalem.

teachings.title: Why Paul circumcised Timothy
teachings.summary: Paul refused circumcision for Titus because it was pressed as a condition of salvation, yet circumcised Timothy for access to the Jews, since circumcision is nothing when not made a means of justification.
teachings.text:
There is a lot going on here, in this chapter. Especially on the heels of 15, where we see the pillars of the church in Jerusalem issuing their judgment that Paul go to the Gentiles and their denouncing the adding of works to the faith that saved them. They agree at Paul's behest to write and visit the various churches, warning them against taking on the yoke of bondage to the carnal ordinances of the law, primarily circumcision. This crisis comes about by new Christians, confused in the faith by certain men crept in unawares, seeking to force Gentile Titus to be circumcised as part of salvation. Paul steadfastly refuses understanding the what they were attempting to do would subvert the Gospel, and James and the other apostles agree.

Yet here we see Paul circumcised Timothy, who being half-Gentile, but raised Jewish by his mother, would be hindered by the Jews in the region when giving the Gospel. And as Paul says in 1 Corinthians, in this case *Circumcision is nothing,* because it's not being put forth as a condition of justification before God.

We must look at the epistles to Corinth and especially the Galatians for more understanding, and so I think I will devote time to them today and tomorrow.

teachings.title: If thou believest with all thine heart
teachings.summary: Acts 8:37 gives the order of salvation, believing that Jesus is the Son of God and then baptism, which is why modern versions remove or doubt it.
teachings.text:
Now, after Philip has given him the gospel and shown him, out of the Bible the truth of Jesus Christ, the eunuch asks what hinders him from being baptized in the water the caravan had come to, and Philip answers with pure doctrine;

*If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest.*

*And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.*

This is the Gospel. This is how salvation works. This is the order of things, and baptism is but a public expression of the salvation that came from belief.

And so Acts 8:37 is either removed or footnoted into doubt by all modern perversions of the Bible. The simplicity of the Gospel, that we are saved by our belief in this truth that Jesus is the Son of God, the Christ who saves us by His perfect work, as God promised from the foundation of the world.

The removal or doubt-casting on this verse, the clearest and most explicit example of 1-on-1 soul winning thus far in the New Testament, can only be done for one reason, and to serve one agenda; Satan's.

We see the eunuch saved, baptized and Philip carried away by the Holy Spirit, leaving one of the most powerful men in Ethiopia joyfully proclaiming Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Repent in the KJV and the modern versions
teachings.summary: Notes that of 105 uses of repent or repentance in the KJV, the modern versions remove it in 46 verses, including the 35 times God repents. Argues this protects the claim that repent means turn from sin.
teachings.text:
**Fun fact**: Of 105 instances of the term "repent" or "repentance," contained in the authorized translation, the KJV, the modern versions eliminate its use in 46 verses.

Curiously, it is fairly consistent when they choose to change scripture. The NIV and other other corrupt Bible transitions eliminate the 35 different times God is said to "repent" in scripture. Essentially removing from scripture the idea that God can repent. The only rationale one can draw from that is they know the idea of a sinless God repenting undermines their subversive, heretical claim that "repent" automatically means "turn from sin." They also remove other instances such as Exodus 13:17 and Matthew 27:3, which complicate the false works-based doctrine that they are trying to teach. 

It is impossible to come to any other conclusion than that is the agenda behind their selective censorship of the term from any instance that undermines their wicked doctrine.

teachings.title: Answering the works-salvation reading of Matthew 7 and the rich young man
teachings.summary: Answers a Greek Orthodox argument that those who listed their works in Christ's name were relying on faith alone. Points out the text condemns the very doctrine of works for salvation.
teachings.text:
This is from Greek Orthodox Church of America. They legitimately are arguing that the people in Jesus teaching, telling Him all the works they did in His name, were relying on faith alone to save them. The exact opposite of what's being taught by Christ. 

They cannot see the discrepancy. They do not have the ability to. 

Note that this is not Cherry picked out of context, but condemns precisely the doctrine they are defending, works for salvation.

Here again, shortly after conceding that scripture says by the deeds of the law are no men saved, they cite this story of Christ testing a rich young man who lied and claimed was sinless, and was exposed when he refused to give up his wealth to follow Christ. 

As the Bible says, *As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.*

teachings.title: Born of water is the first birth
teachings.summary: In John 3:5 being born of water means natural birth, as verse 6 explains, not baptism, so baptism is no part of being born again.
teachings.text:
Oh one more point of Doctrine from John 3, there are some who like nicodemus, can't understand scripture and so isolate verse 5, out of context, and claim that baptism is part of being born again. That Jesus is saying we must be born both of water, meaning baptism, as well as the Spirit. As we can tell by looking at the entire chapter in context, that's not what's being said at all. Verse 6 explains verse 5, Jesus is saying that we're being born again, because we've already been born once in the flesh, in the water of our birth. So being born in the spirit is our second birth.

Like all bad doctrine, it requires someone to take an autistically literal interpretation of isolated verses, and are as foolish as Nicodemus saying we'd have to crawl back inside our mother to be born again.

teachings.title: Once saved always saved: proof texts
teachings.summary: A run of passages for the security of the believer: kept by the power of God in 1 Peter 1, Galatians 5 against adding a work, Hebrews 13:5 and Deuteronomy 31:6 on never being forsaken, and 1 John 5 on eternal life given in the Son.
teachings.text:
**1 Peter 1:4-9**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath **begotten us again** **unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,** **To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,
Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.** Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:
That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:
Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:
Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.*

Anyone who says we are not saved unto everlasting life, with eternal security, is a liar and is damned. If you're caught up in this false teaching, repent and believe the word of God.

**Galatians 5**
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.

2 Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.

3 For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

4 Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.

5 For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith.

6 For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.*

If you are counting on your own ability not to sin, you are a debtor to the whole of the law and Christ is of no effect. You are fallen from grace. Not in the sense that you've lost your salvation, but that you've never had it. 

You can substitute anything in the place of circumcision in this chapter. Baptism, repenting of sin, going to church... anything, and once you add any condition to the grace and faith in Christ to your belief for salvation (or maintaining salvation) you now are a debtor to the WHOLE of the Law. "*If you offend in one point," *in commission or omission, you are damned. *Christ is become of no effect unto you.*

"Repent of sins" or "you can lose your salvation" are damnable heresy because no one can repent of all sin, and no one saved by faith alone can lose it. Anyone giving these as part of their "gospel" is a false teacher who isn't giving people a "lively hope," but an impossible task.

Literally there were people at the church of Galatia convinced that they needed to do *something *in order to be saved. They added a work to the Gospel, and Paul head to write to tell them that in doing so they made the Gospel of no effect. The same impulse rules men today that make them unable to believe that God would give them eternal life with no strings attached, and the delusion they place themselves under to maintain that false belief keeps them fallen from grace.

Ok, one more swing at this dead horse:

**Hebrews 13:5** 
*Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.*

**Deuteronomy 31:6**
*Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.*

How can you be content with what you have, be strong and without fear, if you believe God the Father will abandon you? How can you call Him a liar when He says He will never leave or forsake His children?

I think one of the most toxic things about the current culture of illegitimacy and divorce we are mired in, that all of us have experienced either directly, as children or in our families, makes people suspicious of unconditional love, and unable to grasp a heavenly Father who won't abandon His sons

Ok, one more proof text for OSAS. Don't miss it, or you might be calling God who cannot lie a liar:


**1 John 5**
*7 For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.

8 And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one.

9 If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.

10 He that believeth on the Son of God **hath the witness in himself**: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.

11 And this is the record, that God hath given to us **eternal** life, and this life is in his Son*

teachings.title: John 1: as many as received him
teachings.summary: John 1 shows Christ lights every man, that the world did not know Him, and that whoever receives Him by believing becomes a son of God, refuting limited atonement and irresistible grace.
teachings.text:
Next, the apostle John introduces us to John the Baptist, the voice crying out in the wilderness bearing witness to Christ.

John the apostle again turns to explain Jesus is the true light which "lighteth *every* man." (RIP limited atonement).

V10 states the matter plainly, the creator has come into the creation and the creation didn't even recognize Him, fallen as we are. Man doesn't recognize Christ (rip irresistible grace)

V11 lays the groundwork for replacement theology. The "chosen people" the Jews don't recognize Christ

V11 is the Gospel itself; the good news. "As many received him..." (that's an indeterminate number, meaning 'all who' (limited atonement BTFO, again), "...to them gave he power to become the sons of God" (the promise made by God), "even to them that believe on his name" (the means of obtaining the aforementioned power to be sons of God; BELIEVING, not works or any other means).

V13 Sons born (you have to be born again to be a son or daughter of God). Not by blood (dispensationalism, ded), not by our fleshly desire (none righteous), not by our works (the will of man) but of God.

V14 is the mystery of Christ made flesh revealed.
V15-17 John the BAPTIST (hint) tells us his ministry has been preaching the coming Christ and salvation by grace, not the law.

When JtB is questioned by the Pharisees he testifies that Jesus is the Christ come in answer to what was taught by all the prophets, the faith that saved OT saints was manifest.

About halfway through one chapter and the doctrines are just boom, boom, boom...

teachings.title: Romans 13: Paul obeyed authority in faith
teachings.summary: Notes that Paul wrote Romans 13 under Roman rule and obeyed authority unless it conflicted with God. Points to Paul staying in the Philippian jail to win the jailer, who is told only to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ.
teachings.text:
And Romans 13 is written 250yrs before that satanic, judaized death cult was founded by Satan, and Paul in the spirit says ALL authority, whomever it is under - state, family, community, employment, all, is to be obeyed unless it conflicts with a higher authority, God being ultimate. 

Catholics not create false doctrine challenge, impossible

FFS the Romans were in charge and persecuting Christians when he wrote that. They had Paul under house arrest, chained to a guard. 

Paul trusted God and obeyed authority, in faith.

Paul could have escaped the Philippian jail after the divine earthquake, but he stayed to get the jailer saved in Acts 16:25-31

*25 And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

26 And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.

27 And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.

28 But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

29 Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,

30 And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

31 And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.*

Paul obeyed authority to the glory of God. 

Note he doesn't say "repent of your sins and be saved" or "get baptized" or "go to church" or "do sacraments" or any other work. Just believe. Call on the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: Romans 8: adopted after first believing
teachings.summary: Paul builds the case for conditional election: we are adopted as sons and joint heirs only after believing, and foreknowledge comes before predestination, which Calvinists reverse.
teachings.text:
Paul has for the past 7 chapters laid out the factual, Biblical case for *conditional election,* that **we must believe to be saved,** starting with the testimonial of God in creation, the lack of excuse by the unbelieving, the refusal to accept the knowledge of God of the reprobate, and the surety of our salvation of placing our faith in God's promise.

Here, tying together these themes, he speaks of the carnal mind that the saved still have, exhorting the saved by faith to live in the spirit, not the flesh, because in that righteousness given us is adoption into the promise; we become heirs of Christ, we call out to our Father. In verse 9, he makes it clear that this is a **conditional** state of being. You aren't adopted without first believing.

Then, Paul begins building onto this foundational theme of being adopted as sons in the spirit by explaining how God's foreknowledge that we (the saved) then be used to His purpose. (Note the order of operations in verse 29, calvanists reverse it, and thus get none of it).

The glory of being joint heirs with Christ, in Christ. The hope, which is an earnest expectation for the thing we believe to come (not a long-shot wish as some use the term) being shared with all of creation, waiting for that kingdom to come. That we are blameless to charge by any because we are justified in our faith in Christ. That, in faith, none can stand before us as God gives us all things, according to His will.

Having laid out the first faith and its terms and rewards, Paul is making the case to the saved to understand what their faith has opened them up to, what God's gifts mean to us if we now walk in the spirit, quickened by the Holy Ghost, that all things are for good to us for loving God, if we simply trust further in the word of God, building faith upon faith.

teachings.title: Jesus the author and finisher of our faith
teachings.summary: Reads Hebrews 12:2 to show that Jesus is the Word of God, the author of what we believe and its finisher. Warns against reading the verse as Christ giving the ability to believe rather than the Gospel we have faith in.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 12**
*2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.*

Jesus is the Word of God. He is the author of what we believe on, and its finisher, having come as promised to do God's will.

Some, misguided by heretics see this verse as Christ literally giving faith, the ability to believe, rather than giving us the Gospel we have faith in. It's foolishness.

teachings.title: The Antichrist deceives the lost, not the saved
teachings.summary: Corrects the idea that saved Christians will be deceived by the Antichrist, from 2 Thessalonians 2: those deceived are those who received not the love of the truth. Adds that name-only Christians are likely to be his biggest supporters.
teachings.text:
This is a category error. Those being deceived aren't saved Christians. The Antichrist does not deceive believers, but those who dwell in inequity. 

**2 Thessalonians 2**
*7 For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.

8 And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:

9 Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,

10 And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.

11 And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:
